# Prose fragments for the lifecycle section (LaTeX).  Assembled by build.py.

INTRO = r"""
% ===================================================================
\section{Session Lifecycle and \texttt{claim-forked}}
\label{sec:lifecycle}
% ===================================================================
%%LIFECYCLE-BEGIN

The sections above model how a session is \emph{correlated} with a
delegation. They say nothing about how a session roster comes to exist,
how it persists or is reclaimed, or how a forked child acquires a
delegation by a sequence of file writes that a process may abandon at
any point. Those are the subject of \fpath{docs/design-opencode-plugin.md}
(DES-078): \S2.1.1 (\field{ensure}, the two sidecars, \field{isStale}),
\S2.3 and \S2.3.1 (the ancestor walk), \S2.6 (\field{session delete}), and
\S5 points~1 and~2 (\field{Store.Ensure} and \field{claim-forked}). That prose
has been through three rounds of review (rounds 5, 6 and 7 of PR \#536),
and each round found a counterexample the previous one had not. The
organisation's rule for a defect class that survives two rounds is to stop
reviewing and model it; this section is that model.

The model is a state machine over the operations \emph{as the design
document currently states them}. It was written first with every
amendment switched off, so that ProB could be asked whether the four
invariants of \S\ref{sec:lc-invariants} hold of the prose as it stood.
They did not. \S\ref{sec:lc-ledger} records each counterexample, the
amendment that removes it, and the switch that turns that amendment on.
The operations below, with every switch on, are the authority the design
document is to be brought into line with; with a switch off, the
corresponding operation is the prose of rounds 6 and 7.

\subsection{Method, and two facts about the toolchain}
\label{sec:lc-method}

\textbf{One machine per file.} \texttt{probcli} reads a \fuzz{} document
as a single B machine: the state is the schema that \field{Init} primes,
and every other schema is promoted to an operation. This file already
contains one machine (\field{Registry}, \S\ref{sec:state}). The machine of
this section is a second, independent one, so it cannot be explored in
place; it is extracted by the commands of \S\ref{sec:lc-verification}
(everything between the two \texttt{LIFECYCLE} markers, together with the
preamble and the given sets), and the schemas \field{LcInit},
\field{LcInitPair} and \field{LcInitChain} stand for the \field{Init} of the
extracted file. Nothing in this section reads or writes a \field{Registry}
component.

\textbf{State predicates are guards.} \texttt{probcli}'s Z-to-B
translation puts only the typing of the state schema into the B
\texttt{INVARIANT}; every predicate in the state schema is conjoined to
the post-state of each operation, as a guard. An operation that would
violate such a predicate is not reported as violating it: it is
silently disabled, and the state is simply not reached. A ``zero
invariant violations'' report from \texttt{/z-spec:test} therefore says
nothing about the predicate part of a state schema (the earlier
\S\ref{sec:validation} figures are of this kind; see
\S\ref{sec:lc-findings}). The state schema of this section accordingly has
\emph{no predicate}. Each invariant is stated as its own schema
(\field{LcInv}\ldots), which \texttt{probcli} never sees, and is checked by
giving ProB its negation as a \texttt{-goal}: a counterexample is then a
reachable state satisfying the goal, and ``no counterexample, all states
visited'' is exhaustive for the instance.

\textbf{Slicing.} The full machine has about thirty operations over
twenty-six variables; ProB explores about two hundred states a second.
Each invariant is therefore checked on a \emph{slice}: the same schemas
with the operations that cannot affect that invariant removed, and a
scenario \field{Init} where a particular lineage is needed. A removed
operation leaves its variables at their initial values. The slices are
named in \S\ref{sec:lc-verification}.

\subsection{Types and constants}

Sessions, missions and delegations are the given sets of
\S\ref{sec:basic}. The liveness of a roster's numeric participant is
abstracted to three kinds, because \field{isStale} distinguishes no more:
a solo or persona-named roster ages out by its \field{Started} time
(\field{rkAged}); a roster whose primary participant is a numeric id is
stale exactly when that process is dead (\field{rkNumLive},
\field{rkNumDead}). A binding's origin is as in \fpath{active.go}:101--119.
Time is $0 \upto \field{lcMaxTime}$ with a stale-after threshold
\field{lcTtl}; a last-seen \emph{later} than \field{now} models a clock that
has stepped backwards, which is the future-dated case.

\begin{zed}
RKIND ::= rkAged | rkNumLive | rkNumDead
\end{zed}

\begin{zed}
BORIGIN ::= boClaim | boDispatch
\end{zed}

\begin{axdef}
lcMaxTime : \nat \\
lcTtl : \nat
\where
lcMaxTime = 2 \\
lcTtl = 1
\end{axdef}

The eight constants below are the amendments of \S\ref{sec:lc-ledger}.
Setting a constant to \field{zfalse} yields the operation as written in
DES-078 rounds 6 and 7; to \field{ztrue}, the amended operation. Each
amended operation is a conjunct guarded by its constant, so the two
versions differ in nothing else.

\begin{axdef}
fixDeleteOrder, fixDeleteCloses, fixCycleCheck, fixRefuseReconciles, \\
fixInertBinding, fixStaleLive, fixCorruptPurge, fixPostCheck : ZBOOL
\where
%%SWITCHES%%
\end{axdef}

\subsection{State}
\label{sec:lc-state}

The state is the conjunction of seventeen small schemas, so that an
operation can name the components it leaves alone with $\Xi$ rather than
by equations. Session level: \field{roster} is the set of existing roster
files, with \field{rkind}, \field{started} and \field{corrupt} (a roster
whose file no longer parses). \field{parentSide} is the
\fpath{parent-session} sidecar; it is a function from a session to its
recorded parent, and may have an entry for a session with no roster.
\field{seen} is the \fpath{last-seen} sidecar and \field{seenBad} the
sessions whose sidecar does not parse. Claim level: \field{claimed} and
\field{corigin} are the active-mission sidecar, \field{binding} the
delegation-binding sidecar, \field{pend} and \field{pendWit} the
\fpath{claim-forked-pending} record (delegation and witness), and
\field{stage} and its companions are a \field{claim-forked} write phase that
is \emph{in flight}, holding the child's dispatch-pending lock (stage $k$
is the next write to perform; \S\ref{sec:lc-ops}). Delegation level:
\field{used} are the ids ever allocated by \field{NewID}, \field{skel} the
skeletons on disk, \field{dOpen} those whose verdict is still open,
\field{dMis} and \field{dOwn} a skeleton's mission and child, and
\field{missOpen} the missions that are open. The last three schemas are
ghosts: they record history so that an invariant over a transition can be
checked as an invariant over a state.
"""

GHOSTS = r"""
\field{sealed} records, when a roster is written, the parent that was then
recorded for it; \field{LineageStable} says the sidecar never departs from
it while the roster exists. \field{purgedLive} collects every session whose
roster a purge removed while it was demonstrably live. \field{leaked}
collects every child for which a \field{claim-forked} call ended with an
interrupted attempt's skeleton still open and no longer resumable.
"""

INV = r"""
\subsection{The invariants}
\label{sec:lc-invariants}

The four invariants of the mission contract, each as a schema over
\field{Lifecycle}, followed by the two checks needed to state the first
precisely and the well-formedness conditions that validate the model
itself. A schema here is a statement, not a guard (\S\ref{sec:lc-method}).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \field{LineageStable}: while a roster exists, the parent that
    \field{Store.ParentOf} reports is the one that was recorded when the
    roster was written.
  \item \field{Acyclic}: the recorded-parent relation has no cycle. This is
    the strong form. It is stated of every sidecar, not only of those
    reachable from some roster, and it makes the visited set of the
    ancestor walk (\S2.3.1) a defence against a corrupt file rather than a
    necessity; the walk keeps its visited set and refuses on a repeat.
  \item \field{NoLiveSessionPurged}: no purge removes a roster whose
    last-seen is within the TTL, or whose numeric participant is live.
    ``Live'' is judged from what ethos can read: the participant kind of an
    unreadable roster is not evidence.
  \item \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}: every open fork-propagated skeleton is
    named by a pending record or by the binding of an existing child. This
    literal form is the first conjunct of the stronger property below.
  \item \field{ReconcileOnExit} (second conjunct of the stronger
    \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}): no \field{claim-forked} call ends, other
    than by ``write failed'', leaving an interrupted attempt's skeleton open
    when it has not adopted it and its binding is not live. The literal form
    holds of a crashed attempt for ever, because the record names the
    skeleton; the harm of an unreconciled attempt is that nothing may ever
    reconcile it (the child may be refused for good), so the postcondition
    is on the exit of the call.
  \item \field{SweepComplete}: an open skeleton whose mission is closed is
    named by a pending record. This is what \field{Store.Close}'s sweep is
    for.
\end{itemize}
"""

OPS_HEAD = r"""
\subsection{Initialisation}

\field{LcInit} is the empty system. \field{LcInitPair} is a child with a
parent that holds an operator claim; \field{LcInitChain} adds a grandparent.
Both are scenario initialisations for the slices that need a lineage.
"""

OPS_SESSION = r"""
\subsection{Operations}
\label{sec:lc-ops}

\paragraph{Environment.} The clock may be set to any time, so it may step
backwards; a numeric participant dies; a roster or a last-seen file
becomes unparseable.
"""

OPS_ENSURE = r"""
\paragraph{\field{ensure}} (\S2.1.1, \S5 point~1). \field{LcEnsureCreate} is a
first registration or a registration over a leftover sidecar: the
lineage sidecar is written first, then the roster, then, if \field{--touch},
the last-seen. The three rules of the design appear as guards in order:
a non-empty parent must have a roster unless \field{--parent-gone}; a
recorded parent must equal the supplied one; and the supplied parent, with
\field{par?} empty or a singleton, is then recorded. With
\field{fixCycleCheck} the new edge is refused if the session is already an
ancestor of the supplied parent. \field{LcEnsureLineageOnly} is the crash
between the sidecar and the roster. \field{LcEnsureRefresh} is the existing
roster with \field{--touch}. \field{LcCreateCli} is \field{session create},
which refuses an id whose sidecar records a parent.
"""

OPS_DELETE = r"""
\paragraph{\field{deleteFiles}} (\S2.6; \fpath{store.go}:278--301). The call
stops at the first failure, so a failed call has performed a prefix of its
steps; \field{done?} is the length of that prefix. The steps are numbered
in the order the code performs them. As written, the last-seen and
parent-session sidecars precede the roster file, so step~7 is the roster
removal and a failure there leaves a roster whose lineage sidecar has gone.
With \field{fixDeleteOrder} the roster is removed at step~6 and the
lineage sidecar last, so the sidecar can outlive the roster (which the
design already treats as authoritative) but never the reverse. With
\field{fixDeleteCloses} step~1 closes, with verdict \field{aborted}, every
open skeleton named by the session's pending record or binding, before
either is cleared.

\paragraph{Purge} (\fpath{store.go}:385--404). A purge deletes a roster that
does not parse, or whose \field{isStale} holds, through the same
\field{deleteFiles}. When a valid last-seen is present, staleness is decided
by the later of \field{Started} and last-seen alone (round 6). With
\field{fixStaleLive} a live numeric participant also protects the roster;
with \field{fixCorruptPurge} an unreadable roster with a fresh last-seen is
left alone.
"""

OPS_CF = r"""
\paragraph{\field{claim-forked}} (\S5 point~2). The read phase takes no lock
and writes nothing; \field{LcCfBegin} is a read phase that passes (the
child's roster loads, the witness holds a claim-origin binding, and the
witness is reached by the walk of \S2.3.1: each hop is read from
\field{parentSide} and the session reached must have a readable roster) and
that goes on to take the child's dispatch-pending lock. \field{LcCfRefuse}
is a read-phase refusal. The write phase reconciles the pending record
first (stage~0), in one of three ways: the child already holds a claim
(\field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}), the record is resumable
(\field{LcCfReconcileReuse}), or it is closed and removed
(\field{LcCfReconcileFresh}). It then allocates an id and re-checks that
the mission is open (stage~2), and writes the record, the skeleton, the
binding and the claim, one stage each (3 to 6), before removing the
record. A process may \field{LcCfCrash} at any stage, leaving the files
written so far; or, if it survives a failed write, \field{LcCfAbort}.

With \field{fixRefuseReconciles} a refusal also reconciles. With
\field{fixInertBinding} the claimed case closes the skeleton unless the
binding is live, that is, unless the child's claim is for the skeleton's
mission. With \field{fixPostCheck} the binding is not written unless the
mission is still open: the check that follows the skeleton write, which
closes the window the unlocked sweep leaves.
"""

OPS_MISSION = r"""
\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked} is \field{Store.Close} with the
exclusive mission lock: it cannot run while a write phase holds the shared
lock (stage $\geq 2$ for that mission). \field{LcCloseUnlocked} is the
fallback of \fpath{store.go}:1107--1114, taken when the lock cannot be
acquired: the sweep runs with no exclusion. \field{LcAbandonMission}
refuses while any skeleton of the mission is open; that guard is
\field{countBlockingDelegations}
(\fpath{store.go}:2004--2010) as an observer, and it is why an unaccounted
open skeleton is a defect and not a curiosity.
"""

tool_input.content:
\subsection{Counterexamples and amendments}
\label{sec:lc-ledger}

Every counterexample below was found by ProB against the committed
revision of this section in which all eight switches were \field{zfalse},
that is, against the operations as DES-078 rounds 6 and 7 state them. Each
trace is the shortest breadth-first path to a state satisfying the negated
invariant, in the notation of the operations; ``$a$, $b$'' are sessions,
$m_1$, $m_2$ missions and $d$ a delegation. The first four are the
counterexamples of the three review rounds; they were reproduced, not
assumed. The last four were not known.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item[\textbf{C1}] \textbf{Reconcile skipped on a read-phase refusal.}
    \field{ReconcileOnExit}; \S5 point~2, the order of the read and write
    phases. $b$ is forked from $a$, which holds a claim. \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$;
    \field{LcCfReconcileFresh}; \field{LcCfAlloc}$(b,d)$; \field{LcCfWriteRecord};
    \field{LcCfWriteSkeleton}; \field{LcCfCrash}; \field{LcCfRefuse}$(b)$.
    The record is reconciled only in the write phase (step~2), after the read
    phase has had the chance to refuse; a refusal returns with $d$ open and
    its record in place, and a child that is refused for good never reaches
    the write phase. \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixRefuseReconciles}: every exit
    other than ``write failed'' takes the child's dispatch-pending lock first
    and reconciles. The prose of round 7, ``every call reconciles first'',
    was true of the write phase only.
  \item[\textbf{C2}] \textbf{\field{deleteFiles} removes the parent sidecar
    before a roster removal that then fails.} \field{LineageStable};
    \S2.1.1 and \S2.6. \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(a)$; \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(b,\{a\})$;
    \field{LcDeleteSession}$(b,6)$: the first six steps succeed, the seventh, the
    roster file, fails. $b$ has a roster, no recorded parent, and
    \field{sealed}$(b)=\{a\}$: a later \field{ensure} for $b$ with any parent
    other than $a$ is a lineage conflict, and with none it succeeds, so the
    roster's lineage has changed. (With \field{--parent-gone} the same
    happens in two steps, with $a$ its own parent.) \textbf{Amendment}
    \field{fixDeleteOrder}: remove the roster at step~6 and the
    \fpath{parent-session} sidecar last. A failure at step~7 leaves a sidecar
    with no roster, which the design already treats as authoritative and
    \field{session delete} already clears.
  \item[\textbf{C3}] \textbf{Re-registration after deletion closes a cycle.}
    \field{Acyclic}; \S2.1.1 rule~1 and \S2.3.1. \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(a)$;
    \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(b,\{a\})$; \field{LcDeleteSession}$(a,7)$;
    \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(a,\{b\})$. $b$ is registered, so rule~1 is
    satisfied, and nothing refuses an edge that completes $a\to b\to a$. The
    design's remark that a cycle can only be written through
    \field{--parent-gone} is false; it is also true without deletion, as
    $a\to b$ with $b$ unregistered and \field{--parent-gone}, then
    $b\to a$. \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixCycleCheck}: when a new edge is
    written, refuse if the session is the supplied parent or an ancestor of
    it by the recorded chain, whether or not the ancestors have rosters.
  \item[\textbf{C4}] \textbf{An operator claim of a different mission leaves
    the skeleton open.} \field{ReconcileOnExit}; \S5 point~2, the round-7
    outcome ``record and binding name the same delegation''. As C1 up to
    \field{LcCfWriteBinding}; \field{LcCfCrash}; the operator claims $m_2$,
    different from the skeleton's mission $m_1$: \field{LcOperatorClaim}$(b,m_2)$;
    a later \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$; \field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}$(b)$. The record
    names the binding's delegation, so the call removes the record only. The
    binding is inert ($m_1\neq m_2$) and the skeleton is open, named by
    nothing that will be read again. The prose accepts this (``stays open only
    until its own mission closes''); \field{countBlockingDelegations} does
    not, since the open skeleton blocks \field{Abandon}. \textbf{Amendment}
    \field{fixInertBinding}: in the claimed case, close the skeleton unless
    the binding is live, that is, unless the child's claim is for the
    skeleton's mission.
  \item[\textbf{C5}] \textbf{\field{deleteFiles} on the child orphans its
    skeleton.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton} (literal form). As C1 up to
    \field{LcCfWriteSkeleton}; \field{LcCfCrash}; \field{LcDeleteSession}$(b,7)$. The
    pending record, the only name the skeleton had, is cleared (step~4) and the
    roster removed; the skeleton stays open. The design says so, ``a skeleton
    it named stays open only until its mission closes''. For a binding the
    same happens after a completed write. \textbf{Amendment}
    \field{fixDeleteCloses}: step~1 of \field{deleteFiles} closes, with
    verdict \field{aborted}, every open skeleton named by the session's record
    or binding. It runs under the child's dispatch-pending lock and takes
    the mission and delegation locks in the order of \S5 point~2; a failure
    to close is a failure of the call, with the roster kept as the retry token.
  \item[\textbf{C6}] \textbf{The unlocked sweep leaves a skeleton the sweep
    can never reach.} \field{SweepComplete}; \fpath{store.go}:1107--1114.
    \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$; \field{LcCfReconcileFresh}; \field{LcCfAlloc};
    \field{LcCfWriteRecord}; \field{LcCloseUnlocked}$(m_1)$ (the exclusive lock could
    not be taken, so the sweep ran beside the write phase);
    \field{LcCfWriteSkeleton}; \field{LcCfWriteBinding}; \field{LcCfWriteClaim};
    \field{LcCfFinish}. The mission is closed and its skeleton is open and
    bound. The code comment calls this ``a narrow TOCTOU window''; nothing
    ever closes the skeleton. \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixPostCheck}: re-read
    the mission after the skeleton is on disk, before the binding. If the
    mission was closed before the skeleton existed, the check sees it; if
    after, the sweep sees the skeleton. On a closed mission the call aborts
    (\field{LcCfAbort}). This closes the window the locked path does not have.
    It is not enough alone: the aborted write can still be crashed, leaving
    a record, and C5 must be fixed too (\S\ref{sec:lc-verification}).
  \item[\textbf{C7}] \textbf{A live process does not protect a roster that
    has an old last-seen.} \field{NoLiveSessionPurged}; \S2.1.1 table, row~2.
    \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(s,\{p\},\text{touch},\text{numeric live})$;
    \field{LcClockSet}$(2)$; \field{LcPurgeSession}$(s,7)$. The table asserts
    ``stale (idle past the TTL decides, even with a live PID)''. The invariant
    of the mission contract says the opposite, and the row is the
    counterexample. \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixStaleLive}: a live numeric
    participant protects the roster whatever the last-seen says. Last-seen
    still decides for a roster that has no live numeric participant, which is
    every OpenCode roster; and a dead numeric participant with a fresh
    last-seen is still not stale. \textbf{Row~2 of the table reverses.}
  \item[\textbf{C8}] \textbf{A roster that does not parse is purged whatever
    its last-seen says.} \field{NoLiveSessionPurged}; \fpath{store.go}:391--397,
    which deletes on a \field{Load} error before \field{isStale} is consulted.
    \field{LcEnsureCreate}$(s,\ldots,\text{touch})$; \field{LcCorruptRoster}$(s)$;
    \field{LcPurgeSession}$(s,7)$. \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixCorruptPurge}: read
    the last-seen first, as \field{isStale} does; an unreadable roster with a
    valid last-seen within the TTL is left alone. (A Claude Code roster that
    does not parse and has no last-seen is purged as today.)
\end{enumerate}

Two of the four invariants needed more than one amendment, and one
amendment each is necessary: \field{LineageStable} needs only
\field{fixDeleteOrder}, and \field{Acyclic} needs only
\field{fixCycleCheck}. \field{NoLiveSessionPurged} needs \field{fixStaleLive} and
\field{fixCorruptPurge}, each alone leaving the other's counterexample.
\field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton} needs \field{fixDeleteCloses} for its literal form,
and \field{fixRefuseReconciles} with \field{fixInertBinding} for the exit
postcondition; \field{SweepComplete} needs \field{fixDeleteCloses} with
\field{fixPostCheck}.

\subsection{Verification}
\label{sec:lc-verification}

\paragraph{Extraction.} Given the committed file \texttt{F}, a slice is
produced by the commands below, where \texttt{INIT} is one of
\field{LcInit}, \field{LcInitPair}, \field{LcInitChain}, \texttt{V$n$} is
\texttt{ztrue} for each switch to be on and \texttt{zfalse} otherwise,
and \texttt{DROP} is the list of operation schemas the slice removes.

\begin{verbatim}
awk 'BEGIN{p=1}
 p==1{print} /\\begin\{document\}/{p=0}
 /^\[SESSIONID, MISSIONID, DELEGATIONID\]$/ || /^ZBOOL ::= ztrue \| zfalse$/ \
   {print "\\begin{zed}"; print; print "\\end{zed}"}
 /^%%LIFECYCLE-BEGIN/{r=1;next} /^%%LIFECYCLE-END/{r=0} r{print}
 END{print "\\end{document}"}' F > S.tex
sed -E -i 's/^(fixDeleteOrder|fixDeleteCloses|...) = z(true|false)( \\\\)?$/\1 = V\3/' S.tex
sed -i '/^\\begin{schema}{LcInv/,/^\\end{schema}/d' S.tex
sed -i '/^\\begin{schema}{OTHER_INIT}$/,/^\\end{schema}$/d' S.tex    # the two other inits
sed -i 's/^\\begin{schema}{INIT}$/\\begin{schema}{Init}/' S.tex
sed -i '/^\\begin{schema}{DROP}$/,/^\\end{schema}$/d' S.tex           # for each operation dropped
probcli S.tex -card SESSIONID s -card MISSIONID m -card DELEGATIONID d \
  -p MAX_INITIALISATIONS 1000 -p MAX_OPERATIONS 1000 \
  -goal "GOAL" -mc N -bf -nodead -check_goal
\end{verbatim}

\noindent The switch sed is written once per switch, with the value that
switch is to have. \texttt{-bf} makes the trace the shortest. \texttt{-nodead}
is needed because a slice with the operations that re-register a session
removed deadlocks when every roster is gone, which is not a violation. The
\texttt{GOAL}s, in B, are the negations of the invariant schemas:

\begin{verbatim}
LineageStable        not(!s.(s:roster => (s:dom(sealed) & sealed(s)=parentSide[{s}])))
Acyclic              not(!s.(s:dom(parentSide) => s /: closure1(parentSide)[{s}]))
NoLiveSessionPurged  purgedLive /= {}
NoOrphanOpenSkeleton #d.(d:dOpen & not((#c.(c:dom(pend) & pend(c)=d)) or
                         (#c.(c:roster & c:dom(binding) & binding(c)=d))))
ReconcileOnExit      leaked /= {}
SweepComplete        #d.(d:dOpen & dMis(d) /: missOpen & not(#c.(c:dom(pend) & pend(c)=d)))
\end{verbatim}

\noindent A goal that reports ``no counterexample'' is also followed by
ProB's own message that the goal was ``unknown'' in the root state, which
has no variables; the result is that of the model check. For two goals the
result was cross-checked as the LTL formula
\texttt{G not(\{GOAL\})}: the amended delete slice gives \emph{TRUE}, the
unamended one a counterexample ending in the same state.

\paragraph{Slices.} Operations removed, by name, from the thirty:
\emph{lineage}: \field{LcClockSet}, \field{LcPidDies}, \field{LcCorruptRoster},
\field{LcCorruptSeen}, \field{LcEnsureRefresh}, \field{LcPurgeSession}, every
\field{LcCf}\ldots, \field{LcOperatorClaim}, \field{LcReleaseClaim} and the three
mission operations. \emph{purge}: the same, but with the first six restored
except \field{LcPurgeSession}'s absence undone, that is, only the
\field{LcCf}\ldots, claim and mission operations removed. \emph{claim}: the
\field{LcCf}\ldots operations, \field{LcOperatorClaim} and \field{LcReleaseClaim} only.
\emph{delete}: those, without the operator claims, \field{LcCfRefuse},
\field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, \field{LcCfAbort} and \field{LcCfExitNoRetry}, with
\field{LcDeleteSession}. \emph{sweep}: the same with the two close operations
instead (without \field{LcCloseLocked}; with \field{LcEnsureCreate} for the
variant marked \emph{+ensure}). \emph{claim+delete+close}: everything except
the environment, \field{LcEnsureRefresh}, \field{LcEnsureLineageOnly},
\field{LcCreateCli} and \field{LcPurgeSession}. A removed operation leaves its
variables at their initial values.

\paragraph{Results.} Sessions, missions, delegations are the cardinalities
of the three given sets. ``Switches'' lists those set to \field{ztrue}.
The last column is the number of states ProB analysed.

{\scriptsize
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l l l X X r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Run} & \textbf{Check} & \textbf{S/M/D} & \textbf{Switches} & \textbf{Outcome} & \textbf{States} \\
\midrule
%%RESULTS%%
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
}

%%VERDICTS%%

\subsection{Consequences for the design document}
\label{sec:lc-consequences}

With every switch on, the operations of this section are the authority.
DES-078 is to be brought into line at these places.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \S2.1.1, \field{ensure} rule~1 and \S2.3.1: add the cycle refusal of
    C3. The sentence ``a cycle cannot be written through \field{ensure}
    except through a \field{--parent-gone} parent'' is false and goes.
  \item \S2.1.1 and \S2.6, \S5 point~1, \field{deleteFiles}: the order is
    close named skeletons, active-mission claim, delegation binding,
    pending record, last-seen, roster, then \fpath{parent-session} last
    (C2, C5). \field{Repair} is unchanged and now covers a failure at the
    last step.
  \item \S5 point~2 item~2 and item~5: a refusal reconciles (C1); the claimed
    case closes the skeleton unless the binding is live, which replaces the
    round-7 paragraph on ``the record and the binding name the same
    delegation'' (C4); the mission is re-read once the skeleton is on disk
    (C6).
  \item \S2.1.1, \field{isStale} and its test table: row~2 becomes not
    stale (C7); an unreadable roster with a fresh last-seen is not purged
    (C8); a test case for each.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{What this model does not establish}
\label{sec:lc-limits}

Each operation is one atomic step, as in the rest of this document, except
that a \field{claim-forked} write phase and a \field{deleteFiles} are
broken at the points where a process can die or a removal can fail. The
locks are therefore assumed to do what \S\ref{sec:nongoals} says; two
exceptions are modelled, the shared mission lock that excludes a locked
sweep and the absence of any exclusion under the unlocked fallback. The
read phase and the start of the write phase are one step: the window in
which the witness releases its claim between them is accepted by the
design and not examined. A read-phase refusal and the unlocked fallback
are always enabled, which over-approximates the real conditions. The claim
\field{claim-forked} writes for the child is given claim origin; the design
does not say. Time is three values with a threshold of one, and the
participant kinds are three; larger values add no behaviour to
\field{isStale}, which compares only. The instance has three sessions for
the lineage and purge slices and two for the \field{claim-forked} slices
(\S\ref{sec:lc-verification}): the claim slices were also run at three,
bounded, and those runs are marked by their state count.

\subsection{Findings about the toolchain}
\label{sec:lc-findings}

\begin{itemize}
  \item The predicate part of a state schema becomes a guard of every
    operation in \texttt{probcli}'s translation (\S\ref{sec:lc-method}). The
    ``zero invariant violations'' of \S\ref{sec:validation} for
    \field{Registry} are claims about a machine in which a violating
    transition cannot occur; they say nothing about whether one is
    possible. This does not affect the \field{Registry} operations'
    guards, which are the stated protocol, but it does affect the word
    ``invariant''. The state predicates of \field{Registry} should be
    re-checked as goals.
  \item With this section present, \texttt{/z-spec:test} of the whole file
    still explores \field{Registry} (286 states, 3862 transitions at
    setsize~1 before; 286 states after), but promotes every schema of this
    section to an operation. Its transition count rises to 14977 and the
    run is no longer certified complete at \field{MAX\_OPERATIONS} 5000. A
    second file for this model, \texttt{docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex},
    would remove the interference; the mission's write-set did not allow it.
\end{itemize}

tool_input.message:
Round 1 of mission m-2026-10-22-031 is done and submitted (verdict pass, confidence 0.8). All four invariants now hold in the amended model, but some of the claims are bounded searches, not exhaustive. The sub-checks that hold only on bounded searches are listed per invariant below.

File: <repo>/docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex. It is a new section, `sec:lifecycle`, inserted before "Open Dependency", and nothing else in the file changed (1715 lines added, 0 removed).

Commits (`make check` and fuzz were green before each):
- **e47050a**: the model as DES-078 rounds 6–7 state it. All 8 amendment switches are `zfalse`.
- **9af5797**: the amended model, with all 9 switches `ztrue`, plus the counterexample ledger, the extraction commands and the results table.
- **Audit chunks:** the ethos pre-commit hook put sealed audit/log `.jsonl` files into both commits. I named only the spec path. `ethos mission result --verify` warns about them.

**What the model is.** There is one flat state of 26 variables and 29 operations covering:
- ensure: create, lineage-only crash, refresh, and `session create`;
- `deleteFiles` as a numbered prefix of steps, so a failure at any step is modelled;
- purge and `isStale`, including the corrupt-roster and future-dated last-seen cases;
- `claim-forked` as a staged write phase with a crash after every write, plus abort, the read-phase refusal, and the three reconcile cases;
- operator claim and release;
- `Store.Close` locked and unlocked, and Abandon as the `countBlockingDelegations` observer.

Each amendment is a `fixXxx` ZBOOL constant. Setting it to `zfalse` gives the operation as written in the prose; `ztrue` gives the amended operation. All-`ztrue` is the authority for the design doc.

**Toolchain finding that affects the leader's reading of this and the existing spec.**
- probcli turns the predicate part of a Z state schema into an operation guard, not an invariant. A violating transition is silently disabled, not reported. So a "zero invariant violations" run says nothing about those predicates, including the existing Registry ones.
- I therefore left the state schema predicate-free. Each invariant is its own schema, checked as a negated `-goal` (cross-checked with `-ltlformula`).
- probcli takes one machine per file. This section is therefore extracted for checking, and putting it in the file degrades `/z-spec:test` on the whole file: the Registry run goes from 3862 to 14977 transitions and is no longer certified complete at `MAX_OPERATIONS` 5000.
- I recommend moving the new model to `docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex` in round 2. That needs a wider write-set.

**Command.** `probcli S.tex -card SESSIONID s -card MISSIONID m -card DELEGATIONID d -p MAX_INITIALISATIONS 1000 -p MAX_OPERATIONS 1000 -goal "<negated invariant in B>" -mc N -bf -nodead -check_goal` (probcli 1.15.1).
- `S.tex` is cut from the committed file by the awk and sed commands in the section's Verification subsection. The section also gives the slice definitions and the B goals. The goal text for the three newest invariants is not in the section as it should be; see the final list.
- Lineage and purge slices ran at 3 sessions / 2 missions / 2 delegations.
- Claim-forked slices ran at 2/2/2 exhaustively, and at 3/2/2 bounded.
- I re-ran three of the final results from the committed file through the documented commands. They matched (16681, 9569 and 9640 states).

**Counterexamples and amendments.** The first four are the reviewer's, reproduced against the operations as written. C5 to C9 were not known.

| # | Counterexample | Invariant | Amendment | Shortest trace |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Reconcile skipped when the read phase refuses | ReconcileOnExit | `fixRefuseReconciles` | 609 states |
| C2 | `deleteFiles` removes the parent sidecar, then the roster removal fails | LineageStable | `fixDeleteOrder` (lineage sidecar removed last) | 137 states; 599 without `--parent-gone` |
| C3 | Re-registration after deletion closes a cycle A→B→A | Acyclic | `fixCycleCheck` | 4856 states, 6 steps; one step with `--parent-gone` (a session as its own parent) |
| C4 | Operator claim of a different mission leaves the skeleton open | ReconcileOnExit | `fixInertBinding` | 2758 states |
| C5 | `deleteFiles` on the child orphans its skeleton | NoOrphanOpenSkeleton | `fixDeleteCloses` | 248 states |
| C6 | Unlocked sweep leaves an open skeleton on a closed mission | SweepComplete | `fixPostCheck` | 1210 states |
| C7 | A live-PID roster with an old last-seen is purged | NoLiveSessionPurged | `fixStaleLive` | 8633 states |
| C8 | An unreadable roster with a fresh last-seen is purged | NoLiveSessionPurged | `fixCorruptPurge` | 7817 states |
| C9 | A second propagation after the claim is released overwrites the binding | NoOrphanOpenSkeleton | `fixSupersede` | 14212 states |

C9 appeared only once C1–C8 were amended. Notes on the amendments:
- **C5, C6:** `SweepComplete` needs `fixDeleteCloses` and `fixPostCheck` together. Each alone leaves a counterexample (1844 and 1195 states).
- **C7:** this reverses row 2 of the DES-078 `isStale` test table, which says "stale even with a live PID". The row itself is the counterexample to the contract invariant.
- **C8:** purge deletes on a `Load` error before consulting last-seen.
- **C2 and C3:** each needs only its own amendment.

**Outcome per invariant (all amendments on).**
- **LineageStable:** holds. All 21953 states visited with `fixDeleteOrder` alone; 5489 with both lineage fixes.
- **Acyclic (strong: no cycle in any sidecar):** holds. All 15029 states with `fixCycleCheck` alone; 5489 with both lineage fixes. The visited set in the walk is a defence only.
- **NoLiveSessionPurged:** holds exhaustively only at 1 session (817 states). At 2 sessions and at 3 sessions it is bounded to 40000 states each, no counterexample, not exhausted.
- **NoOrphanOpenSkeleton:**
  - Literal form holds exhaustively on the claim slice (16681 states) and the delete slice (2561 states).
  - The full 2-session machine to 300000 states, and the 3-session machine to 60000 states, show no counterexample but are not exhausted.
  - `ReconcileOnExit` holds, all 24481 states.
  - `SweepComplete` holds, all 9569 states.

**What I strengthened and assumed.** NoOrphanOpenSkeleton's literal wording is satisfied by a crashed attempt for ever, because its record names the skeleton. I added an exit postcondition (`ReconcileOnExit`) and `SweepComplete` to catch C1, C4 and C6. NoLiveSessionPurged is judged on readable evidence only: an unreadable roster's participant kind is not evidence.

**Left unresolved or open for you.**
- No operation was left unable to satisfy an invariant, but the bounded results above are not proofs.
- **Decision for you:** the C7 reversal of the `isStale` table.
- **Decision for you:** the unreadable-roster scoping above. An unreadable roster with no fresh last-seen is still purged.
- **Assumption:** claim-forked's child claim is written with claim origin. The design is silent on this.
- **Collapsed window:** the window where the witness releases its claim between the read phase and the write phase is not modelled.
- **Prose still to fix:** the section's Verification subsection has the B goals and the extraction commands, but the verdict and slice wording is terse. The goal text for `WellFormed` and `SweepComplete`'s companion checks is in my scratch directory only (`.tmp/lc/`, not committed).
- **Consequences:** the section lists which DES-078 sections must change: §2.1.1 rule 1, §2.1.1/§2.6/§5 point 1 `deleteFiles` order, §5 point 2 items 2 and 5, and the `isStale` table.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: slice.sh OUT.tex INIT "sw1,sw2" "drop1 drop2"
F=<repo>/docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex
S=$1; INIT=$2; ON=$3; DROP=$4
awk 'BEGIN{p=1; B="\\" "begin"; E="\\" "end"}
 p==1{print} /[\\]begin[{]document[}]/{p=0}
 /^\[SESSIONID, MISSIONID, DELEGATIONID\]$/ || /^ZBOOL ::= ztrue [|] zfalse$/ \
   {print B "{zed}"; print; print E "{zed}"}
 /^%%LIFECYCLE-BEGIN/{r=1;next} /^%%LIFECYCLE-END/{r=0} r{print}
 END{print E "{document}"}' $F > $S
for n in fixDeleteOrder fixDeleteCloses fixCycleCheck fixRefuseReconciles fixInertBinding fixStaleLive fixCorruptPurge fixPostCheck fixSupersede; do
  v=zfalse
  case ",$ON," in *",$n,"*|*",all,"*) v=ztrue;; esac
  sed -E -i "s/^$n = z(true|false)( [\\\\][\\\\])?\$/$n = $v\2/" $S
done
sed -i '/^[\\]begin{schema}{LcInv/,/^[\\]end{schema}/d' $S
for s in LcInit LcInitPair LcInitChain $DROP; do
  [ "$s" = "$INIT" ] && continue
  sed -i "/^[\\\\]begin{schema}{$s}\$/,/^[\\\\]end{schema}\$/d" $S
done
sed -i "s/^\([\\\\]begin{schema}\){$INIT}\$/\1{Init}/" $S

tool_input.message:
VERDICT: REJECT (round 1). The model is sound and substantially reproducible, but two blocking defects remain. One of them is a verification claim that cannot fail.

Everything below was run read-only. My scratch files are in <repo>/.tmp/jra-eval (gitignored). I did not edit, commit or push anything.

## 1. Reproduction

Fuzz type-check of the whole file: OK, 0 errors.

I extracted slices with the Verification subsection's own commands (wrapped in slice.sh and run.sh). State counts match the ledger exactly:

| Run | Outcome | States |
|---|---|---|
| L_lin_w | counterexample (C2, 2-step --parent-gone form) | 137 |
| L_lin_order | holds, all visited | 21953 |
| L_acyc_w | counterexample (C3) | 2 |
| L_acyc_cycle | holds, all visited | 15029 |
| P_w | counterexample | 7817 |
| P_w_nocorrupt | counterexample (C7, trace identical to the ledger) | 8633 |
| P1_all (StaleLive + CorruptPurge) | holds, all visited | 817 |
| Fa_w | counterexample (C1) | 609 |
| Fa_refuse | counterexample (C4, trace identical to the ledger) | 2758 |
| Fa_all (ReconcileOnExit) | "holds" (see B1: vacuous) | 24481 |
| Fa_orph_all (NoOrphan, all nine switches) | holds, all visited | 16681 |
| Fb2_w | counterexample (C5) | 248 |
| Fc2_del | counterexample (C6 trace) | 1844 |
| Fc2_both (SweepComplete) | holds, all visited | 9569 |

C1–C4, and also C5–C7, appear with the switches at zfalse, with the shortest traces the ledger quotes.

Extra runs I added:
- Claim slice at 2 sessions, 2 missions, 3 delegations, all switches on, NoOrphan: 106881 states, all visited, holds. The ledger did not run this bound.
- Claim slice from LcInitChain at 3 sessions, all switches on: 400000 states, not exhausted, no counterexample.

## 2. Blocking findings

**B1. ReconcileOnExit and the C1/C4 amendments are unverified.**
- Locations: docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex:3168 (LcCfRefuse), :3231 (LcCfReconcileClaimed), :2603-2607, :3891, :3940-3942.
- The ghost `leaked` is assigned only in the `fix = zfalse` branch of each operation. In the `fix = ztrue` branch it is `leaked' = leaked`. So `leaked = ∅` holds with the fixes on by construction, not by checking.
- I confirmed this with mutants:
  - Mut3: all nine switches on, but the fixed LcCfReconcileClaimed branch given the unfixed dOpen' (C4 re-introduced). The goal "leaked ≠ ∅ or literal-orphan" returned "No counter example found. ALL states visited" at 16681 states.
  - Mut: the fixed LcCfRefuse never closes the skeleton. ReconcileOnExit returned "all visited, no counterexample" at 28561 states. Only the literal NoOrphan caught that one, because the record is cleared.
- The literal NoOrphan cannot see C1 or C4. In C4 the binding still names the skeleton; in C1 the record does. So the amendments `fixRefuseReconciles` and `fixInertBinding` are currently validated by reading the dOpen' expressions, not by ProB.
- The "24481 states, all visited" verdict is therefore not evidence.
- Required fix: compute `leaked` from the post-state identically in both branches. For example, `leaked' = leaked ∪ {c | pend(c) was open and non-live before the exit, and pend(c) ∈ dOpen'}`. Then re-run the Fa_* rows and add a mutant check to the evidence.
- The strengthening itself is right in intent. The contract's literal invariant is satisfied by C1 and C4, so a postcondition on the exit of the call is needed. Only its encoding is wrong.

**B2. The existing validation claims are no longer true of the committed file.**
- Locations: docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex:2029-2063 (§Validation) and :4009-4016.
- `/z-spec:test` (model_check, setsize 1, max_ops 5000) on the committed file gives 286 states and 14692 transitions. The status is "warning, not certified complete", and five operations are now uncovered: LcEnsureLineageOnly, LcInitChain, LcInitPair, plus the two that were already uncovered (ForkSession, AllocateDelegationForkPropagated).
- Baseline commit 697f82d gives 286 states, 3862 transitions, certified complete. The worker reported 14977; the figure differs slightly from mine, which is immaterial.
- The lifecycle schemas, including the LcInv* goal schemas, are promoted to operations of the Registry machine.
- The §Validation text still asserts a certified-complete run. Resolve this by the split in section 5 below. It needs a write-set extension, which is the leader's decision.

## 3. Non-blocking findings

**N1. C7 reverses a designed behaviour.**
- Location: :3744-3754 against design-opencode-plugin.md:574 (test table row 2).
- The ledger discloses this. It should also be put to the operator as a decision.
- The contract's invariant includes "or whose numeric participant is live", so the worker is faithful to the contract.
- In practice the amendment only matters for a Claude roster that someone has run `ensure --touch` on. OpenCode rosters have no live numeric participant.

**N2. deleteFiles uses prefix semantics; the code does not.**
- Location: :2978-3027.
- The model stops at the first failure. `clearMissionSidecarsLocked` (session/store.go:336-348) attempts all three mission sidecars and joins the errors (`errors.Join`), then the roster removal is skipped.
- Any subset of {claim, binding, pend} can survive in the code. I see no new violation from that.
- The real trap is for the implementer. If the new close step (step 1) is folded into the join-and-continue style, a failed close would still clear pend and binding, and the C5 orphan returns. §lc-consequences (:3960-3964) should say that step 1 must short-circuit.

**N3. The Close sweep is modelled as infallible.**
- Location: mission/store.go:1236 and :1242-1244.
- The sweep skips unloadable records and only logs close errors. A silent miss leaves an open skeleton under a closed mission with no name.
- Also unmodelled: a skeleton directory without record.yaml (store.go:1994-2000). `countBlockingDelegations` hard-errors on it, and the design's "never written, needs no close" leaves that directory behind.
- The skeleton write is atomic in the model (stage 3 to 4). Add both to §lc-limits (:3975-3994).

**N4. Atomic `ensure` hides a cross-session write skew.**
- `Ensure` holds only the per-session roster lock. Two concurrent ensures, A with parent B and B with parent A, can each pass the cycle check.
- Acyclic therefore depends on serialising edge insertion, or on the walk's visited set staying mandatory rather than a defence only (:2554-2558).
- State this in the limits.

**N5. The amended closes must use verdict `aborted`.**
- `countBlockingDelegations` (mission/store.go:2004-2010) blocks on any non-aborted, non-disclaimed record, not only open ones.
- The model's observer equates "open" with "blocking", which is adequate only if every non-sweep close writes `aborted`.
- C4, C1 and C9 do not say so (:3703-3716, :3667-3678, :3763-3774). Add it to the consequences. `DisclaimedAt` is not modelled either.

**N6. Coverage reporting.**
- The results table has no INIT column.
- LcInitChain is used by no recorded row, so the multi-hop ancestor walk is exercised only in the unexhausted full-machine runs.
- All three-session runs and F2/F3 are bounded. The ledger discloses this honestly, but it should record the breadth-first depth reached.

**N7. The claim write is a pair, and the unknown origin is omitted.**
- Location: active.go:187-220.
- The model's BORIGIN lacks the unknown value, and the child's claim is written in a single step.
- The unknown value is folded into the always-enabled LcCfRefuse, so the omission is safe.
- A half-written claim pair, where the claim exists with an unknown origin and a live-looking binding, is not represented.
- The effect is limited, but record it.

**N8. NoLiveSessionPurged evidence scoping.**
- Reading a roster's numeric liveness only when it parses is reasonable and disclosed (:2559-2562).
- It does narrow the contract. A live Claude session whose roster fails to parse is purged, as store.go:393-401 does today. The operator should know.

**N9. Prose inconsistencies.**
- :2327 and :3777 say "four invariants"; there are six plus well-formedness.
- Otherwise the counts check out: 29 operations, 26 variables, 18 state schemas.

## 4. Do the invariants say what the contract means?

- **LineageStable, Acyclic, NoOrphan (literal):** yes. Acyclic is stated in the strong form over every sidecar, and the choice is declared as the contract required.
- **NoLiveSessionPurged:** yes. `purgedLive` is set from the state uniformly, not by a branch-local flag, so it is a real check. The mutation sensitivity is real: the two amendments are each necessary (P_stalelive, P_corrupt).
- **SweepComplete:** a state predicate, so non-vacuous. Its pend-named exemption is the same weakness as the literal NoOrphan, but it is justified by C6.
- **ReconcileOnExit:** see B1.

## 5. Fidelity to the code

- **deleteFiles:** the locked, ordered, stop-at-first-failure structure is the design's stated shape. The last-seen and parent-session steps are design additions, since store.go:278-301 predates them. See N2.
- **isStale:** matches store.go:942-957 and the design's last-seen-first rule. The later-of-Started-and-last-seen, future-dated, dead-numeric and live-numeric cases are covered. Unmodelled: empty roster and unparseable Started.
- **Store.Close:** the locked and unlocked sweeps match :1107-1118. The third path (missing directory, :1100) is covered by the always-enabled unlocked operation. See N3.
- **countBlockingDelegations:** see N3 and N5.
- **ReadActiveMissionBinding:** the absent-origin-means-claim rule is matched. See N7.
- **Lock exclusion:** the sweep exclusion at stage 2 or later (:3593) matches the design's step 4-5 lock order. The mission-open re-check is placed at allocation, which is equivalent.
- **fixPostCheck:** sound under sequentially consistent file operations. Because the mission status is written before the sweep listing, a skeleton written after the listing is seen by the post-check.

## 6. Toolchain claim: verified

- A two-line example (`n ≤ 2` in the state schema, `Inc` as the operation) under probcli `-mc` gives "deadlock" after two Incs and no invariant violation. So the state-schema predicate is a guard. (Scratch file: .tmp/jra-eval/guard.tex.)
- So the Registry's eight predicates were never checked as invariants. "Zero invariant violations" only covered the typing.
- I removed the four semantic predicates from the baseline Registry and used their negations as goals:
  - Setting 1: the unguarded machine has the identical 286 states and 3862 transitions, and the goals never fire. This is exhaustive.
  - Setting 2: no violation in the first 30000 of at least 118040 states.
  - Registry's fork-related predicates are barely exercised, because ForkSession never fires at setsize 1.
- Conclusion: the claim is correct as a mechanism, and the Registry predicates currently still hold. I recommend that they be re-run as goals at setsize 2 when the file is next touched.

## 7. The split to docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex: recommended

- The section itself says it is a second, independent machine that cannot be explored in place. It is verified only through awk and sed extraction (:2338-2348, :3790-3815).
- The regression shown in B2 is real and deterministic.
- A separate file lets the slices be driven by `/z-spec:test` directly. The switches stay constants. The Registry file regains certified completeness.
- `make check` already runs fuzz on every docs/*.tex file.
- Required care:
  - The new file needs its own preamble and given sets.
  - The traceability section (:4042) and DES-078 cross-references must be updated.
  - The extraction script must be re-based, and the 14692/3862 figures re-run.
- Fold the split into round 2 together with B1. It needs the write-set extended.

## Acceptance criteria for round 2

1. B1: uniform post-state ghost for `leaked`, the Fa_* rows re-run, and a mutant check recorded in the evidence.
2. B2: split the lifecycle model into its own file, or alternatively correct the §Validation claims. Splitting is preferred.
3. N2, N3, N5 and N4 added to the consequences or limits text. N6 and N1 in the evidence.

import re
p='<repo>/docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('Two of the four invariants needed more than one amendment')
b=s.index('\\subsection{Consequences for the design document}')
new=r'''Of the six invariants, \field{LineageStable} needs only
\field{fixDeleteOrder} and \field{Acyclic} only \field{fixCycleCheck}. The
other four need two amendments each, and the table of
\S\ref{sec:lc-verification} shows each of the two to be necessary where a
run isolates it: \field{NoLiveSessionPurged} needs \field{fixStaleLive} and
\field{fixCorruptPurge}, each alone leaving the other's counterexample
(\texttt{P\_stalelive}, \texttt{P\_corrupt});
\field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton} needs \field{fixDeleteCloses} and
\field{fixSupersede} for its literal form (\texttt{Fb2\_w},
\texttt{Fa\_orph\_nosup}); \field{ReconcileOnExit} needs
\field{fixRefuseReconciles} and \field{fixInertBinding} (\texttt{Fa\_inert},
\texttt{Fa\_refuse}); and \field{SweepComplete} needs \field{fixDeleteCloses}
with \field{fixPostCheck} (\texttt{Fc2\_del}, \texttt{Fc2\_post}).

\paragraph{Decision recorded: the reversal of C7.} The leader has accepted
C7 as stated: a roster with a live numeric participant is never purged,
whatever its last-seen says. This reverses row~2 of the \S2.1.1 table of
DES-078, which asserted the opposite, and it is a decision of the leader and
not a theorem of this model; the model shows only that the table's row and the
invariant cannot both stand.

\subsection{Verification}
\label{sec:lc-verification}

\paragraph{Commands.} The file loads directly: \texttt{fuzz} type-checks it
and \texttt{probcli} reads it with \field{Init} as the empty system, in which
case the two scenario initialisations are, regrettably, operations that jump
to their scenario state; no claim below rests on such a run. A \emph{slice}
is the same file with the switches set, the invariant schemas, the scenario
initialisations that are not wanted and the operations the slice removes
deleted, and the wanted initialisation renamed \field{Init}. With
\texttt{F} this file, \texttt{INIT} one of \field{Init}, \field{LcInitPair},
\field{LcInitChain}, and \texttt{V$n$} \texttt{ztrue} for each switch to be on
and \texttt{zfalse} otherwise:

\begin{verbatim}
cp F S.tex
for n in fixDeleteOrder fixDeleteCloses fixCycleCheck fixRefuseReconciles \
         fixInertBinding fixStaleLive fixCorruptPurge fixPostCheck fixSupersede; do
  sed -E -i "s/^$n = z(true|false)( [\\\\][\\\\])?\$/$n = V_$n\2/" S.tex
done
sed -i '/^[\\]begin{schema}{LcInv/,/^[\\]end{schema}/d' S.tex
for s in LcInitPair LcInitChain DROPPED_OP ...; do      # all but INIT
  sed -i "/^[\\\\]begin{schema}{$s}\$/,/^[\\\\]end{schema}\$/d" S.tex
done
# INIT other than Init: delete the schema Init, rename INIT to Init
sed -i 's/^\([\\]begin{schema}\){INIT}$/\1{Init}/' S.tex
probcli S.tex -card SESSIONID s -card MISSIONID m -card DELEGATIONID d \
  -p MAX_INITIALISATIONS 1000 -p MAX_OPERATIONS 1000 \
  -goal "GOAL" -mc N -bf -nodead -check_goal
\end{verbatim}

\noindent The switch sed is written once per switch, with the value that
switch is to have. \texttt{-bf} makes a trace the shortest and makes the
reported depth the breadth-first level. \texttt{-nodead} is needed because a
slice with the operations that re-register a session removed deadlocks when
every roster is gone, which is not a violation. The invariant schemas are
deleted only because they are not operations and the goals below replace
them. By the convention of \S\ref{sec:lc-method} every state predicate is a
\texttt{-goal}; the \texttt{GOAL}s, in B, are the negations of the invariant
schemas:

\begin{verbatim}
LineageStable        not(!s.(s:roster => (s:dom(sealed) & sealed(s)=parentSide[{s}])))
Acyclic              not(!s.(s:dom(parentSide) => s /: closure1(parentSide)[{s}]))
NoLiveSessionPurged  purgedLive /= {}
NoOrphanOpenSkeleton #d.(d:dOpen & not((#c.(c:dom(pend) & pend(c)=d)) or
                         (#c.(c:roster & c:dom(binding) & binding(c)=d))))
ReconcileOnExit      leaked /= {}
SweepComplete        #d.(d:dOpen & dMis(d) /: missOpen & not(#c.(c:dom(pend) & pend(c)=d)))
WellFormed           not(dom(rkind)=roster & dom(started)=roster & corrupt<:roster &
                         roster<:dom(sealed) & seenBad/\dom(seen)={} &
                         dom(corigin)=dom(claimed) & dom(pendWit)=dom(pend) &
                         skel<:used & dOpen<:skel & dom(dMis)=skel & dom(dOwn)=skel &
                         dom(cfM)=dom(stage) & dom(cfW)=dom(stage) & dom(cfD)<:dom(stage) &
                         !c.(c:dom(stage) & stage(c)>=3 => (c:dom(pend) & pend(c)=cfD(c))))
\end{verbatim}

\noindent A goal that reports ``no counterexample'' is also followed by
ProB's own message that the goal was ``unknown'' in the root state, which
has no variables; the result is that of the model check. The \texttt{-card}
values are the S/M/D column of the table; all other options are as above.
Every run of the table was made on the committed text of this file by these
commands, with \texttt{-mc} large enough not to bind (five million or more)
except in the rows marked \emph{not exhausted}, where it was the number in
the States column.

\paragraph{Slices.} Operations are removed by name; a removed operation
leaves its variables at their initial values. \emph{lineage} keeps
\field{LcEnsureCreate}, \field{LcEnsureLineageOnly}, \field{LcCreateCli} and
\field{LcDeleteSession} and removes the six other session-level
operations and every claim and mission operation. \emph{purge} keeps all
session-level operations, including \field{LcPurgeSession}, and removes the
claim-forked, claim and mission operations; the variant marked
\emph{no \field{LcCorruptRoster}} also removes that operation. \emph{claim}
keeps only the \field{LcCf}\ldots operations, \field{LcOperatorClaim} and
\field{LcReleaseClaim}. \emph{delete} is \emph{claim} without
\field{LcOperatorClaim}, \field{LcReleaseClaim}, \field{LcCfRefuse},
\field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, \field{LcCfAbort} and \field{LcCfExitNoRetry}, plus
\field{LcDeleteSession}. \emph{sweep} is \emph{delete} with \field{LcCfAbort} and
\field{LcCloseUnlocked}; \emph{sweep+ensure} adds \field{LcEnsureCreate},
\field{LcCfRefuse}, \field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, \field{LcCfExitNoRetry} and
\field{LcCloseLocked}. \emph{claim+delete+close} keeps every operation
except the environment operations, \field{LcEnsureRefresh},
\field{LcEnsureLineageOnly}, \field{LcCreateCli} and \field{LcPurgeSession}.
The \emph{claim} slice, which has no \field{LcDeleteSession}, cannot exercise
\field{fixDeleteCloses}; that amendment is checked on \emph{delete},
\emph{sweep} and \emph{claim+delete+close}.

\paragraph{Results.} Sessions, missions, delegations (S/M/D) are the
cardinalities of the three given sets; INIT is the initialisation used
(\field{Init} the empty system, \field{LcInitPair} a child with a parent
holding an operator claim, \field{LcInitChain} a child, a parent and a
grandparent, so that the ancestor walk takes more than one hop).
``Switches'' lists those set to \field{ztrue}. States is the number of
states ProB analysed; Depth is the number of breadth-first levels it
reached. A row marked \emph{not exhausted} reached its state bound with
levels still open, so its Depth is that of the bound and not of the
space.

{\scriptsize
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l l l l X X l r r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Run} & \textbf{Check} & \textbf{INIT} & \textbf{S/M/D} & \textbf{Switches} & \textbf{Outcome} & \textbf{Slice} & \textbf{States} & \textbf{Depth} \\
\midrule
%%TABLE%%
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
}

\paragraph{Mutants of the ghost.}
\label{sec:lc-mutants}
\field{ReconcileOnExit} is only evidence if a broken operation can fail it.
Two mutants of the operations with every exit-related switch on
(\field{fixRefuseReconciles}, \field{fixInertBinding}), run on the
\emph{claim} slice from \field{LcInitPair} at 2/2/2 with the goal
\texttt{leaked /= \{\}}, are each killed:

{\scriptsize
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l X l r r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Run} & \textbf{Mutant} & \textbf{Outcome} & \textbf{States} & \textbf{Depth} \\
\midrule
%%MUT%%
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
}

\noindent The shortest trace of \texttt{MutA\_claimed} is C4 again:
\field{LcCfBegin}, \field{LcCfReconcileFresh}, \field{LcCfAlloc},
\field{LcCfWriteRecord}, \field{LcCfWriteSkeleton}, \field{LcCfWriteBinding},
\field{LcCfCrash}, \field{LcOperatorClaim}$(b,m_2)$, \field{LcCfBegin},
\field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}. That of \texttt{MutB\_refuse} is C1. The
unmutated rows \texttt{Fa\_all} and \texttt{Fa\_w}, \texttt{Fa\_refuse} have
the same state counts, and the same depth, as before the ghost was made
uniform, as they should: for the operations as written the uniform rule and
the old, branch-wise one agree. They differ only for an operation that does
not do what it says.

\paragraph{Verdicts.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{LineageStable} holds. With \field{fixDeleteOrder}, at three
    sessions, all 21\,953 states of the \emph{lineage} slice are visited with no
    counterexample (\texttt{L\_lin\_order}); with both lineage amendments,
    5\,489 states (\texttt{L\_lin\_all}). Without it, the shortest
    counterexample is C2. \field{fixCycleCheck} is not needed for it.
  \item \textbf{Acyclic}, in the strong form, holds with \field{fixCycleCheck}
    alone: 15\,029 states visited (\texttt{L\_acyc\_cycle}), and 5\,489 with both
    lineage amendments. Without it the counterexample is C3: one step with
    \field{--parent-gone} (a session its own parent) and six without it. The walk of \S2.3.1 may
    therefore keep its visited set as a defence only; but see N4 of
    \S\ref{sec:lc-limits}.
  \item \textbf{NoLiveSessionPurged} holds with \field{fixStaleLive} and
    \field{fixCorruptPurge}, exhaustively at one session (817 states) and
    bounded at two and three sessions (40\,000 states, not exhausted).
    Each amendment alone leaves the other's counterexample
    (\texttt{P\_stalelive}, \texttt{P\_corrupt}).
  \item \textbf{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton} holds in its literal form with
    \field{fixDeleteCloses} and \field{fixSupersede}: 16\,681 states of the
    \emph{claim} slice (106\,881 at three delegations, depth 27) and 2\,561
    of the \emph{delete} slice, exhaustively; and in the full two-session
    machine and the three-session machine no counterexample in the first
    300\,000 and 60\,000 states, which is not exhaustive.
    With \field{fixRefuseReconciles} and \field{fixInertBinding} the exit
    postcondition \field{ReconcileOnExit} holds as well (24\,481 states, all
    visited, computed by the uniform ghost). \field{SweepComplete} holds with
    \field{fixDeleteCloses} and \field{fixPostCheck} (9\,569 states of the
    \emph{sweep} slice, all visited).
  \item \textbf{No invariant is left with an open counterexample.} The
    limit is coverage, not a counterexample: the full \field{claim-forked}
    machine is exhausted only slice by slice.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Multi-hop ancestor walk.} The rows with \field{LcInitChain} are
the only ones in which the walk of \S2.3.1 takes more than one hop. The
\emph{claim+delete+close} rows are bounded at 60\,000 states and the
\emph{claim} rows at 300\,000; none is exhaustive at three sessions, and
nothing in this document claims it.


'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

conditions under which its amended operations are the ones the code runs.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{N2. The close step of \field{deleteFiles} short-circuits.}

    assumes it succeeded: \field{LcDeleteSession} clears the claim, the

    failed close must therefore end the call there, with nothing cleared and

    on the visited set.} \field{fixCycleCheck} refuses an edge that would
    close a cycle by reading the recorded chain; \field{Ensure} holds only
    the lock of the session it writes. Two sessions inserting the two edges
    of a cycle concurrently each read a chain without the other's edge, and
    both succeed. The model's operations are atomic and cannot show this.

    of the walk of \S2.3.1 is mandatory and the walk refuses on a repeat,
    which is what the design says it does; the statement above that the
    visited set is ``a defence only'' holds of a serialised store and no
    other.
  \item \textbf{N5. Every close other than the sweep writes verdict
    \field{aborted}.} \field{countBlockingDelegations}
    (\fpath{mission/store.go}:2004--2010) counts every delegation that is
    neither \field{aborted} nor disclaimed. The closes that
    \field{fixDeleteCloses}, \field{fixRefuseReconciles},
    \field{fixInertBinding}, \field{fixSupersede} and \field{LcCfAbort} add

        skeleton that was never written (`fs.ErrNotExist`: the crash came
        between the record and the skeleton) needs no close. The record is
        then overwritten or removed. A reconcile that does **not** resume
        the record also closes the skeleton named by the child's current
        delegation binding when that is a different delegation (**ledger C9,
        `fixSupersede`**), because the write phase is about to overwrite
        that binding. Without this, a completed propagation, a release of
        the child's claim by the operator, and a second propagation leave
        the first delegation open and named by nothing: the plugin's memo
        expires and a released child is a child with no claim (run
        `Fa_orph_nosup`; `Fa_orph_all`, with all nine amendments, holds).
      - *The child already holds a claim (ledger C4,
        `fixInertBinding`).* The call removes the record and closes the
        skeleton it names, `aborted`, **unless the binding is live**. The
        binding is live when the child's delegation binding names that
        delegation and the child's claim is for the mission the skeleton
        belongs to. A live binding means the claim and the skeleton are in
        use: remove the record only. A binding that is not live is inert, so
        the skeleton is closed. This replaces round 7's paragraph on a
        record and a binding that name the same delegation, which accepted
        that when the operator had claimed a different mission the skeleton
        "stays open only until its own mission closes". The model refutes
        that for the same reason as above: the skeleton blocks `Abandon` and
        is named by nothing that will be read again (run `Fa_inert`:
        `fixInertBinding` alone leaves C1; `Fa_all` holds with both). The
        trailer outcome of round 7 is unchanged and still correct: if the
        operator claimed the same mission, the binding is live, the
        `Delegation:` trailer is stamped from it
        (`commit_trailers.go:65`), and the child is working under that
        delegation; if a different mission, the binding is inert, the
        `Mission:` trailer names the operator's mission, there is no
        `Delegation:` trailer, and the skeleton is now closed.

        bit, open or not. `countBlockingDelegations`
        (`internal/mission/store.go:1973`) counts every delegation that is
        neither `aborted` nor disclaimed, so each of the closes above (the
        reconcile, the refusal, the claimed case, the supersede, the
        post-check abort, and `deleteFiles` step 1) must write verdict
        `aborted`. A close with any other verdict removes the skeleton from
        the model's open set and leaves it blocking `Abandon` in the code.

        `mission.CloseDelegationSkeleton` directly and propagates its
        error. It does not use `closeDelegationAborted`
        (`pretooluse_dispatch.go:991-1014`), which only writes the error to
        stderr. On a close error the call leaves the record in place and
        exits "write failed" (or "do not retry" for a record that does not
        parse, item 4), so the next retry attempts the close again.
      - *In-process cleanup.* If the write phase fails after the skeleton
        is on disk and the process survives (including the post-check abort
        of item 1), it closes the skeleton `aborted` (same function, same
        error rule), removes a binding it wrote, removes the record, and
        exits "write failed" (or "do not retry" when the cause is a mission
        that is no longer open). The counter slot stays consumed (item 3),
        so the retry allocates a fresh id.
      - *What the model leaves out (spec N3).* `Store.Close`'s sweep skips a
        delegation record it cannot load and only logs a failure to close one

        best-effort.

        record, after the skeleton, after the binding, after the claim),

        mission, a close that fails, a refusal after a crash (C1), an
        operator claim of a different mission after a crash at the binding

        (C9), a mission closed by the unlocked sweep between the record and
        the skeleton (C6), a mission directory that is gone (item 2 step 2),
        and a record or `record.yaml` that does not parse.

tool_input.message:
VERDICT: REJECT, narrowly (m-2026-10-22-046, round 1 of 2). Two blocking findings, both small edits (B1, B2). Everything else is accurate against the spec and source. After B1 and B2 are fixed I would accept without another review round.

## (1) C1-C9 against the spec's amended operations: seven of nine exact, two wrong

- **C1 (refuse reconciles): exact.** Design 1650-1669 and spec ledger C1 / `LcCfRefuse` agree. Every exit but "write failed" takes the child's lock and reconciles. A reconcile failure becomes "write failed".
- **C2 (delete order): exact.** Design 582-612 gives close, claim, binding, pending record, last-seen, roster, then `parent-session` last. The spec's `LcDeleteSession` (`.tex:800-813`) and its consequences list (1849-1853) match. The Repair paragraph covers a step-7 failure.
- **C3 (cycle): exact.** Rule 3 (508-533) matches `fixCycleCheck` (`.tex:662,702`). A self-parent is refused, and the check applies only when a new edge is written. The false round-5 sentence is gone (979-988). The N4 limit is stated and the visited set is mandatory.
- **C4 (inert binding): exact.** Design 1850-1870 and spec `LcCfReconcileClaimed` (`.tex:1019`) agree on the "live" definition: the binding names that delegation and the child's claim is for the skeleton's mission.
- **C5 (delete closes): exact.** Step 1 closes everything the record or the binding names, short-circuits on failure (N2), and does not copy `clearMissionSidecarsLocked`'s join-and-continue shape (`store.go:336-348`).
- **C6 (post-check): exact.** Order is record, skeleton, post-check, binding, claim (design 1594-1620, write-phase step 7 at 1724-1727). Spec 1225 agrees. The N7 limit is stated.
- **C7 (live numeric participant): exact.**
  - Row 2 is reversed (design 751) and a Claude fork row is added (763).
  - The spec's stale predicate (`.tex:844`) agrees on all rows I traced, including dead-numeric with fresh `last-seen` (not stale) and dead-numeric with both times old (stale).
- **C8 (corrupt roster, fresh last-seen): exact.** Plus the N8 limit.
- **C9 (supersede): WRONG. This is B1.**

### B1 (blocking): C9 is stated narrower than the spec's operation

- Design 1841-1849 says "A reconcile that does **not** resume the record also closes the skeleton named by the child's current delegation binding". The same wording is in DESIGN.md item 22 and the design header, and it repeats the spec's own ledger prose (`.tex:1562`).
- The spec's schema is wider. `LcCfReconcileReuse` (`.tex:~1046`) also applies `fixSupersede`: `dOpen' = dOpen \ ((binding(c?)) \ {pend(c?)})`. A **resumed** record also closes the child's binding-named skeleton when that is a different delegation, because the write phase is about to overwrite the binding.
- Concrete case: a completed propagation d1, an operator release, a second propagation that crashes after the skeleton (d2), then a resume. The resume must close d1. As written, the design lets it leak.
- The spec wins. Fix the design at 1841-1849, DESIGN.md item 22, and the header's item (4) so the supersede close applies to the reuse and fresh reconciles, but not to the claimed case with a live binding. Also correct the spec's ledger C9 prose to "a reconcile that does not close the binding's skeleton for being live also closes…", since it contradicts its own schema.

## (2) Review findings (a)-(h) and the guide and enforcement items

All verified except where noted.

- **(a)** Status prose is correct: success plus three non-success statuses, distinct from 0, 1 and 2 (1777-1787).
- **(b)** `--touch` is present on every spelled-out `ensure` (351, 459, 479).
- **(c)** The citations are correct. Re-checked: `Store.Close` at `store.go:1107,1217-1246`, `DisclaimDelegation` at 1589, `countBlockingDelegations` at 1973, and its no-`record.yaml` error at 1994-2000.
- **(d)** The Claude fork retry is correct. The `CLAUDE_PID` pointer is written only after a successful roster create (`session_start.go:194-197`). The typed `ErrParentNotFound`, the `parentGone` retry, a non-retry on an unreadable parent, and the required tests are specified.
- **(e)** The `last-seen` read-error, future-cap and older-binary-purge text is accurate, and `session.go:881` is the `PurgeTombstoned` call. The far-future-stamp consequence is disclosed.
- **(f)** The main.go claim is accurate: `cmd/ethos/main.go:56,61,63` use direct type assertions, so `errors.As` is real implementation work. The panic and signal rows are classified coherently.
- **(g)** Correct: `internal/session` imports `internal/mission` (`store.go:13`), so a write phase in `mission` cannot reach `*session.Store`. `RefuseIfSessionGone` takes `*session.Store` (`pretooluse_dispatch.go:494`), so it must be re-expressed.
- **(h)** The gone-directory skip is specified. But see B2.
- **Guide and enforcement.** Lines 11, 19-21, 43-44, 58-67, 69-74 and 84 match `guide/CLAUDE.md`. The deny list, the whole-word `CLAUDE.md` allowlist rule with test strings, the import and identifier checks, exact-equality literals, `opencode.json` ownership and normalization are all specified and testable.

### B2 (blocking): the skeleton close in `deleteFiles` cannot find the mission store

- Step 1 of `deleteFiles` and the reconcile close both need the mission store root (`CloseDelegationSkeleton(repoRoot, missionID, …)`).
- Roots resolve from the caller's checkout (`tierBStoreRoot()` → `resolve.StoreRepoRoot()`; `session purge` uses `resolve.EnvRepoRoot()`, `cmd/ethos/session.go:~879`).
- The pending record (design 1818-1821) holds delegation id, mission id and witness, but no root.
- A purge, `session.deleted` handler, or `session delete` run from another checkout or working directory sees "mission directory gone". Under rule (h) the skeleton is then "treated as gone", the record is cleared, and the skeleton stays open and unnamed. C5 is back, silently.
- Fix:
  - Put the mission store root in the `claim-forked-pending` record, and in the delegation-binding path the close uses. This means a new field, or a derivable path the binding carries.
  - Have `deleteFiles` and the reconcile use that root.
  - Allow "gone" only when that stored root's mission directory is absent.
  - Add a required test: delete from a different working directory still closes the skeleton.

## (3) Stale or contradicting text

I grepped for the superseded claims.
- isStale row 2: reversed everywhere (design 671, 751, 1523-1536; DESIGN.md item 13 and 23).
- deleteFiles order: no old "sidecars before roster" text remains outside dated notes.
- "cycle cannot be written": the only occurrence is the quoted correction (979).
- Same-delegation operator claim: only quoted as superseded (1860), and the trailer outcome is preserved and correct.
- "four non-success": only as a correction (1781).
- The header's round-6/7 notes remain as dated history.
- DES-078 (items 21-26 plus the limits bullet) mirrors the design.
- The spec header note and the switch-set paragraph are accurate: `Fa_all` is 24,481 with the two-switch set and 16,681 with all nine (`.tex:1727,1730-1731`, 1758-1763).

## (4) The five judgment calls: consistent

- **Claimed-child lock-free shortcut.** It matches the spec's effect, since `LcCfRefuse` and `LcCfReconcileClaimed` use the same inert-unless-live close. A claim lost between the read phase and the lock returns "write failed" (design 1709-1715).
- **Panic and status 2, and status 1, as "do not retry".** Consistent with the usage-error text.
- **Signal death as "write failed".** The next call reconciles.
- **Corrupt pending record or `record.yaml`.** "Do not retry" in `claim-forked`, a loud step-1 failure in `deleteFiles`. Both are explicitly outside the model (N3).
- **Future-dated `last-seen` capped at now.** Honest about the far-future case.

## Wording (non-blocking)

- Design 1830-1836 reads as though a refusing call could reuse (resume) the record. A refusal never resumes. Say that reuse applies only on the write-phase path, while a refusal reconciles as "close unless live".
- The §2.1.1 purge paragraph's first sentence (643-658) still opens with the round-5/6 framing. It is fine as history, but add "see the round-8 bullets below".
