## Review of `git diff 3c7fc87..HEAD`: `docs/design-opencode-plugin.md`, `DESIGN.md` (DES-078), `docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex`

Read-only; I edited nothing. I found three high-confidence issues: one stale passage in DES-078, one gap in the design that undoes ledger C5, and one place where the design disagrees with the spec.

**Citations hold.** I checked the repo `file:line` references that the round 6–8 text adds or changes against the source, and every one matches:
- `internal/session/store.go`: 82-93, 110-196, 200-203, 230-245, 278-301, 279, 336-348, 360-362, 385-404, 391-397, 404, 514, 933, 942-957, 950-956, 962-964, 13
- `internal/mission/store.go`: 1107, 1217-1246, 1236, 1242-1244, 1589, 1973, 1994-2000, 2004-2010
- `cmd/ethos/main.go`: 51-70, 64-70
- `cmd/ethos/session.go`: 79, 697, 881
- `cmd/ethos/mission.go`: 2112, 2113
- `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`: 222, 494-508, 775-787, 791-808, 810-838, 853-861, 880-889, 991-1014
- `internal/hook/commit_trailers.go`: 32-40, 45-72, 53-56, 65
- `internal/mission/active.go`: 101-119, 240-250, 495-497, 619-625
- `internal/mission/delegation.go`: 462-466
- `internal/hook/session_start.go`: 69, 187-188, 194-197
- `internal/resolve/resolve.go`: 316-322
- `cmd/ethos/hook.go`: 234-251
- `plugin/hooks/commit-msg.sh`: 55, 160-161
- `internal/enable/enable.go`: 46, 119-137, 173
- `internal/enable/deposit.go`: 15
- `internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md`: 11, 19-21, 43-44, 58-67, 69-74, 84
- `internal/session/session.go`: 10, 25-32

I did not verify the `.tmp/` OpenCode references.

**Other checks that came out consistent:** the seven-step `deleteFiles` order, the `isStale` and purge rules, and the `ensure` rules 1–3 agree across the design, DESIGN.md items 21–23, and the spec schemas (`LcDeleteSession`, `LcPurgeSession`, `LcEnsureCreate`, `LcCfReconcile*`). Every spelled-out plugin `ensure` command in the design doc carries `--touch`, and every `--parent-gone` use there follows the rules.

### Important (80-89)

**1. DES-078 decision point 3 has round-2/4/5 text that later rounds superseded.** Confidence 85.
- **Where:** `<repo>/DESIGN.md:12360`, `:12370`, `:12374`.
- **12360:** the plugin's fork-registration command is spelled `ethos session ensure --parent-session <id>` with no `--touch`. Round 8 item 26 (DESIGN.md:12273-12274) says every spelled-out plugin `ensure` command carries `--touch`.
- **12374:** it says Claude Code's `SessionStart` hook calls `session ensure --parent-session`. That reads as the CLI path the plugin uses. The design says the hook calls `Store.Ensure` in-process, never with `touch`, and retries with `parentGone` on `ErrParentNotFound` (design §2.5; DESIGN.md items 12, 18, 24).
- **12370:** it says "the order is skeleton, binding, then claim, and a retry reuses unclaimed partial state". Round 8 changed both halves:
  - The order is now record, skeleton, post-check, binding, claim (C6).
  - A retry reuses a delegation only when mission, witness, open skeleton, open mission and unclaimed child all match. Otherwise it closes the skeleton `aborted` (C1, C4, C9; design §5 point 2 item 5).
- **Fix:**
  - 12360: append `--touch` ("`ethos session ensure --parent-session <id> --touch`").
  - 12374: change to "to register lineage through `Store.Ensure` (in-process, with the fork's parent, without `touch`) and call `claim-forked`".
  - 12370: add a round-8 qualifier: "round 8: record, skeleton, post-check, binding, claim; a retry reuses only a matching open record and otherwise closes the skeleton `aborted`, see items 21–22".

**2. The pending record and the binding don't carry the mission's repo root, so `deleteFiles` step 1 can skip an open skeleton without reporting it, which undoes C5.** Confidence 82.
- **Where:**
  - `<repo>/docs/design-opencode-plugin.md:1818-1820` (record schema "YAML: delegation id, mission id, witness")
  - `:587-593` (`deleteFiles` step 1)
  - `:1703-1708` ("If the record's mission directory is gone … treats the skeleton as gone")
- **Why it breaks:**
  - Skeletons are repo-local. `CloseDelegationSkeleton(repoRoot, missionID, …)` refuses an empty `repoRoot` (`internal/mission/delegation.go:650-652`), and the path is `RepoStatePath(repoRoot, "missions", …)`.
  - The session store, the pending record and the `DelegationBinding` are global, and none of them records the repo root.
  - `deleteFiles` runs from `ethos session delete`, the OpenCode `session.deleted` handler, and `ethos session purge`. Purge may run outside any repo (`cmd/ethos/session.go:875-879`).
  - From the wrong root or no root, the close finds no mission directory. The "directory gone → treat as gone" rule then counts that as success. Step 4 clears the only name the skeleton had, and the skeleton stays open and blocks `Abandon` (`countBlockingDelegations`).
- **Fix:**
  - Add the mission store root (`resolve.StoreRepoRoot()` at write time) to the `claim-forked-pending` record and to the binding written by `claim-forked`, or state where step 1 gets it.
  - Use "mission directory gone" only when a recorded, resolvable root shows the mission directory is absent.
  - When the root is unknown or unresolvable, make it a step-1 failure (keep the roster as the retry token) rather than "gone".
  - Add a test that runs `deleteFiles` from a different working directory.

**3. On a roster that exists but won't parse, the design has `ensure --touch` refresh `last-seen`, but the spec forbids that refresh.** Confidence 80.
- **Where:** `<repo>/docs/design-opencode-plugin.md:534-541` (rule 4: "If a roster exists, `ensure` with `--touch` changes only `last-seen`").
- **The conflict:**
  - The spec's `LcEnsureRefresh` has the guard `s? \notin corrupt` (`docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex:729`), so the model never refreshes `last-seen` on an unreadable roster.
  - The design gives no exception. Read literally, the plugin's 15-minute refresh would keep a corrupt roster fresh for ever, which with C8 (`fixCorruptPurge`) makes it permanently unpurgeable.
  - The design says the spec wins where they disagree, and design rule 4 states the opposite.
- **Fix:** add to rule 4: "If the roster exists but fails to load, `ensure` writes nothing (`last-seen` included) and exits non-zero with the load error (spec `LcEnsureRefresh`, `s? \notin corrupt`)." Also add a test that a corrupt roster's `last-seen` is unchanged after `ensure --touch`.

### Critical (90-100)

None.

## DES-078 invariant and completeness audit, round 8 (read-only)

I checked the design against `docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex` and against the cited Go source. The fixes for C1 to C9 match the spec's operations where the design restates them. Four claims are still false. Three of them come from closes or creates that the spec never models: the Claude Code Tier B delegation binding, the non-fork `SessionStart` creator, and the Claude-side `claim-forked` caller.

### Verdicts on the claims from earlier passes

1. **Lineage write-once: holds, with stated gaps** (N4; older-binary leftovers are covered by Repair). Two new defects, F3 and F6 below.
2. **Purge liveness: holds, with a stated gap** (N8 and the older binary). Three new wording defects, F7.
3. **No orphan skeleton: FALSE.** See F1 (CRITICAL) and F2 (HIGH).
4. **Exit-status table is complete and exclusive: FALSE.** See F4.
5. **Guide neutrality is enforced: FALSE.** See F5.
6. **The harness list is the single source of truth: holds, with a gap** narrower than the prose. See F8.
7. **The design claims nothing the spec does not model without saying so: FALSE.** See F1, F3, F6 and F7(a).
8. **The `deleteFiles` seven steps: complete for the files the design names**, but the scope of step 1 is wrong (F1). Minor: crash leftovers named `last-seen.*.tmp` and `claim-forked-pending.*.tmp` (the `writeSidecarFile` temp naming, `active.go:290`) are not on the removal list.

### F1. CRITICAL: `deleteFiles` step 1 aborts live Claude Code Tier B delegations

- **Claim:** "Close, with verdict `aborted`, every open skeleton named by the session's `claim-forked-pending` record or by its delegation binding."
  - Where: `design-opencode-plugin.md:587-594`, repeated at `:1169-1172` and `:1821-1823`.
  - Spec basis: ledger C5. In the spec, `binding` is written only by `LcCfWriteBinding`.
- **Falsifying case:** Tier B dispatch writes the leader's own binding: `WriteDelegationBinding(globalRoot, sessionID, {DelegationID, MissionID, ParentSession: sessionID})` at `pretooluse_dispatch.go:880-884`.
  - Tier B skeletons stay `open` until `Store.Close` sweeps them. `CloseDelegation` has no production caller, so nothing closes them earlier.
  - Sequence: a Claude leader dispatches a worker, the worker finishes, then the leader's `SessionEnd` (or a purge) runs `deleteFiles`. Step 1 rewrites that delegation to `aborted`. The later mission close skips it (`store.go:1239`, which skips any delegation not `open`), so the true `pass` or `fail` verdict is lost.
  - Every Claude Code session change of this kind is unmodelled and undisclosed.
- **Fix:** Step 1 closes the binding's skeleton only when it is a fork-propagated delegation owned by this session. Discriminators: the binding's `ParentSession != sessionID`, or a `spawn_pattern`/`bound_via` value on the record that `claim-forked` writes. Add a test that a Tier B leader binding survives `deleteFiles` with its verdict still `open`.

### F2. HIGH: the supersede close is stated more broadly than the spec

- **Claim:** "A reconcile that does **not** resume the record also closes the skeleton named by the child's current delegation binding" (`:1841-1849`). The design also says a read-phase refusal "runs the reconcile of item 5" (`:1653-1657`).
- **What the spec actually does:** `fixSupersede` appears only in `LcCfReconcileReuse` and `LcCfReconcileFresh`. `LcCfRefuse` and `LcCfReconcileClaimed` close only skeletons named by the pending record that are not live.
- **Falsifying case:** A claimed child has a live binding to D2 (for example a Claude fork that ran Tier B dispatch) and a stale record naming D1. Read literally, the design's claimed or refusal exit also closes D2 with `aborted`, even though the child is working under it.
- **A second ambiguity:** the supersede sentence sits inside "If a record exists…". But C9's own trace has no record, because it was removed at finish.
- **Fix:** Restrict supersede explicitly to the two write-proceeding paths, and say it applies whether or not a record exists.

### F3. HIGH: an unspecified creator runs over a recorded lineage

- **Claims:**
  - `:624-633`: "`ethos session create` (`Store.CreateInCheckout` called on behalf of the CLI) … refuses"; "a `SessionStart` for any other source keeps today's `CreateInCheckout` path".
  - `:1151-1152`: "`Ensure` never overwrites a recorded lineage, so a repeated or resumed `SessionStart` … cannot erase it."
- **Falsifying case:** `createSessionRoster` (`session_start.go:69,194`) runs on every `SessionStart`, including `compact`, `resume` and `clear`. A Claude fork that later compacts or resumes calls `CreateInCheckout` on an id whose `parent-session` sidecar is set. The outcome depends on where the refusal lives:
  - If the refusal is in the Store method, roster creation fails and `WriteCurrentSession` is skipped (`:196`). A resumed fork gets no pointer file, so later session resolution fails.
  - If the refusal is CLI-only, the roster is replaced by a transition the spec forbids. `LcCreateCli` guards `parentSide[s] = ∅`, and `SessionStart`'s create is not modelled at all.
  - Either way, line 1151 justifies `resume` by citing `Ensure`, which that path does not call.
- **Fix:** Put the refusal in the CLI only, and route every `SessionStart` source for an id that already has a roster or sidecar through `Ensure` (create-if-absent). Add that path to the spec as an operation, and add tests for `compact` and `resume` of a fork.

### F4. MEDIUM: the exit-status table is not exhaustive (§5 point 2 item 4, `:1777-1800`)

- **Claim:** "assigns every cause exactly one of four statuses", with "a plugin action for each". Causes with no row:
  - an I/O error from `ReadActiveMissionBinding` (`active.go:187-202`) on the child (read-phase step 2) or on the witness (step 3);
  - a read error from `ParentOf` that is not not-found, during the walk;
  - a `ReadDelegationBinding` error during the reconcile's liveness test;
  - failure to remove the record at finish;
  - a post-check abort whose cleanup close also fails. Its cause maps to "do not retry", but the close failure maps to "write failed", so it has two statuses.
- **Internal contradiction:** §2.3 (`:885-887`) offers ancestors "until one succeeds", but "do not retry" says "do not try another ancestor". A nearer witness whose claimed mission has since closed therefore blocks a grandparent whose mission is open, once per memo interval, indefinitely.
- **Caller scope:** §5 point 3 makes Claude Code's `SessionStart` a second caller, but the table gives actions only for the plugin. Claude has no `execute.before` retry, and the design does not say how its witnesses are chosen.
- **Minor:** `main.go:85-100` also exits 2 when the error message begins with certain prefixes. The design does not fix the order of the `errors.As` mapping relative to that test.
- **Fix:** Add rows for each cause above, resolve the post-check-cleanup combination explicitly, make the witness-iteration rule match the table, and add a caller-action column for Claude.

### F5. HIGH: the guide deny list does not enforce the neutrality it claims (`:2043-2061`)

- **Claim:** the deny list (`.claude/`, `Claude`, `SessionStart`, `CLAUDE_`, `subagent`) "so a harness name cannot return to the shared guide unnoticed". The text also implies round 8's list closes the `@`-import gap that round 7 missed.
- **Falsifying inputs:**
  - The guide's line 11 (`` `@`-imported ``) passes the check.
  - Any OpenCode-only line, such as one naming `opencode.json` or `.opencode/plugins`, passes. "OpenCode" is a harness name and is not on the list.
  - The guide's lines 19-20, "Session hooks inject your persona into context at start and after compaction", are false under OpenCode (§1.2 item 4 registers no session hook). They pass the check, and the enumeration describes lines 19-21 only as the agent-file generation note.
  - The enforcement wording at lines 43-44 passes the check.
- **Fix:** Generate the deny list from `harnesses.go`: every harness name plus its literals. Add an explicit `@`-import pattern. Name the persona-injection sentence in the enumeration.

### F6. MEDIUM: refreshing a corrupt roster differs from the spec

- **Rule 4** (`:540-542`): "If a roster exists, `ensure` with `--touch` changes only `last-seen`".
- **Spec:** `LcEnsureRefresh` requires `s? ∉ corrupt`.
- **Consequence:** the plugin refreshes `last-seen` on an unparseable roster every 15 minutes. Under `fixCorruptPurge` that roster is then never purged and never repaired, and `claim-forked` returns "do not retry" for it.
- **Fix:** `Ensure` loads the roster on refresh and refuses on a parse error. State this.

### F7. MEDIUM: three statements about current code and purge are inaccurate

- **(a)** `:695-701`: "any other case (absent, unparseable, older than the TTL) purges it". This leaves the `last-seen` read error (permission denied) unassigned. `:682-688` says a read error is "not stale". Pick one for the unreadable-roster branch.
- **(b)** `:696-699` says `Purge` and `PurgeTombstoned` delete an unreadable roster. In fact `Store.Purge` has no production caller, and `PurgeTombstoned` refuses without `--force` (`store.go:469-503`). C8 applies only under `--force`.
- **(c)** `:710-712`: "a long-running `ethos serve`… ages a … roster out". `internal/mcp` has no purge path, so this is false. Delete it.

### F8. MEDIUM: the single source of truth is narrower than the prose (`:2106-2153`)

- **Claims:** "Adding a harness is one entry"; "none is a hand-written string that names a harness". Gaps:
  - The allowlist entry `CLAUDE.md`, matched by exact equality, also admits `filepath.Join(repoRoot, "CLAUDE.md")` (`enable.go:127,173`). That path is Claude Code's own root memory file, so it is a harness artifact, not the guide.
  - `cmd/ethos/uninstall.go:37-49` (removes only the Claude Code plugin) is not scanned.
  - The doctor remedy strings (`doctor.go:371` and others) are not scanned.
  - The `validate-content` remedy (`main.go:88`, "run `ethos enable`") is not scanned.
  - The deny list in F5 is a second, hand-maintained list of harness terms.
- **Fix:** Allowlist only the literal `.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md`, scan the whole `cmd/ethos` and `internal/doctor` trees, and derive the deny list from the harness list.

### Lower-severity items

- **F9.** The `claim-forked` reuse path (`:1830-1837`) "finishes the missing writes" at reconcile step 2, which comes before the locks of step 5. The spec's `LcCloseLocked` guard assumes the shared mission lock is held at stages 4 and 5. Fix: state that reuse goes through steps 5 and 6 before it writes.
- **F10.** `:1695-1699` says the delegation lock "excludes every other writer of the same `record.yaml`". The unlocked fallback of `Store.Close` (`store.go:1107-1114`, `closeDelegationSkeletons`) takes no delegation lock, so a reconcile can overwrite a sweep's `pass` with `aborted`. Fix: disclose this, or take the delegation lock in the sweep.
- **F11.** `DESIGN.md:12369-12370` still says the write order is "skeleton, binding, then claim, and a retry reuses unclaimed partial state". It omits the pending record and the post-check (C6) and contradicts the conditional reuse rule. `DESIGN.md:12395` ("any … literal") contradicts the round-8 allowlist.
- **F12.** `:1667-1669`: "a child whose roster is gone cannot have [a record]". An older binary's `Delete` leaves the record behind. The behavior is still safe, because the condition is on whether the directory exists, but the sentence is false.

### Confirmed against the spec and code

- The fixes:
  - C2 order, C3 cycle refusal, C6 post-check;
  - the C7 and C8 rules and the `TestIsStale` rows;
  - the N2 short-circuit;
  - N5 verdict `aborted`.
- The `commit_trailers.go:53-56` and `:65` gating.
- The `main.go:51-70` direct type assertions.
- The `RefuseIfSessionGone` semantics.
- The `EnableTo` marker-before-`chainHooks` order.
- Coverage limits: `DESIGN.md` states the model is exhaustive only slice by slice (`NoLiveSessionPurged` is exhaustive only at one session). `design-opencode-plugin.md` itself does not say this.

Files: `<repo>/docs/design-opencode-plugin.md`, `<repo>/DESIGN.md`, `<repo>/docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex`, `<repo>/internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`, `<repo>/internal/hook/session_start.go`, `<repo>/internal/session/store.go`, `<repo>/internal/mission/active.go`, `<repo>/internal/mission/store.go`, `<repo>/internal/mission/delegation.go`, `<repo>/internal/enable/enable.go`, `<repo>/internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md`, `<repo>/cmd/ethos/main.go`, `<repo>/cmd/ethos/uninstall.go`, `<repo>/cmd/ethos/session.go`, `<repo>/cmd/validate-content/main.go`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Stage 1: F1 (origin discriminator, Tier B dispatch, NoForeignAbort).
import re, sys
P = '<repo>/docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s = open(P).read()

def sub(old, new, count=1):
    global s
    n = s.count(old)
    assert n == count, (n, count, old[:80])
    s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- types
sub(r"""\begin{zed}
BORIGIN ::= boClaim | boDispatch
\end{zed}
""", r"""\begin{zed}
BORIGIN ::= boClaim | boDispatch
\end{zed}

\begin{zed}
DKIND ::= dkFork | dkTierB
\end{zed}
""")

# --- switch
sub("fixSupersede : ZBOOL\n\\where", "fixSupersede, fixOrigin : ZBOOL\n\\where")
sub("fixSupersede = ztrue\n\\end{axdef}", "fixSupersede = ztrue \\\\\nfixOrigin = ztrue\n\\end{axdef}")

# --- state
sub(r"""dMis : DELEGATIONID \pfun MISSIONID \\
dOwn : DELEGATIONID \pfun SESSIONID
\end{schema}""", r"""dMis : DELEGATIONID \pfun MISSIONID \\
dOwn : DELEGATIONID \pfun SESSIONID \\
dKind : DELEGATIONID \pfun DKIND
\end{schema}""")
sub(r"""\begin{schema}{LcMission}""", r"""\begin{schema}{LcVerdict}
dAbort : \power DELEGATIONID
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{LcMission}""")
sub(r"LcOpen \land LcMission \land LcSealed", r"LcOpen \land LcVerdict \land LcMission \land LcSealed")

# --- inits
for name in ("Init", "LcInitChain", "LcInitPair"):
    pass
sub("dOwn' = \\emptyset \\\\\n", "dOwn' = \\emptyset \\\\\ndKind' = \\emptyset \\\\\ndAbort' = \\emptyset \\\\\n", count=3)

# --- Xi LcVerdict in every operation that does not change it
delta_verdict = {'LcDeleteSession', 'LcPurgeSession', 'LcCfRefuse', 'LcCfReconcileClaimed',
                 'LcCfReconcileReuse', 'LcCfReconcileFresh', 'LcCfAbort'}
out = []
cur = None
for line in s.split('\n'):
    m = re.match(r'\\begin\{schema\}\{(Lc[A-Za-z]+)\}', line)
    if m:
        cur = m.group(1)
    out.append(line)
    if line == '\\Delta Lifecycle \\\\' and cur and cur not in delta_verdict:
        out.append('\\Xi LcVerdict \\\\')
s = '\n'.join(out)

# --- origin filter, as a text fragment used below
def own(d, c):
    return r"(fixOrigin = zfalse \lor ((%s \mapsto %s) \in dOwn \land (%s \mapsto dkFork) \in dKind))" % (d, c, d)

# --- deleteFiles and purge step 1 (two identical occurrences)
old = r"""fixDeleteCloses = ztrue \implies dOpen' = dOpen \setminus ((pend \limg \{ s? \} \rimg) \cup (binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg)) \\
fixDeleteCloses = zfalse \implies dOpen' = dOpen \\
"""
new = (r"""(\exists X : \power DELEGATIONID @ X = \{ d : dOpen | fixDeleteCloses = ztrue \land d \in (pend \limg \{ s? \} \rimg) \cup (binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg) \land """
       + own('d', 's?') + r""" @ d \} \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus X \land dAbort' = dAbort \cup X) \\
""")
sub(old, new, count=2)

# --- LcCfRefuse
old = r"""(fixRefuseReconciles = zfalse \land pend' = pend \land pendWit' = pendWit \land dOpen' = dOpen) \lor (fixRefuseReconciles = ztrue \land pend' = \{ c? \} \ndres pend \land pendWit' = \{ c? \} \ndres pendWit \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus (\{ rd : pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg | \lnot ((c? \mapsto rd) \in binding \land (\exists m : MISSIONID @ (rd \mapsto m) \in dMis \land (c? \mapsto m) \in claimed)) @ rd \})) \\"""
new = (r"""(fixRefuseReconciles = zfalse \land pend' = pend \land pendWit' = pendWit \land dOpen' = dOpen \land dAbort' = dAbort) \lor (fixRefuseReconciles = ztrue \land pend' = \{ c? \} \ndres pend \land pendWit' = \{ c? \} \ndres pendWit \land (\exists X : \power DELEGATIONID @ X = \{ rd : dOpen | rd \in pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg \land \lnot ((c? \mapsto rd) \in binding \land (\exists m : MISSIONID @ (rd \mapsto m) \in dMis \land (c? \mapsto m) \in claimed)) \land """
       + own('rd', 'c?') + r""" @ rd \} \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus X \land dAbort' = dAbort \cup X)) \\""")
sub(old, new)

# --- LcCfReconcileClaimed
old = r"""(fixInertBinding = ztrue \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus (\{ rd : pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg | \lnot ((c? \mapsto rd) \in binding \land (\exists m : MISSIONID @ (rd \mapsto m) \in dMis \land (c? \mapsto m) \in claimed)) @ rd \})) \lor (fixInertBinding = zfalse \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus \{ rd : pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg | (c? \mapsto rd) \notin binding @ rd \}) \\"""
new = (r"""(\exists X : \power DELEGATIONID @ X = \{ rd : dOpen | rd \in pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg \land ((fixInertBinding = ztrue \land \lnot ((c? \mapsto rd) \in binding \land (\exists m : MISSIONID @ (rd \mapsto m) \in dMis \land (c? \mapsto m) \in claimed))) \lor (fixInertBinding = zfalse \land (c? \mapsto rd) \notin binding)) \land """
       + own('rd', 'c?') + r""" @ rd \} \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus X \land dAbort' = dAbort \cup X) \\""")
sub(old, new)

# --- LcCfReconcileReuse
old = r"""(fixSupersede = zfalse \land dOpen' = dOpen) \lor (fixSupersede = ztrue \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus ((binding \limg \{ c? \} \rimg) \setminus \{ pend(c?) \})) \\"""
new = (r"""(\exists X : \power DELEGATIONID @ X = \{ d : dOpen | fixSupersede = ztrue \land d \in binding \limg \{ c? \} \rimg \land d \neq pend(c?) \land """
       + own('d', 'c?') + r""" @ d \} \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus X \land dAbort' = dAbort \cup X) \\""")
sub(old, new)

# --- LcCfReconcileFresh
old = r"""(fixSupersede = zfalse \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus (pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg)) \lor (fixSupersede = ztrue \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus ((pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg) \cup (binding \limg \{ c? \} \rimg))) \\"""
new = (r"""(\exists X : \power DELEGATIONID @ X = \{ d : dOpen | (d \in pend \limg \{ c? \} \rimg \lor (fixSupersede = ztrue \land d \in binding \limg \{ c? \} \rimg)) \land """
       + own('d', 'c?') + r""" @ d \} \land dOpen' = dOpen \setminus X \land dAbort' = dAbort \cup X) \\""")
sub(old, new)

# --- LcCfAbort
sub(r"""dOpen' = dOpen \setminus \{ cfD(c?) \} \\""",
    r"""dOpen' = dOpen \setminus \{ cfD(c?) \} \\
dAbort' = dAbort \cup (\{ cfD(c?) \} \cap dOpen) \\""")

# --- LcCfWriteSkeleton
sub(r"""dOwn' = dOwn \oplus \{ cfD(c?) \mapsto c? \} \\""",
    r"""dOwn' = dOwn \oplus \{ cfD(c?) \mapsto c? \} \\
dKind' = dKind \oplus \{ cfD(c?) \mapsto dkFork \} \\""")

# --- Tier B dispatch operation
tierb = r"""\paragraph{Tier B dispatch} (\fpath{pretooluse\_dispatch.go}:775--884).
\field{LcTierBDispatch} is the path Claude Code already runs when a leader
spawns a subagent against a mission. It takes the id (\field{NewID}), the
shared mission lock and the delegation lock, re-reads the mission, and
writes the skeleton with \field{ParentSession} equal to the \emph{session
itself}; it then writes the session's own delegation binding, naming the
new skeleton, over whatever the binding named before. Nothing in the
dispatch closes the skeleton: \fpath{subagent\_stop.go} does not, and
\field{CloseDelegation} has no caller outside the tests, so a Tier B
skeleton stays open until \field{Store.Close} sweeps it
(\fpath{mission/store.go}:1239 skips only a skeleton that is already not
open). The operation is atomic here, since it holds the shared mission
lock; the window in which the unlocked fallback can pass it is that of
\S\ref{sec:lc-limits}. A Tier B skeleton has kind \field{dkTierB}; the
skeleton \field{claim-forked} writes has kind \field{dkFork}. In the code
the kind is the skeleton's \field{BoundVia} (a new value for
\field{claim-forked}); the binding sidecar carries no field of its own and
its origin is that of the skeleton it names.

\begin{schema}{LcTierBDispatch}
\Delta Lifecycle \\
\Xi LcTime \\
\Xi LcRoster \\
\Xi LcKind \\
\Xi LcStarted \\
\Xi LcCorrupt \\
\Xi LcLineage \\
\Xi LcSeen \\
\Xi LcClaim \\
\Xi LcPending \\
\Xi LcFlight \\
\Xi LcVerdict \\
\Xi LcMission \\
\Xi LcSealed \\
\Xi LcPurged \\
\Xi LcLeak \\
s? : SESSIONID \\
m? : MISSIONID \\
d? : DELEGATIONID
\where
s? \in roster \\
s? \notin \dom stage \\
m? \in missOpen \\
d? \notin used \\
used' = used \cup \{ d? \} \\
skel' = skel \cup \{ d? \} \\
dOpen' = dOpen \cup \{ d? \} \\
dMis' = dMis \oplus \{ d? \mapsto m? \} \\
dOwn' = dOwn \oplus \{ d? \mapsto s? \} \\
dKind' = dKind \oplus \{ d? \mapsto dkTierB \} \\
binding' = binding \oplus \{ s? \mapsto d? \}
\end{schema}

"""
sub(r"""\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked}""", tierb + r"""\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked}""")

# --- invariants
sub(r"""\begin{schema}{LcInvNoOrphanOpenSkeleton}
Lifecycle
\where
\forall d : dOpen @ (""", r"""\begin{schema}{LcInvNoOrphanOpenSkeleton}
Lifecycle
\where
\forall d : dOpen | (d \mapsto dkFork) \in dKind @ (""")
sub(r"""\begin{schema}{LcInvReconcileOnExit}""", r"""\begin{schema}{LcInvNoForeignAbort}
Lifecycle
\where
\forall d : dAbort @ (d \mapsto dkTierB) \notin dKind
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{LcInvReconcileOnExit}""")
sub(r"""\dom dOwn = skel \\
""", r"""\dom dOwn = skel \\
\dom dKind = skel \\
dAbort \subseteq skel \setminus dOpen \\
""")
open(P, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')

P='docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s=open(P).read()
old=r"""    closes the skeleton named by the child's current binding.
\end{enumerate}"""
assert s.count(old)==1
new=r"""    closes the skeleton named by the child's current binding.
  \item[\textbf{C10}] \textbf{\field{deleteFiles} and the reconcile closes
    abort a delegation they do not own.} \field{NoForeignAbort}; found by
    reading the Claude Code path the model had left out
    (\fpath{pretooluse\_dispatch.go}:775--884). A Tier B dispatch writes the
    leader's \emph{own} delegation binding, with \field{ParentSession} equal
    to the session itself, and leaves the skeleton open until
    \field{Store.Close} sweeps it. \field{LcTierBDispatch}$(s,m,d)$;
    \field{LcDeleteSession}$(s,2)$ (run \texttt{T1\_off}, four steps, three
    states). The step~1 of C5, which closes every open skeleton named by the
    session's binding, aborts $d$: a running subagent's delegation, which the
    leader's session ending (or being purged) does not end. The same happens
    in \field{LcCfReconcileFresh} and \field{LcCfReconcileReuse}, whose
    supersede close (C9) names the child's binding, which a Tier B dispatch by
    the child may have written. \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixOrigin}: a
    skeleton has a kind, \field{dkFork} for the one \field{claim-forked}
    writes and \field{dkTierB} for the dispatch; every close of
    \field{deleteFiles}, purge, refusal, claimed case, resume and supersede
    closes only an open skeleton of kind \field{dkFork} whose owner is the
    session. In the code the kind is the skeleton's \field{BoundVia}, which
    \field{claim-forked} sets to a new value; the binding sidecar gains no
    field, since the skeleton it names carries the kind.
\end{enumerate}"""
s=s.replace(old,new)
old2=r"""  \item \field{SweepComplete}: an open skeleton whose mission is closed is
    named by a pending record. This is what \field{Store.Close}'s sweep is
    for.
\end{itemize}"""
assert s.count(old2)==1
s=s.replace(old2,old2[:-len("\\end{itemize}")]+r"""  \item \field{NoForeignAbort}: no skeleton written by a Tier B dispatch is
    ever closed with verdict \field{aborted} by \field{deleteFiles}, a purge or
    a \field{claim-forked} reconcile. The model has one such writer of a
    Tier B skeleton (the dispatch), so the invariant is a predicate over the
    set of aborted skeletons.
\end{itemize}""")
open(P,'w').write(s)

new=r"""\paragraph{Close-time clearing} (\fpath{cmd/ethos/mission.go}:2278--2311;
\fpath{mission/active.go}:891--955). After \field{ethos mission close} the
\emph{closing} session runs \field{ClearMissionBindings}: it clears its
active-mission claim if the claim names the closed mission, and, independently,
its delegation binding if the binding's mission is the closed one. The two
tests are separate, so a session that closes a mission other than the one it
claims can keep a binding for a mission that is not its claim. That is the
state \field{fixSupersede} exists for (C9), once \field{mission release} no
longer leaves it behind.

\begin{schema}{LcClearClosed}
\Delta Lifecycle \\
\Xi LcTime \\
\Xi LcRoster \\
\Xi LcKind \\
\Xi LcStarted \\
\Xi LcCorrupt \\
\Xi LcLineage \\
\Xi LcSeen \\
\Xi LcPending \\
\Xi LcFlight \\
\Xi LcUsed \\
\Xi LcSkeleton \\
\Xi LcOpen \\
\Xi LcVerdict \\
\Xi LcMission \\
\Xi LcSealed \\
\Xi LcPurged \\
\Xi LcLeak \\
s? : SESSIONID \\
m? : MISSIONID
\where
s? \in roster \\
s? \notin \dom stage \\
m? \notin missOpen \\
(s? \mapsto m?) \in claimed \lor (\exists d : binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg @ (d \mapsto m?) \in dMis) \\
(s? \mapsto m?) \in claimed \implies (claimed' = \{ s? \} \ndres claimed \land corigin' = \{ s? \} \ndres corigin) \\
(s? \mapsto m?) \notin claimed \implies (claimed' = claimed \land corigin' = corigin) \\
(\exists d : binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg @ (d \mapsto m?) \in dMis) \implies binding' = \{ s? \} \ndres binding \\
\lnot (\exists d : binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg @ (d \mapsto m?) \in dMis) \implies binding' = binding
\end{schema}

"""
s=s.replace(r"\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked}", new+r"\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked}")

python3 - <<'E'
P='docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s=open(P).read()
i=s.index(r"  \item[\textbf{C9}]")
j=s.index(r"  \item[\textbf{C10}]")
newc9=r"""  \item[\textbf{C9}] \textbf{A second propagation overwrites the binding of
    the first.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton} (literal form), found only
    after C1 to C8 were amended. A completed propagation: \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$;
    reconcile; \field{LcCfAlloc}$(b,d_1)$ and the four writes; \field{LcCfFinish}.
    Then the child's claim is replaced by an operator claim of another
    mission $m_2$ and $m_2$ is closed by the child's own session
    (\field{LcOperatorClaim}, \field{LcCloseLocked}, \field{LcClearClosed}):
    \field{ClearMissionBindings} clears the claim, which names $m_2$, and
    leaves the binding, which names $d_1$ of $m_1$ (the two tests are
    independent, \fpath{mission/active.go}:907--935). A second
    \field{claim-forked}: \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$; reconcile (the record is
    gone); \field{LcCfAlloc}$(b,d_2)$; the writes up to
    \field{LcCfWriteBinding} (run \texttt{T3\_nosup}, nineteen steps). The
    binding now names $d_2$; $d_1$ is open, named by no record and no
    binding. \textbf{Errata (this revision).} The first statement of C9 reached
    the same state by \field{LcReleaseClaim} leaving the binding in place.
    That was a defect of the model, not of the code: \field{ethos mission
    release} clears the binding as well as the claim
    (\fpath{cmd/ethos/mission.go}:2150--2153), so after a release there is no
    binding for a second propagation to overwrite. The state is reached by
    the close-time clearing above, which is why \field{fixSupersede} is
    still needed (\texttt{T3\_nosup} counterexample, \texttt{T3\_all}
    holds). \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixSupersede}, with its scope stated
    exactly: it applies on the two reconcile paths that go on to write, that
    is \field{LcCfReconcileFresh} and \field{LcCfReconcileReuse}, whether or
    not a pending record exists, and on no other path. It closes the open
    \field{dkFork} skeleton the child's binding names when that is not the
    skeleton the call will use: on the fresh path every such skeleton, on the
    resume path the one that differs from the record's. It is never applied
    by \field{LcCfRefuse} or \field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, whose child either
    does not write or holds a claim, and may be working under the binding. The
    earlier wording, ``a reconcile that does not resume the record'',
    contradicted the schema of \field{LcCfReconcileReuse}, which carries the
    clause; it is withdrawn.
  \item[\textbf{C11}] \textbf{\field{mission release} leaves the skeleton it
    unnames open.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}; found by reading the
    release command that C9 had modelled wrongly. After a completed
    propagation, \field{LcReleaseClaim}$(b)$ clears the claim and the binding
    and nothing closes $d_1$ (run \texttt{T2\_norel}: eleven steps). The
    skeleton is open, named by nothing, and the child that held it has no claim.
    \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixReleaseCloses}: \field{mission release} closes,
    \field{aborted}, the open \field{dkFork} skeleton owned by the session that
    its binding names, before it clears the binding, under the same locks
    as the other closes. A binding that names a Tier B skeleton is cleared
    and the skeleton is left open: it is a subagent's delegation.
  \item[\textbf{C12}] \textbf{A Tier B dispatch by a propagated child buries
    its fork skeleton.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}; open, not amended. The
    child $b$ completes a propagation (binding $d_1$, kind \field{dkFork}) and
    then spawns a subagent against the mission: the dispatch writes
    \emph{its} binding for $b$ over $d_1$ (\fpath{pretooluse\_dispatch.go}:880--884),
    and $d_1$ is open, named by nothing (\field{LcTierBDispatch}, run
    \texttt{T2\_all} with \field{assumeNoTierBOverFork} off). No close in the
    design can find $d_1$ afterwards, since every close is by name. The
    constant \field{assumeNoTierBOverFork} excludes the dispatch from a session
    whose binding names an open fork skeleton, so that the other invariants
    can be checked; it is an assumption of the verification and not a fix.
    The options are listed in \S\ref{sec:lc-consequences}; the choice belongs
    to the leader.
"""
s=s[:i]+newc9+s[j:]
# C10 should precede C11/C12: move C10 block after C9? order: C9, C11, C12, C10 -> fix by renaming: swap labels
open(P,'w').write(s)
E

b=s.index(r"  \item[\textbf{C10}]")

mid=s[a:b]; c10=s[b:e]

E

every source. With \field{fixSessionStart} every source goes through

sources other than \field{fork} take the replacing path: the roster is
rewritten with the lineage a fresh \field{create} has, which is none, over a

\field{parentSide} is not). A resumed or compacted fork is the case. For

gone? : ZBOOL \\

\# par? \leq 1 \\

src? \neq srcFork \implies par? = parentSide \limg \{s?\} \rimg \\

(fixSessionStart = zfalse \land src? \neq srcFork) \implies (roster' = roster \cup \{ s? \} \land rkind' = rkind \oplus \{ s? \mapsto k? \} \land started' = started \oplus \{ s? \mapsto now \} \land corrupt' = corrupt \setminus \{ s? \} \land parentSide' = parentSide \land sealed' = sealed \oplus \{ s? \mapsto \emptyset \})

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re, os, subprocess
P = '<repo>/docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
R = '<repo>/.tmp/lc3/r6/'
s = open(P).read()

def out(n):
    return open(R + n + '.out').read()
def S(n):
    m = re.search(r'States analysed: (\d+)', out(n)); assert m, n
    return '{:,}'.format(int(m.group(1))).replace(',', '\\,')
def D(n):
    m = re.search(r'Breadth-first levels: (\d+)', out(n)); assert m, n
    return m.group(1)
def cex(n): return 'COUNTER EXAMPLE FOUND' in out(n)
def full(n): return 'ALL states visited' in out(n)
def need(n, kind):
    ok = {'cex': cex, 'full': full, 'bound': lambda x: (not cex(x)) and (not full(x)) and 'States analysed' in out(x))}[kind](n)
    assert ok, (n, kind)
    return n

table = open('<repo>/.tmp/lc3/table3.tex').read().rstrip('\n')
mut = open('<repo>/.tmp/lc3/mut3.tex').read().rstrip('\n')
assert 'NOT FINISHED' not in table and 'NOT FINISHED' not in mut

a = s.index(r'\paragraph{Direct run.}')
b = s.index(r'\subsection{Consequences for the design document}')

new = r'''\paragraph{Direct run.} \texttt{/z-spec:test} of this file as it stands, with
no extraction, at setsize~1 (\field{MAX\_OPERATIONS} 1000): \texttt{init},
\texttt{animate}, \texttt{cbc\_assertions}, \texttt{cbc\_deadlock} and the
model check pass, the last over 6\,496 states and 213\,008 transitions with no
state-schema violation and no deadlock. The coverage check fails, as it must:
seventeen operations never fire, for a structural reason. Every
\field{LcCf}\ldots operation except \field{LcCfRefuse}
(fourteen of them), \field{LcEnsureLineageOnly} and the two scenario
initialisations need two distinct sessions, which a carrier of size one cannot
supply. The run says nothing about the invariants, which are goals
(\S\ref{sec:lc-method}); it establishes that the file loads, that its
constants and initialisation are satisfiable, and that the state space of the
environment, session, Tier B and sweep operations is finite and deadlock-free
at that size.

\paragraph{Slices.} Operations are removed by name; a removed operation
leaves its variables at their initial values. \emph{lineage} keeps
\field{LcEnsureCreate}, \field{LcEnsureLineageOnly}, \field{LcCreateCli} and
\field{LcDeleteSession} and removes every other operation. \emph{start} is
\emph{lineage} without \field{LcEnsureCreate} and with
\field{LcSessionStart}, whose \field{srcFork} case is the registration.
\emph{purge} keeps the session-level operations, including
\field{LcPurgeSession}, and removes the claim-forked, claim, Tier B and
mission operations; the variant marked \emph{no \field{LcCorruptRoster}} also
removes that operation. \emph{claim} keeps only the \field{LcCf}\ldots
operations (with \field{LcCfLockReuse}), \field{LcOperatorClaim} and
\field{LcReleaseClaim}; \emph{claim+} adds \field{LcTierBDispatch},
\field{LcClearClosed} and \field{LcCloseLocked}. \emph{delete} is \emph{claim}
without \field{LcOperatorClaim}, \field{LcReleaseClaim}, \field{LcCfRefuse},
\field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, \field{LcCfAbort} and \field{LcCfExitNoRetry},
plus \field{LcDeleteSession}. \emph{sweep} is \emph{delete} with
\field{LcCfAbort}, \field{LcCloseUnlockedBegin} and \field{LcSweepWrite};
\emph{sweep+ensure} adds \field{LcEnsureCreate}, \field{LcCfRefuse},
\field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, \field{LcCfExitNoRetry} and
\field{LcCloseLocked}. \emph{verdict} keeps every \field{LcCf}\ldots
operation, \field{LcEnsureCreate}, \field{LcDeleteSession},
\field{LcCloseLocked} and both halves of the unlocked sweep.
\emph{tierb-delete}, \emph{tierb-purge} and \emph{tierb-reconcile} keep the
\field{LcCf}\ldots operations, \field{LcTierBDispatch}, the operator claim and
release, and one of \field{LcDeleteSession}, \field{LcPurgeSession} with
\field{LcClockSet}, or neither: the three ways in which a close can reach a
Tier B skeleton. \emph{claim+delete+close} keeps every operation except the
environment operations, \field{LcEnsureRefresh}, \field{LcEnsureLineageOnly},
\field{LcCreateCli}, \field{LcSessionStart} and \field{LcPurgeSession}. The
\emph{claim} slice, which has no \field{LcDeleteSession}, cannot exercise
\field{fixDeleteCloses}; that amendment is checked on \emph{delete},
\emph{sweep} and \emph{claim+delete+close}. \emph{start} replaces the
\field{LcEnsureCreate} of \emph{lineage} because the inputs of
\field{LcSessionStart} (five sources, a parent, a flag, a kind) make the
union of the two unfinishable: two runs of it were abandoned after five
minutes and are not in the table.

\paragraph{Results.} Sessions, missions, delegations (S/M/D) are the
cardinalities of the three given sets; INIT is the initialisation used
(\field{Init} the empty system, \field{LcInitPair} a child with a parent
holding an operator claim, \field{LcInitChain} a child, a parent and a
grandparent, so that the ancestor walk takes more than one hop).
``Switches'' lists those set to \field{ztrue}. States is the number of
states ProB analysed; Depth is the number of breadth-first levels it
reached. A row marked \emph{not exhausted} reached its state bound with
levels still open, so its Depth is that of the bound and not of the
space. Every row was run on the text of this file as committed, with a
\texttt{-mc} large enough not to bind (five million or more) except where
the row says \emph{not exhausted}. The rows \texttt{Fc2\_*},
\texttt{*\_wf\_*} and \texttt{L\_wf\_*} were run again after the goals for
\field{SweepComplete} and \field{WellFormed} were corrected to the schemas
of \S\ref{sec:lc-invariants}.

{\scriptsize
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l l l l X X l r r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Run} & \textbf{Check} & \textbf{INIT} & \textbf{S/M/D} & \textbf{Switches} & \textbf{Outcome} & \textbf{Slice} & \textbf{States} & \textbf{Depth} \\
\midrule
''' + table + r'''
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
}

\paragraph{Mutants.}
\label{sec:lc-mutants}
An invariant is only evidence if a broken operation can fail it. The
operations are run with every switch their invariant needs on, and one
amended operation is broken, by the edit named in the table; the goal is the
invariant's, and each mutant is killed except where the row says otherwise.
\texttt{MutA\_claimed} and \texttt{MutB\_refuse} are the two mutants of the
\field{ReconcileOnExit} ghost of the previous revision, re-run: the shortest
trace of the first is C4, that of the second C1. Each new amendment has a mutant:
\field{fixOrigin} three (\texttt{F1D\_mut}, \texttt{F1R\_mut},
\texttt{F1P\_mut}, the origin filter removed from \field{LcDeleteSession},
\field{LcCfReconcileFresh} and \field{LcPurgeSession}),
\field{fixSessionStart} two (\texttt{S\_lin\_mutC}, \texttt{S\_lin\_mutR}: the
compact, or the resume, source routed to the replacing create),
\field{fixCas} one (\texttt{MutCasFresh}: the reconcile close written without
the open test), \field{fixReuseLocks} one (\texttt{MutLockReuse}: the locks
taken, \field{cfH} not set), and the scope of \field{fixSupersede} two
(\texttt{MutSupClaimed}: supersede applied in the claimed case, which closes a
live binding; \texttt{MutSupReuse}: supersede removed from the resume path).

{\scriptsize
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l l l l X X l r r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Run} & \textbf{Check} & \textbf{INIT} & \textbf{S/M/D} & \textbf{Switches} & \textbf{Outcome} & \textbf{Slice} & \textbf{States} & \textbf{Depth} \\
\midrule
''' + mut + r'''
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
}

\noindent \texttt{MutSupReuse} \emph{survives}, and the survival is a finding.
The resume path of the reconcile carries the supersede clause (it closes the
fork skeleton the child's binding names when that is not the record's), and
the leader asked that the model confirm it. It cannot: with every amendment on,
no reachable state has a pending record, a child with no claim and a binding
that names an open fork skeleton other than the record's (\texttt{Reach\_all}, '''+S('Reach_all')+r''' states, all
visited, no state), so the clause never fires, and removing it changes no
invariant. Without \field{fixSupersede} on the fresh path such a state is
reachable (\texttt{Reach\_nosup}, depth '''+D('Reach_nosup')+r'''), which is why the clause is
needed there and only there. The resume-path clause is therefore redundant given the
fresh-path clause and the closes of C11; it is kept in the schema, since it is
what the design says, and the claim that it is verified is withdrawn. The code
may keep or drop it.

\paragraph{Verdicts.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{LineageStable} holds. With \field{fixDeleteOrder}, at three
    sessions, all ''' + S(need('L_lin_order', 'full')) + r''' states of the \emph{lineage} slice are
    visited with no counterexample (\texttt{L\_lin\_order}); with both lineage
    amendments, ''' + S(need('L_lin_all', 'full')) + r''' states (\texttt{L\_lin\_all}). Without it, the
    shortest counterexample is C2. \field{fixCycleCheck} is not needed for it.
    With \field{SessionStart} in the machine (\emph{start} slice) it holds
    exactly when \field{fixSessionStart} is on: ''' + S(need('S_lin_on', 'full')) + r''' states
    visited (\texttt{S\_lin\_on}); off, the counterexample is C13 in
    ''' + D(need('S_lin_off', 'cex')) + r''' steps (\texttt{S\_lin\_off}).
  \item \textbf{Acyclic}, in the strong form, holds with \field{fixCycleCheck}
    alone: ''' + S(need('L_acyc_cycle', 'full')) + r''' states visited (\texttt{L\_acyc\_cycle}), and ''' + S(need('L_acyc_all', 'full')) + r''' with both
    lineage amendments; with \field{SessionStart} added it holds
    (\texttt{S\_acyc\_on}, ''' + S(need('S_acyc_on', 'full')) + r''' states) and fails without the cycle check
    (\texttt{S\_acyc\_nocycle}). Without it the counterexample is C3: one step with
    \field{--parent-gone} (a session its own parent) and six without it. The walk of \S2.3.1 may
    therefore keep its visited set as a defence only; but see N4 of
    \S\ref{sec:lc-limits}.
  \item \textbf{NoLiveSessionPurged} holds with \field{fixStaleLive} and
    \field{fixCorruptPurge}, exhaustively at one session (''' + S(need('P1_all', 'full')) + r''' states) and
    bounded at two and three sessions (40\,000 states, not exhausted).
    Each amendment alone leaves the other's counterexample
    (\texttt{P\_stalelive}, \texttt{P\_corrupt}).
  \item \textbf{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}, for skeletons of kind \field{dkFork},
    holds in its literal form with \field{fixDeleteCloses},
    \field{fixSupersede} and \field{fixReleaseCloses}, on the assumption
    \field{assumeNoTierBOverFork}: ''' + S(need('Fa_orph_all', 'full')) + r''' states of the
    \emph{claim} slice (''' + S(need('Fa_orph_d3', 'full')) + r''' at three delegations, depth ''' + D('Fa_orph_d3') + r'''),
    ''' + S(need('C9_all', 'full')) + r''' of \emph{claim+}, and ''' + S(need('Fb2_del', 'full')) + r''' of the \emph{delete} slice,
    exhaustively; and in the full two-session and three-session machines no
    counterexample in the bounded runs, which are not exhaustive. Each of the
    three is necessary where a run isolates it: \texttt{Fb2\_w},
    \texttt{Fa\_orph\_norel} (C11), \texttt{C9\_nosup} (C9). With the assumption off it fails
    (\texttt{C12\_open}, C12), and no amendment of this model closes that.
    With \field{fixRefuseReconciles} and \field{fixInertBinding} the exit
    postcondition \field{ReconcileOnExit} holds as well (''' + S(need('Fa_all', 'full')) + r''' states with the
    two switches, ''' + S(need('Fa_leak_all', 'full')) + r''' with all fourteen, all visited).
    \field{SweepComplete} holds with \field{fixDeleteCloses} and
    \field{fixPostCheck} (''' + S(need('Fc2_both', 'full')) + r''' states of the \emph{sweep} slice, all
    visited), stated of the skeletons the sweep has not yet written.
  \item \textbf{NoForeignAbort} holds with \field{fixOrigin}: all states of
    the three Tier B slices are visited (''' + S(need('F1D_on', 'full')) + r''', ''' + S(need('F1P_on', 'full')) + r''' and ''' + S(need('F1R_on', 'full')) + r''' states),
    and fails without it in four, five and five steps (\texttt{F1D\_off},
    \texttt{F1P\_off}, \texttt{F1R\_off}): through \field{deleteFiles}, through a
    purge, and through the supersede close of a reconcile.
  \item \textbf{NoVerdictOverwrite} holds with \field{fixCas}: ''' + S(need('Fv_on', 'full')) + r''' states of
    the \emph{sweep} slice, all visited, and no counterexample in the first
    300\,000 of \emph{verdict}; it fails without it in ''' + D(need('Fv_off', 'cex')) + r''' steps
    (\texttt{Fv\_off}), the trace of C14.
  \item \textbf{LockedWrites} holds with \field{fixReuseLocks} (''' + S(need('Fa_lockw_all', 'full')) + r''' states
    of \emph{claim}, all visited) and fails without it in ''' + D(need('Fa_lockw_off', 'cex')) + r''' steps
    (\texttt{Fa\_lockw\_off}), the trace of C15.
  \item \textbf{LiveSpared} holds: ''' + S(need('Fa_live_all', 'full')) + r''' states of \emph{claim}, all visited,
    and ''' + S(need('C9_live_all', 'full')) + r''' of \emph{claim+}.
  \item \textbf{WellFormed} holds in every run in which it is checked,
    including the five new components (\texttt{L\_wf\_all}, \texttt{S\_wf\_on},
    \texttt{P1\_wf}, \texttt{Fa\_wf\_all}, \texttt{C9\_wf\_all}).
  \item \textbf{No invariant is left with an open counterexample except
    NoOrphanOpenSkeleton with the assumption off (C12).} The limit
    otherwise is coverage, not a counterexample: the full
    \field{claim-forked} machine is exhausted only slice by slice.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Multi-hop ancestor walk.} The rows with \field{LcInitChain} are
the only ones in which the walk of \S2.3.1 takes more than one hop. The
\emph{claim+delete+close} rows are bounded at 40\,000 states and the
\emph{claim} rows at 200\,000; none is exhaustive at three sessions, and
nothing in this document claims it. The \emph{claim+delete+close} rows at two
sessions are bounded at 200\,000 states and reach a depth of eight, which is
the depth of the first propagation and not of a second one; the second
propagations of C9 and C11 are exercised by the exhaustive \emph{claim} and
\emph{claim+} rows.


'''
s = s[:a] + new + s[b:]
open(P, 'w').write(s)
print('written')

Each first closes the skeleton the record names (fork kind, owned by the session, compare-and-set on verdict open).
- With the switch off, `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton` fails (`C12_off`, 60,514 states, depth 11): complete a propagation, then a Tier B dispatch over the fork binding.
- With it on and no assumption, it holds over all 257,269 states of the claim+ slice, which includes Tier B over fork, operator claim, mission close and clearing.
- A complete record is never resumable, since `LcCfReconcileReuse` now requires the child not be in `pendDone`.
- "Live" now means the child's claim is for the skeleton's mission, whatever the binding names, for a complete record. An incomplete record is live only if the binding also names it, as in C4. A live record is kept and marked complete.
- The `leaked` and `liveAborted` ghosts use the same notion of live.
- Re-checked with the switch on, all holding: `ReconcileOnExit`, `SweepComplete`, `LiveSpared`, `LockedWrites`, `NoForeignAbort`, and `WellFormed` (now including `pendDone`).
- Mutants killed: the record removed at finish (`MutFinishRec`, `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton` counterexample) and a complete record judged live by the binding alone (`MutLiveNoDone`, `LiveSpared` counterexample). The round-1 mutants were re-run and all die. `MutA_claimed` had silently stopped mutating after the edit; I re-pointed it at the new text and it dies again.

**Reuse supersede clause, ruled keep as defensive:** the ledger and verification now say it is unexercised, not verified. `Reach_all` visited all 257,269 states and found none with a record, no claim and another open fork binding. `Reach_nosup` (supersede off, record not durable) reaches that state; `Reach_nosup_dur` does not.

**Two other results to know about:**
- `MutReuseDone` (a complete record treated as resumable) survives. Every operation that takes the claim away closes the skeleton and removes the record, so the guard is defensive. Your instruction was to model the complete/crashed distinction and check it; it is checked in the claimed case by `MutLiveNoDone`, not by this guard.
- With the durable record, `fixReleaseCloses` and `fixSupersede` are no longer needed for `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton`. `Fa_orph_norel_dur` and `C9_nosup_dur` hold, while the same rows with the switch off are counterexamples. I kept both switches and recorded this in the ledger; whether the code keeps them is your call.

**Verification:** I re-ran all 96 rows on the round-2 model.
- The bounded full-machine rows (200,000, 40,000 and 200,000 states) found no counterexample but are not exhaustive.
- The `/z-spec:test` run at setsize 1 gives the same figures as before: 6,496 states, 213,008 transitions, 5 of 6 checks. Coverage fails by design because 17 operations need two sessions.

**Design sections that must change, beyond the round-1 list:**
- The §5 point 2 item 5 sentences "removed as the last step of a successful write" and "the record is then overwritten or removed".
- The record format needs a stage field (complete or not).
- `ClearMissionBindings` (`internal/mission/active.go`:907-957) must also close and remove the record-named skeleton when it clears a claim. That is a change to an existing Claude Code path.
- `mission release` and `deleteFiles` close the record-named skeleton before removing the record.
- The "record does not parse" row of the exit-status table now applies for as long as the claim lasts.
- The Tier B dispatch path is unchanged.

## 1. Reproduction (my own runs on commit e905e0c, using the worker's x2.sh slicer and goals; counts equal the table)

| Row | Outcome | States |
|---|---|---|
| C12_off (NoOrphan, claim+ slice) | counterexample | 60514 |
| C12_on / C9_all (NoOrphan, claim+ slice) | holds, all visited | 257269 |
| F1D_off / F1P_off / F1R_off (NoForeignAbort) | counterexample | 84 / 337 / 191 |

| S_lin_on and S_acyc_on | hold, all visited | 1025 each |
| Fv_off / Fv2_off (NoVerdictOverwrite) | counterexample | 1198 / 5838 |

| Fv2_on | bounded, no counterexample | 300000 |

| Fa_lockw_all | holds, all visited | 16601 |
| Fa_live_all (LiveSpared) | holds, all visited | 16601 |
| Fa_orph_all | holds, all visited | 16601 |

- The 257,269-state NoOrphanOpenSkeleton row is reproduced.
- I checked every row in the lifecycle spec against the worker's raw outputs in .tmp/lc3/r6: 96 rows, 2 mismatches (see B1).
- fixes off versus on behave as claimed for C12, F1, F3, F10 and F9.

## 2. My own mutants of the durable record (claim+ slice, all fifteen switches on, 2/2/2)

| Mutant | Goal | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MyFinishRm (Finish removes the record, the old behaviour) | NoOrphan | killed, 60514 states (C12 returns) |
| MyRelNoClose (release removes the record but closes nothing) | NoOrphan | killed, 48840 states |
| MyReuseComplete (a complete record treated as resumable; guard `c ∉ pendDone` dropped) | NoOrphan and LiveSpared | survives, 257269 states, all visited |
| MyRelKeepRec (release closes but leaves the record) | NoOrphan and LiveSpared | survives, 318189 states |
| MyRefuseDropRec | – | invalid: I conjoined an unsatisfiable term, so the transition was merely disabled; discard |

- **MyReuseComplete** survives for the reason the worker states. The combination "complete record, no claim, open skeleton, open mission" is unreachable, because every claim-removing path also closes and unnames. The `pendDone` guard in LcCfReconcileReuse is therefore defensive and unverified, as lifecycle.tex:2480-2488 says.
- **MyRelKeepRec** shows that "release also removes the record" is unchecked. Keeping the record is harmless in the model, because a closed skeleton is not resumable. Record clearance on release is hygiene, not an invariant, and the text should not describe it as verified (non-blocking, N3 below).

## 3. Fidelity

### 2.7 What the lifecycle model proves, and how far (round 9)

`docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex` checks each invariant as the negation of a
goal given to ProB, on a slice of the machine (the operations that can affect
that invariant), at the instance named. "Exhaustive" below means ProB visited
every reachable state of that slice and found no counterexample; "bounded"
means it stopped at a state limit with levels still open and found none in the
states it saw. The instance is two missions and two delegations, and two
sessions for the `claim-forked` slices and three for the lineage and purge
slices, unless stated. Time takes three values with a threshold of one, and
the participant kinds are three. A claim that an invariant holds is a claim
about the slice and instance in the table, and nothing wider.

| Invariant | Exhaustive | Bounded |
|---|---|---|
| `LineageStable` (with `fixDeleteOrder`, `fixSessionStart`) | lineage slice, three sessions (21,953 states); start slice (1,025) | none |
| `Acyclic` (strong form, every sidecar; `fixCycleCheck`) | lineage slice, three sessions (15,029); start slice (1,025) | none; but see N4 below |
| `NoLiveSessionPurged` (`fixStaleLive`, `fixCorruptPurge`) | one session (817) | two and three sessions (40,000 states, not exhausted) |
| `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton`, fork skeletons (`fixDurableName`) | claim slice (16,601; 106,881 at three delegations); claim+ slice, which includes a Tier B dispatch over a completed fork claim, the operator claim, the mission close and the close-time clearing (257,269); delete slice (4,877) | claim+delete+close, two sessions (200,000 states, depth 8) and three (40,000, depth 5); claim, three sessions (200,000, depth 12) |
| `ReconcileOnExit` | claim slice (16,601); claim+ (257,269) | the same full-machine runs |
| `SweepComplete` (`fixDeleteCloses`, `fixPostCheck`) | sweep slice (37,025) | the same full-machine runs |
| `NoForeignAbort` (`fixOrigin`) | the three Tier B slices (11,073; 33,217; 2,013) | the same full-machine runs |
| `NoVerdictOverwrite` (`fixCas`) | sweep slice (19,697) | verdict slice (300,000 states); full-machine runs |
| `LiveSpared` | claim slice (16,601); claim+ (257,269) | full-machine runs |
| `LockedWrites` (a condition of the model's lock assumption, not an invariant of the design; `fixReuseLocks`) | claim slice (16,601) | full-machine runs |
| `WellFormed` (the model's own well-formedness) | every run in which it is checked | the three-session full-machine run |

No invariant has an open counterexample. The limit is coverage: the full
`claim-forked` machine, with the deletes, purges and closes interleaved, is
exhausted only slice by slice, and the second propagations of C9 and C11 are
exercised by the exhaustive claim and claim+ slices, not by the bounded
full-machine rows. The three-session rows exercise the multi-hop ancestor walk
and are bounded at 40,000 and 200,000 states. A switch is shown necessary
where a run isolates it (the ledger's rows); the amendments that the durable
record makes redundant for `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton` (the binding-named close at
release, `fixSupersede`) are labelled defensive in §5 point 2 item 5, and
the resume path's supersede clause and the guard that a complete record is
never resumed are unexercised and unverified (`MutSupReuse`, `MutReuseDone`
survive).

**Limits the design relies on.** The model's operations are atomic except
where a process can die or a removal can fail, so it cannot show any race. The
limits the spec states and where this design meets them: N2, `deleteFiles`
step 1 short-circuits (§2.1.1); N3, `Store.Close`'s sweep is best-effort and a
skeleton with no `record.yaml` refuses `Abandon` (§5 point 2 item 5); N4,

mandatory (§2.1.1 rule 3, §2.3.1); N5, every close but the sweep writes
`aborted` (§5 point 2 item 5); N7, the child's claim is two files (§5 point 2
item 1); N8, a live Claude Code session whose roster does not parse and has no
`last-seen` is still purged (§2.1.1); N9 and N17, the Tier B dispatch is one
atomic step and three of its paths are not represented (§5 point 2 item 5);
N10, the compare-and-set is taken to be atomic as the delegation lock is; N11,
a `SessionStart` for a roster that does not parse is a no-op (§2.1.1); N12,
the owner test of the origin filter is vacuous in the model, whose only
writers of a binding are the session itself; N13, the dispatch-pending
entries `ClearMissionBindings` clears and the MCP path that calls it are not
represented; N15, the record's stage is one bit and a record that no longer

`release` and the close-time clearing is an implementation constraint (§5
point 2 item 5); N18, that a release removes the record is hygiene and the
`pendDone` guard of the resume path is defensive (§5 point 2 item 5). The
read phase and the start of the write phase are one step in the model, so the
window in which the witness releases its claim between them is accepted and
not examined.

VERDICT: REJECT, narrowly (m-2026-10-23-005, round 1 of 2). One blocking finding (B1, a few lines), plus wording fixes (W1-W5). Every other contract criterion holds against the spec and source. After B1 and W1-W5 I would accept without another review round.

## (1) Ledger amendments and the consequences list

I read the spec's ledger (C10-C15), verification verdicts, consequences list and limits (N1-N18) against the design.

- **Origin discriminator (C10, `fixOrigin`): exact.**
  - Design 738-762 matches spec 2043-2063: kind is the skeleton's `BoundVia` (new value `claim_forked`), owner is `ParentSession`, and every close applies the test.
  - A Tier B binding is cleared and its skeleton left open (deleteFiles step 1, release, close-time clearing).
- **Durable record with stage (C12, `fixDurableName`): exact.**
  - Design 2202-2235 and 2236-2280. The record carries stage and store root and is not removed at finish. It is removed only by release, `ClearMissionBindings` and `deleteFiles`, each after closing the fork skeleton it names.
  - A complete record is never resumable. Live means the child's claim is for the skeleton's mission, and an incomplete record also needs the binding to name it. This matches spec 2085-2103.
  - The "record does not parse" row applies for the claim's lifetime (2228-2232, 2168).
  - The superseded sentences are quoted only as superseded (lines 253-266, 2212, DESIGN.md item 28).
- **Release and close-time clearing (C11/C12/N16): exact.**
  - Design 2312-2354. Sequence is close, unname, clear, under the child's dispatch-pending lock, restructured to take the lock once because it is not reentrant.
  - The existing code paths cited are correct: `runMissionRelease` takes the lock only for `ClearDispatchPending`, and `ClearMissionBindings` only for `ConsumeDispatchPending`. The independent claim and binding tests in `ClearMissionBindings` are quoted accurately.
  - I checked for deadlock: `clearClosedSessionBindings` and the MCP path call `ClearMissionBindings` after `Close` returns, so the dispatch lock does not nest inside a held mission lock.
- **CAS everywhere including the sweep (C14): exact.** Design 2355-2377: the load and write happen under the skeleton's delegation lock, and the sweep takes each skeleton's delegation lock in both branches, in mission-then-delegation order, using `s.root` as `DisclaimDelegation` does (`store.go:1589`).
- **Reuse locks (C15): exact.** Write-phase steps 5-7 (2071-2098) and the status row: the resume path takes the step-5 locks and re-reads the mission before writing.
- **`fixSupersede` scope (C9): exact.** Fresh and resume paths only, never on a refusal or the claimed case. The resume clause is labelled defensive and unexercised (`MutSupReuse`).
- **SessionStart through Ensure (C13): exact for the spec's operation.** Every source, without touch, and sources other than fork pass the recorded parent (design 792-817, 1363-1377, §5 point 3). But see B1.
- **C1-C9 and N2/N4/N5: unchanged and still exact** (spot-checked `LcCfRefuse`, `LcCfReconcileClaimed`/`Reuse`, `LcDeleteSession`).

## (2) B2, review items, earlier wording

- **B2: closed.**
  - The record stores `resolve.StoreRepoRoot()` (`resolve.go:~729`), and every close uses the recorded root.
  - "Gone" is concluded only from a recorded, resolvable root whose mission directory is absent.
  - An empty, absent or unresolvable root is a step-1 failure with the roster kept, and "do not retry" in a reconcile.
  - The cross-working-directory test is required (design 763-787).
- **Code-reviewer items: closed.**
  - DESIGN.md decision point 3 gets `--touch`, the SessionStart wiring with the parentGone retry, and the new write order with the conditional reuse rule.
  - Rule 4: `ensure --touch` on a roster that fails to load writes nothing and exits non-zero, with a test (design 622-637; spec `LcEnsureRefresh` guard).
- **F4: closed.**
  - Rows for the binding I/O errors, the `ParentOf` error, the `ReadDelegationBinding` error, record-removal failure and cleanup-close failure.
  - A mission-closed witness is "witness refused". A Claude Code column. `errors.As` is consulted before the prefix test (`main.go:51-71`, `85-100`, citations verified).
- **F5/F8: closed.**
  - The deny list is derived from the harness list, with vocabulary, an `@` pattern and a whole-word `CLAUDE.md` strip.
  - The persona-injection sentence is enumerated at guide lines 19-20.
  - The harness-name test scans `cmd/ethos`, `internal/doctor` and `cmd/validate-content` with one allowlisted literal. The `uninstall.go:37-49` and `doctor.go:198` hits are cited correctly, and the non-harness literals are escalated rather than allowlisted.
- **F7: closed.**
  - (a) A `last-seen` read error is "not stale, warn" on every path.
  - (b) `Store.Purge` has no production caller and `PurgeTombstoned` refuses an unreadable roster without `--force` (`store.go:469-503`).
  - (c) The `ethos serve` aging claim is deleted.
- **F12: closed** (design 1996-2009). The temp-name leftovers (`last-seen.*.tmp`, `claim-forked-pending.*.tmp`, `active.go:289`) are removed by `deleteFiles`.
- **§2.7: accurate.** The exhaustive and bounded table matches the spec's verdict figures I spot-checked: 817, 21,953, 257,269 and 16,601 states.
- **My earlier wording items: closed.** A refusal never resumes (1981-1984), and the §2.1.1 purge opening points to the bullets (849-854).

## (3) Superseded text

I grepped the superseded phrases. Every remaining occurrence is a quotation marked as superseded, in the header supersession list (253-266) or a dated round note. None is stated as current. DESIGN.md item 22's "does not resume" wording carries its "round 9 withdraws" marker.

## (4) The leader-accepted calls

Consistent, with the notes in W1 and W3.
- **Mission-closed witness as "witness refused".** Applied identically in the table (2166), write-phase step 6 (2088), the post-check (1921) and in-process cleanup (2405). State effect is identical to the spec's `LcCfExitNoRetry`.
- **F8 scan scope.** One allowlisted literal, with non-harness literals escalated.
- **A binding with no record is Tier B.** Justified: the binding carries neither a kind nor a store root, so the design closes on the record alone. The spec's step 1 also closes a fork skeleton only the binding names. The design says `Fa_orph_norel_dur` holds without that close, which supports it, and §2.7 labels it defensive.

## Findings

### B1 (blocking): the SessionStart refresh is incomplete, and `Ensure` is not specified to do it

- The leader added "update the primary participant to the current `CLAUDE_PID` on an existing roster" (design 822-839, 1373-1377, DESIGN.md item 30).
  - The reason given is right: a resumed session would keep a dead primary id and be purged while live.
- But `CreateInCheckout` rewrote more on every `SessionStart`: `Repo`, `Checkout` and `Host` (`store.go:82-93`, `session_start.go:~189-193`).
  - `Checkout` is the DES-058 live-audit-zone binding, which the purge and probe logic read (`store.go:22-27` roster doc).
  - A session resumed from a different checkout under create-if-absent would keep the old `Checkout`.
  - It is the same regression class, only less likely.
- Also, nothing in §5 point 1 says `Ensure` does the refresh.
  - The `Ensure(sessionID, root, primary, repo, checkout, host, parentSession, parentGone, touch)` signature at 1818 has no refresh mode or argument.
  - Rules 1-4 of §2.1.1 say an existing roster is changed only by `--touch`.
  - The refresh appears only in §2.1.1's last bullet and §2.5.
- Fix:
  1. Extend the refresh to `Repo`, `Checkout` and `Host` as well as the primary id, or state the limit explicitly.
  2. Add the refresh as a named argument or mode of `Ensure` in §5 point 1 and in §2.1.1's rule list, so the plugin and CLI `ensure` do not get it.
  3. Extend the required test to assert the other roster fields.

### Wording

- **W1.** The mission-closed witness maps to "witness refused", but the spec labels that exit `LcCfExitNoRetry`, which the spec's C15 prose also calls "do not retry".
  - The design never names `LcCfExitNoRetry` or states that the label deliberately differs.
  - Add one sentence at the table row (2166) and in §2.7's limits: the state effect is identical, and the leader chose to try the next ancestor (cost: a closed-mission witness chain costs one reconcile and one consumed counter slot per ancestor).
- **W2.** DESIGN.md:12287 says the spec adds "five more fix switches". It added six (`fixOrigin`, `fixReleaseCloses`, `fixDurableName`, `fixSessionStart`, `fixCas`, `fixReuseLocks`), taking nine to fifteen, as the same paragraph and the design header say.
- **W3.** `TestHarnessNamesOnlyInList` (design 2675-2740): as specified, the scan will fail on day one for the non-harness hits it lists (the COO handle `"claude"`, `claude-md`, `.claude/skills`), and the allowlist is not to grow. State plainly that the test stays red until the leader's ruling on those hits. It is already said in prose, but the "proves none was missed" claim reads as if the test is passable as written.
- **W4.** Design 2013-2016: the table names the Claude Code `SessionStart` hook as running `claim-forked`, but §5 point 3 and §2.5 say the hook runs `Ensure` then `claim-forked`. Say in the table column heading that the `Ensure` step's own failures are separate: they leave no pointer, §2.5.
- **W5.** §2.7 table row for `WellFormed` lists "the three-session full-machine run" as bounded. The spec says only "every run in which it is checked". Match the spec's wording.

**Checked and correct (no finding):**
- **Citations:** every file:line reference on an added line matches the source. That covers `main.go`, `pretooluse_dispatch.go`, `active.go`, `delegation.go`, mission and session `store.go`, `mission.go`, `mcp/mission_tools.go`, `session_start.go`, `resolve.go:729`, `enable.go`, `deposit.go`, `uninstall.go`, `doctor.go` and `validate-content/main.go`.
- **State counts:** every count in the §2.7 table and in DESIGN.md's round 9 limits paragraph matches the spec's run table.
- **Fix switches:** the spec has fifteen.
- **Spelled-out commands:** all three spelled-out plugin `ensure` commands carry `--touch` (design doc lines 430-431, 538, 558-559), and `--parent-gone` is used only together with `--parent-session`.
- **New BoundVia value:** it is `claim_forked` everywhere, consistent with spec line 2600.

## Critical (90-100)

**1. Primary-participant refresh contradicts "changes nothing" (confidence 92)**
- Commit cbb1b6a added this at design doc lines 822-839: the SessionStart `Ensure` call updates an existing roster's primary participant to the current `CLAUDE_PID`. Older text in the same doc was not updated:
  - Line 804-806: "for a session that has a roster it changes nothing" (same bullet as the new rule).
  - Lines 815-817: the required test says resume/compact SessionStart against a fork with a roster and sidecar "change neither". The roster's primary participant now changes.
  - Lines 1025-1026: "a `SessionStart` with `source: "fork"` against a roster that already has lineage changes nothing."
  - §5 point 1 (lines 1818-1829): the `Store.Ensure(...)` signature and the four rules have no parameter or rule for the refresh. Without `touch`, an existing roster is left untouched, yet line 834 says OpenCode and the CLI "do not pass this refresh", which implies a caller-controlled input.
  - §5 point 3 (lines 2471-2477) omits the refresh from the SessionStart write-set.
- Fix:
  - Lines 805, 815-817 and 1025-1026: change them to "changes nothing except the primary participant, which is set to the current `CLAUDE_PID`". The required tests should assert that the `parent-session` sidecar, `last-seen` and lineage are unchanged, not the whole roster.
  - §5 point 1: add the refresh input to the `Store.Ensure` signature and rules (for example a `refreshPrimary` argument), and state that only the SessionStart hook passes it.
  - §5 point 3: mention the refresh.

**2. Design and spec give different statuses for a mission found closed on the resume path (confidence 90)**
- Design doc line 2088 (write phase step 6) and the "witness refused" row at line 2166 say this exits "witness refused". So do the header note at line 235 and DESIGN.md item (31).
- Spec line 2634-2635 (C15 consequence) says it "exits 'do not retry'".
- Design doc line 203 and DESIGN.md say the spec wins where the two disagree, so the design as written is overridden on this point.
- Fix: amend the spec's C15 bullet to "witness refused", matching round 9 finding (c). Otherwise, state explicitly in the design doc and DESIGN.md (31) that this is a deliberate departure from the spec.

## Important (80-89)

**3. DESIGN.md Decision point 3 says a non-resumable record is always closed (confidence 85)**
- DESIGN.md, Decision point 3, "Round 9 order" paragraph (around new line 12437) ends: "in every other case it closes the skeleton and removes the record first."
- That is false for the refusal and claimed cases with a live record. There the record is kept and marked complete: DESIGN.md item (28) ("A refusal keeps a live record"), design doc lines 1984-1985 and 2244-2248, and the spec's `LcCfRefuse` / `LcCfReconcileClaimed`.
- Fix: "otherwise, a live record (refusal or already-claimed case) is kept and marked complete, and any other record has its skeleton closed and is removed before a fresh write."

**4. DESIGN.md item 22 points to the wrong round 9 item (confidence 85)**
- DESIGN.md item (22) (around new line 12256) says the `errors.As` mapping is "consulted before the prefix test of `isUsageError` (round 9, item 31)".
- Item (31) does not mention `errors.As`. That rule is in item (33): "the typed-status `errors.As` mapping runs before the prefix test at `main.go:85-100`".
- Fix: change "item 31" to "item 33".

**5. "Removed only by" release, clearing and deleteFiles is overstated (confidence 80)**
- Design doc line 2219-2224 says the `claim-forked-pending` record is "removed **only** by `mission release`, by the close-time clearing of the claim, and by `deleteFiles`". The header note (lines 213-215) and DESIGN.md item (28) say the same.
- The same item 5 also removes records in other places:
  - The refusal and claimed-case reconcile removes a record that is not live (line 2249).
  - The fresh path removes the record (line 2279).
  - In-process cleanup removes the record (line 2404).
- The spec's wording (line 2089) has the same overstatement, but its own `LcCfRefuse` and `LcCfReconcileFresh` also remove records.
- Fix: "a live record (one naming the skeleton of the child's current fork claim) is removed only by `mission release`, the close-time clearing, or `deleteFiles`; a record that is not live is closed and removed by the next reconcile or by in-process cleanup." Apply the same wording at lines 213-215 and DESIGN.md (28).
