I read the worktree only with git log, git diff, git show and git archive, and wrote nothing there. The sandbox is ~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/cr26-classes/, with git-archive copies of HEAD (334e663), main (cbc1e60) and prev (2046342), each git-inited and built. Every run used HOME=<sandbox>/home, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>, TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1. The dry runs printed targets under `<sandbox>/sc/...` before I ran anything with --apply.

## (a) Main against HEAD, run with the real binaries
- **Existing clone with a commit, origin `https://example.invalid/other.git`, `add-bundle --apply --name b https://example.invalid/o/b.git`:** HEAD and main give the same result. Both print "Adding existing repo at '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b' to the index", exit 0, stage `A .gitmodules` and `A .punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b`, and write `url = https://example.invalid/o/b.git`.
- **Existing clone with no commit:** HEAD and main give the same result. Both print `fatal: '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b' does not have a commit checked out` and `ethos: running git submodule add ...: exit status 128`, exit 1, and stage nothing.
- **Clone made from `../src`, then `add-bundle --apply --name b ../src`:** HEAD and main both adopt it and exit 0. The previous commit 2046342 refused it: "has origin .../../../src, not ../src". The fix works.

## (b) isOwnGitRepo
Each case that used to return a silent (false, nil) now returns an error, and checkBundleDestination wraps it with %w. A timeout still comes back as ErrTimeout, and `IsNotARepo` on the trimmed stderr still matches. Nothing to report.

## (d) The new tests fail against the defect
I copied HEAD's add_bundle_precheck_test.go into the 2046342 tree and ran it there:
- **`TestAddBundleHandsAnExistingCloneToGit`:** both subtests fail with `"--version\n-C\n-C\n-C\n-C\n" does not contain "submodule"`.
- **`TestIsOwnGitRepoReportsFailures/a_failure_with_no_stderr_names_the_exit`:** fails with `"git rev-parse --show-toplevel: " does not contain "exit status 3"`.
- **`TestIsOwnGitRepoReportsFailures/a_top_level_that_cannot_be_examined`:** fails with `Expected error with "file does not exist" in chain but got nil`.
- **`TestAddBundleLeavesToGitWhatGitAccepts/pre-cloned_submodule_path`:** fails.

On HEAD, `go vet ./cmd/ethos` is clean and `go test -count=1 ./cmd/ethos` passes.

## (c) The DES-079 paragraph and the CHANGELOG entry are true
- "An existing clone is passed to `git submodule add` whatever its `origin` ... git adopts it if it has a commit checked out and otherwise refuses it with its own message" matches what git 2.43 did above.
- "A failed or timed-out probe ... is reported as that failure" matches the code.
- The CHANGELOG entry at lines 303-307 matches the code.
- The walkedPast comment in internal/resolve/resolve.go:1081-1086 matches the loop at 1094-1109.

## Finding

**cmd/ethos/add_bundle_precheck_test.go:351-353 (in HEAD's file), bar (c), minor.** The comment on the new test says the two fixtures "are clones of exactly the URL given". The relative-URL fixture (`remote add origin /somewhere/else/src`, then `runAddBundle(t, "../src")`) is not.
- **Why it is false:** the superproject in that test has no remote, so git resolves `../src` to `<parent of repo>/src`. `/somewhere/else/src` is a different repository.
- **What the code does:** HEAD hands the fixture to `git submodule add` (the log contains "submodule"), and 2046342 refuses it. Neither fact shows the fixture is a clone of `../src`.
- **Fix, either one:** set the fixture's origin to `filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(repo), "src")`, or change the comment to "whatever its origin, even one that does not match the URL given".

- team_bundle.go:681: an empty stderr gives a trailing separator, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel: exit status 3: `. The `%s` of `ee.Error()` also drops `*exec.ExitError` from the error chain.
- add_bundle_precheck_test.go:373, insteadOf subtest: the `url.ssh://...insteadOf` config is set in the superproject `repo`, which `dest` never reads. The test only works because origin is set to the ssh URL directly, so the config line does nothing.
- add_bundle_precheck_test.go:182-185: the comment says the clone is "handed to git submodule add, which adopts it". The fixture has no commit, so git refuses it. The comment also lists "(an insteadOf rewrite, a relative URL)", but those cases are in the other test.
- resolve.go:1088-1090: walkedPast returns nil when `os.Stat(top)` fails, even if the walk would reach the gitDir directory. The comment does not mention this case. `top` comes from a successful rev-parse, so it can only happen in a race.
- loggedGit (outside this range): it logs `$1` after skipping `-c`, so calls made with `git -C dir ...` are logged as `-C`, not their subcommand. That weakens `assertNoNetwork` for those calls.

Every other probe gives the same result on HEAD and main, or HEAD is better. No error is dropped in `checkBundleDestination` or `isOwnGitRepo`. No path I tried made git stage something other than a submodule while HEAD reported success.

**How I tested.** The sandbox is `~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/sfh26-classes/`.
- I made `git archive` copies of 334e663 and cbc1e60 in `src-head/` and `src-main/`, ran `git init` in each, and built `bin/ethos-head` and `bin/ethos-main`. Git is 2.43.0.
- Every probe ran under `env -i` with its own HOME, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>` and `TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp`. GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR were never set.
- I did the dry run first; both binaries put their targets inside the sandbox.
- The scripts are `scripts/lib.sh`, `p00-dry.sh`, `p01-cases.sh` and `p02-more.sh`.
- Each case is a fresh superproject at `probes/<case>-<bin>/p`, running `ethos team add-bundle <local upstream> --name b --apply`. I then recorded `git ls-files -s`, `.gitmodules` and `git submodule status`.
- I ran nothing against the real repo or its worktrees.

## Finding 1 — (a) regression against main, and (c) a false CHANGELOG sentence

**Where:** `cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go:658` (the refusal), using `isOwnGitRepo` at `:668`–`:690`. The test is `return os.SameFile(top, d)` at `:690`. The CHANGELOG sentence is at about line 303–307 of HEAD's CHANGELOG.md.

**Input (worktree-elsewhere):** clone the upstream to `.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b`, then inside it run `git config core.worktree <C>/wt`. Then run `ethos team add-bundle <U> --name b --apply`.
- **HEAD:** `ethos: the bundle path .../ethos-bundles/b already exists and is not a git repository: remove it, or choose another --name`, exit 1. The path does hold a git repository, so the stated cause is false.
- **main:** `Adding existing repo at '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b' to the index`, then `added bundle "b"`, exit 0. The index gets a gitlink (`160000 a4ab9bb…`), and `.gitmodules` and `git submodule status` are written normally.

**Same class (worktree-rel):** with `core.worktree sub` (a relative path that does not resolve):
- **HEAD:** refuses with the true cause: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel: exit status 128: fatal: cannot chdir to 'sub': No such file or directory`.
- **main:** exit 0 with a gitlink, but `git submodule status` shows no branch.

**Why:** git adopts any directory whose `.git` is a valid non-bare git dir. `isOwnGitRepo` asks a stricter question: is `--show-toplevel` this directory? A clone whose work tree has been moved fails that test.

**The CHANGELOG** says ethos refuses "one that exists and is not a git repository (an existing clone there is left to `git submodule add`)". Both halves are false for this input. DESIGN.md ("exists and is not the top of a git repository") is accurate.

**Fix, either of:**
- Make HEAD agree with git. When `--show-toplevel` names another path, also run `git -C dir rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`. If that equals `dir/.git` (or the gitfile's target), treat the path as an own repository and leave it to git.
- Keep the refusal but report the real cause. Have `isOwnGitRepo` return `topPath`, and change line 658 to say `"%s is in the git work tree %s, not the top of its own; remove it, or choose another --name"` when `topPath` is not empty. Change the CHANGELOG to "one that exists and is not the top of its own git work tree".

## (c) Minor: false sentence in a test comment from this range

`cmd/ethos/add_bundle_precheck_test.go:352-353` says the clone "made from a relative URL" is a clone "of exactly the URL given". That fixture's origin is `/somewhere/else/src`, while the URL given is `../src` from a superproject with no remote. The sentence is true for the insteadOf subtest only.

**Fix:** "…and one whose origin is unrelated to a relative URL given, both reach git submodule add."

## Probes where HEAD and main match, or HEAD is better

| Case | HEAD | main |
|---|---|---|
| Absent path; absent `.punt-labs` | Identical success: gitlink and `.gitmodules` | Same |
| Clone with same origin, different origin, or no origin | Adopted, exit 0, gitlink | Same; the origin-check removal is confirmed |
| Gitfile clone (`--separate-git-dir`), `.git` as a symlink to a gitdir, a `git worktree` of the upstream | Adopted | Same |
| Repo with no commit; orphan branch | git's own "does not have a commit checked out", exit 1 | Same |
| Symlink to a clone at the path | Refused before git runs | Exit 0 "added bundle", but it staged `120000` (a symlink), wrote `.gitmodules`, and `git submodule status` is empty |
| Empty dir, regular file, empty `.git` dir, bare repo, dangling `.git` link, gitfile to a missing dir, mode-000 dir, bad `.git/config`, unknown repository extension | Refused | Refused by git |
| Path already in the index | Refused | Refused by git |
| Path under an ignored directory; parent `ethos-bundles` is a symlink (path absent or a clone) | Same git refusal, exit 1 | Same |

The symlink row is main's silent failure; HEAD's refusal is correct and DESIGN's "git would stage the link" is true.

## Not blocking
- Line 658 error text ("is not a git repository") is also loose for a bare repo, but bare-repo probes fail before it is reached; HEAD reports git's real message "this operation must be run in a work tree".
- The `checkBundleDestination` comment at `team_bundle.go:603-604` ("An existing clone is left for git submodule add, which adopts it") leaves out that git refuses a clone with no commit checked out; DESIGN.md says this correctly.
- `walkedPast` (`internal/resolve/resolve.go:1087-1091`) returns nil with nothing checked when `os.Stat(top)` fails. The rewritten comment says only "Nothing is checked when the walk reaches neither."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: loop.sh <ethos-binary> <repo> <logfile>
set -u
BIN=$1
REPO=$2
LOG=$3
: > "$LOG"
cd "$REPO" || exit 1
prev=""
for i in $(seq 1 400); do
  out=$("$BIN" audit seal 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  printf '### seal %d rc=%d\n%s\n' "$i" "$rc" "$out" >> "$LOG"
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "seal ok after $i iterations" >> "$LOG"
    echo "done iterations=$i"
    exit 0
  fi
  chunk=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -o 'corrupt chunk [^:]*' | head -1 | sed 's/^corrupt chunk //')
  if [ -z "$chunk" ]; then
    echo "seal failed without a corrupt chunk" >> "$LOG"
    echo "stuck iterations=$i"
    exit 2
  fi
  if [ "$chunk" = "$prev" ]; then
    echo "same chunk twice: $chunk" >> "$LOG"
    echo "loop iterations=$i"
    exit 3
  fi
  prev=$chunk
  qout=$("$BIN" audit quarantine "$chunk" 2>&1)
  qrc=$?
  printf '### quarantine %s rc=%d\n%s\n' "$chunk" "$qrc" "$qout" >> "$LOG"
done
echo "cap"
exit 4

tool_input.message:
Review of 334e663..1a13da8 (feat/path-class-table)

I found three items that meet the bar: one regression against main, one code comment that is false and one DESIGN sentence that is false. All three come from one gap. Git adopts any path whose `.git` is a git dir or a valid gitfile, but HEAD refuses some of those with an error. I found no (b) bug and no (d) test defect inside the range. I also found one out-of-range defect that has the (b) shape; it is listed separately for you to rule on.

**Sandbox:** ~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/sfh27-classes/
- Binaries `bin/ethos-head` (1a13da8) and `bin/ethos-main` (cbc1e60), built from git-archived and git-init'ed trees.
- Scripts are in `scripts/`. Every probe ran under `env -i` with its own HOME, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>` and `TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp`, using git 2.43.0.
- Dry run first (`p00-dry.sh`): both binaries put their targets under `probes/dry/`.
- Probe script: `p01-worktree.sh`. Each case runs `ethos team add-bundle <up> --name b --apply` in a superproject P, with bundle path B = `P/.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b`.

## (a) Regression against main: three existing clones that main adopts are refused at HEAD

**Location:** cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go:670-698 (`isOwnGitRepo`) and :650-659 (`checkBundleDestination`). The refusal comes from the first `rev-parse --show-toplevel` probe, which this range did not change, so 334e663 behaves the same. It is still a regression against cbc1e60.

| Case | Input (setup of B) | HEAD | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare-config | `git clone up B; git -C B config core.bare true` | exit 1: `examining the bundle path …/b: git rev-parse: exit status 128: fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree` | exit 0: `Adding existing repo …`, gitlink `160000 8ba1dc1…` staged, `.gitmodules` written |
| wt-rel-missing | `git clone up B; git -C B config core.worktree sub` | exit 1: `git rev-parse: exit status 128: fatal: cannot chdir to 'sub': No such file or directory` | exit 0, gitlink staged |
| wt-abs-missing | `git clone up B; git -C B config core.worktree <C>/nowhere` | exit 1: `examining the top level …/nowhere git reported: stat …/nowhere: no such file or directory` | exit 0, gitlink staged |

- On main in all three cases, the superproject's `git status` then fails ("fatal: 'git status --porcelain=2' failed in submodule …"). So refusing these may be the better behaviour, but then the docs must say so (see c). The new subtest `TestIsOwnGitRepoWithACoreWorktree/unenterable` pins the refusal.
- **Fix, option 1 (match git exactly):**
  - Replace both probes with `git rev-parse --resolve-git-dir <dir>/.git`, run from a neutral directory. That is git's own adoption test (`is_nonbare_repository_dir`).
  - Verified in `p03-resolve.sh`: it exits 0 for wt-abs, wt-abs-missing, wt-rel-missing, bare-config, gitfile-wt, gitfile-super and a linked worktree with its worktree elsewhere.
  - It exits 128 for an empty `.git` dir (`fatal: not a gitdir '…'`), a missing `.git` (`not a gitdir`) and a gitfile to nothing (`not a git repository: …`). Class those three as (false, nil) and anything else as the error.
- **Fix, option 2 (keep the refusal):** state it in the DESIGN paragraph, CHANGELOG and the code comment. Suggested wording: "a clone git cannot set up (`core.bare`, a `core.worktree` that does not exist) is refused with git's error, though `git submodule add` would adopt it."

## (c) False sentences

**1. cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go:603-604** (comment changed in this range):

> "An existing clone is left for git submodule add, which adopts one that has a commit checked out and refuses one that has none."

The three clones above all have a commit checked out. They are never left for git; ethos refuses them first (HEAD output above). The same doc block at :602 says B is refused when it "exists and is not a git repository of its own", but git treats all three as repositories of their own (`--resolve-git-dir` succeeds).

**2. DESIGN.md:12916-12922** (the reworded DES-079 paragraph):

> "a path that exists and is not its own git repository (the top of a work tree, or a `.git` that is git's git dir when `core.worktree` points elsewhere, as git accepts)" and "An existing clone is passed to `git submodule add` whatever its `origin`, as git decides; git adopts it if it has a commit checked out"

"As git accepts" is false: git accepts every `.git` that is a git dir or valid gitfile, whatever `core.bare` or `core.worktree` say. "An existing clone is passed to `git submodule add`" is false for the three inputs above. The next sentence, "A failed … probe of that path is reported as that failure", covers bare-config and wt-rel-missing. It does not cover wt-abs-missing, where git's probe succeeded and ethos's own stat of the top level failed.

**3. CHANGELOG.md:303-305** — "one that exists and is not a git repository (an existing clone there is left to `git submodule add`)". This is false for the same three inputs.

**Fix:** either option 1 above, after which these sentences become true, or reword all three locations as in option 2.

## (b) Nothing inside the range

The new branch (top differs from dir, and `dir/.git` is the git dir) staged a real gitlink and `.gitmodules` in every case I probed, identically to main: wt-abs, wt-rel-exists, wt-inside, wt-super (core.worktree = superproject top), wt-parent, gitfile-wt, wtconfig (`config.worktree`), and a linked worktree with its worktree elsewhere. wt-abs-nocommit is refused by git itself ("does not have a commit checked out") on both.

**Out of range, but (b)-shaped: please rule on it.** At team_bundle.go:684 (`os.SameFile(top, d)`; not changed here, same on main):
- Input: `mkdir B; ln -s P/.git B/.git`.
- HEAD and main both exit 0 with "added bundle "b" at …". Yet `git ls-files -s` shows only `.gitmodules` and `top`: no gitlink. `submodule.<path>.url` and `.active` were written to P/.git/config.
- So ethos reports success while git staged `.gitmodules` and no submodule.
- **Fix:** refuse when the resolved git dir is the same file as the superproject's `--absolute-git-dir` or common dir. Say "the bundle path's .git is this repository's own git dir".
- The gitfile variant (`gitdir: P/.git`) stages a gitlink to the superproject's own HEAD (`25d30d6…`) under the upstream's URL; the same check catches it.

## (d) Nothing

I ran HEAD's add_bundle_precheck_test.go against 334e663 (`p04-tests.sh`, `-run 'TestIsOwnGitRepo|TestAddBundle'`). It passes on HEAD and fails on 334e663 in exactly these places:
- `…/a_failure_with_no_stderr_names_the_exit`: ErrorAs ExitError, and the trailing-": " check.
- `…WithACoreWorktree/elsewhere`, `/a_gitfile_to_the_git_dir` and `/adopted_through_add-bundle` (log was `--version -C -C -C`, no `submodule`).

`/unenterable` passes on both. It pins existing behaviour; it would fail if the error were classed as "not a git repository". The rewritten insteadOf and relative-URL subtests can fail too: a check using `git remote get-url` (which applies the clone's insteadOf) or a literal origin comparison would refuse them.

## Not blocking
- team_bundle.go:667-669: the list of failures that are "the error" omits the new stat failure on the git dir git reported.
- team_bundle.go:694-696: a "not a git repository" answer from the second probe, after the first succeeded, returns (false, nil). That is a race-only path, but it would surface as "is not a git repository".
- resolve.go:1088-1091: `walkedPast` returns nil when top cannot be stat'ed. The comment now says so and it is true, but it is a silent skip.
- add_bundle_precheck_test.go:202 and :41: `os.ReadFile` errors are discarded in `TestAddBundleLeavesToGitWhatGitAccepts` and in `assertNoNetwork`. The range fixed this only in `ran`.
- add_bundle_precheck_test.go:33: `loggedGit` records only `$1`, so a git started as `git -C <dir> submodule …` logs as `-C`. `assertNoNetwork` would miss a network call started that way. The current network calls use Dir, not -C.
- `TestIsOwnGitRepoWithACoreWorktree/adopted_through_add-bundle` uses a no-commit fixture, so git refuses it. The subtest shows the hand-off, not adoption, despite its name.

Round 27: all three items are done in one commit on feat/path-class-table in <repo>/.claude/worktrees/classes. `make check` exited 0 before the commit. Nothing is pushed. I did not edit DESIGN.md or CHANGELOG.md.

Commit after 1a13da8: cdf341b fix(team): add-bundle uses git's own adoption test; refuses the superproject's own git dir

**Item 1: git's own adoption test** (`cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go`)
- `isOwnGitRepo(dir)` now returns `(bool, resolvedGitDir, error)` and runs `git rev-parse --resolve-git-dir dir/.git` from dir's parent. It is bounded and goes through `gitenv`.
- Exit 0 means a repository of its own, and the resolved git dir is returned.
- (false, nil) when `dir/.git` is absent, or git says "not a gitdir" or "not a git repository". The stderr match is on those two substrings. `gitenv.IsNotARepo` would miss "not a git repository: /nonexistent".
- Any other failure is an error wrapping the exit error, with stderr appended. A timeout is returned as is.
- The show-toplevel, absolute-git-dir and top-stat probes are gone. `resolve.DotIsGitDir` is unexported again as `dotIsGitDir`; only `walkedPast` uses it.
- Tests:
  - `TestAddBundleAdoptionFollowsGit`: the clones with `core.worktree` elsewhere, `core.bare true`, `core.worktree sub` (missing) and `core.worktree` at a missing absolute path are each adopted by `isOwnGitRepo` and reach `git submodule add`. It also covers a gitfile to the git dir (resolved dir checked) and a plain directory.
  - `TestIsOwnGitRepoReportsFailures`: no `.git`, timeout, exit with no stderr (the exit error is in the chain), another git failure (dubious ownership), an empty `.git` directory, a gitfile to nothing (both false with no error), and an empty `.git` file (error "invalid gitfile format").
  - The `unenterable` subtest is gone. Under the new test, `core.worktree sub` is adopted.

**Item 2: the superproject's own git dir**
- `refuseOwnGitDir` stats the resolved git dir and compares it by `SameFile` with the superproject's `--absolute-git-dir` and `--git-common-dir`. A match is refused with "the bundle path's .git is this repository's own git dir".
- `TestAddBundleRefusesTheSuperprojectsOwnGitDir` covers both a symlink `B/.git -> P/.git` and a gitfile `gitdir: P/.git`. It also asserts no network call.

**Item 3: tests only**
- `os.ReadFile` errors are checked in `assertNoNetwork`, which tolerates only a missing log because git may never have run, and in the two sites that need git to have run.
- `loggedGit` now skips any `-C <dir>` and `-c k=v` pairs before recording the subcommand.
- The `adopted_through_add-bundle` subtest is now "add-bundle hands it to git submodule add: <case>", one per config variant.

**Fail at 1a13da8**
I ran the new test file in a scratch worktree at 1a13da8. The old `isOwnGitRepo` has a different signature, so I added a test-only shim that adapts it.
- Fail there: the `core.bare true`, `core.worktree sub` missing and absolute-missing cases (both direct and through add-bundle), the gitfile-to-git-dir case, a gitfile to nothing, and both superproject-git-dir cases (symlink and gitfile).
- Pass at 1a13da8: the elsewhere, plain-directory and other pre-existing behaviours (no `.git`, timeout, no stderr, dubious ownership, empty `.git` directory, empty `.git` file).

The scratch worktree is moved to `.tmp/wb6-done` and pruned. `stash@{0}` from round 18 is still there and needs your consent to drop.

tool_input.message:
I reviewed ethos 1a13da8..02588c6 (feat/path-class-table) and ran it in a sandbox. Two findings meet the bar. Finding 1 is blocking: it hides a permission error and turns it into "remove it" advice for a real clone. Finding 2 is a gap in the new self-reference refusal, and main behaves the same way. The rest of the range checked out.

**How I ran it.** Sandbox: ~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/sfh28-classes/. I extracted HEAD and main with `git archive`, ran `git init` in each, and built `bin/ethos-head` and `bin/ethos-main`. git is 2.43.0. Every probe ran under `env -i` with its own HOME, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>` and `TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp`. I never set GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_COMMON_DIR. The dry run came first and kept every target inside the sandbox. Scripts are in `scripts/` (p00-dry, p01-cases, p02-bare, p03-perm) and the full p01 transcript is in `p01.out`. Each probe ran `ethos team add-bundle <U> --name b --apply` in superproject P, with the bundle at P/.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b ("B" below).

## Finding 1: a permission failure becomes "not a git repository: remove it"
Bars (b) and (c), plus (a) for one case.

- **Where:**
  - cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go:700 discards every `os.Lstat` error except ErrNotExist and falls through to git.
  - git answers `fatal: not a gitdir '…/b/.git'` because it cannot stat the file. Line 712 maps that to (false, nil).
  - Line 658 then prints the refusal with "remove it".
- **Input:** a real clone at B, with either `chmod 600 B` (not searchable) or `chmod 000 B`. `stat B/.git` gives "Permission denied".
- **HEAD, both cases:** `ethos: the bundle path …/b already exists and is not a git repository: remove it, or choose another --name`, exit 1.
- **main, `chmod 600`:** `warning: unable to access '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b/.gitignore': Permission denied` / `fatal: unable to stat '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b/README': Permission denied`, exit 1. Main shows the real cause; HEAD hides it. That is the (a) regression.
- **main, `chmod 000`:** `fatal: '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b' already exists and is not a valid git repo`, with no advice to remove anything.
- **Impact:** the EACCES never reaches the user, and following the advice deletes a working clone.
- **False sentence (c):** DESIGN.md:12919-12920 says "A failed or timed-out probe of that path is reported as that failure." Here the failed probe (Lstat EACCES) is not reported.
- **Fix:**
  ```go
  if _, err := os.Lstat(dot); errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
      return false, "", nil
  } else if err != nil {
      return false, "", fmt.Errorf("examining %s: %w", dot, err)
  }
  ```
  Add a test that runs `chmod 600` on a cloned dest and asserts the error wraps `fs.ErrPermission` and does not contain "remove it".

## Finding 2: a `.git` that is another worktree's git dir of the superproject is not refused
Bar (b). Not a regression: main behaves identically.

- **Where:** cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go:667-688. `refuseOwnGitDir` compares B's resolved git dir with the superproject's `--absolute-git-dir` and `--git-common-dir`. It never checks B's own common dir, so a git dir under `<common>/worktrees/<x>` passes.
- **Inputs, all exit 0 with `added bundle "b"`, on HEAD and on main:**
  - **gitfile-super-wtdir:** run `git worktree add C/pw -b pw` in P, then write `gitdir: P/.git/worktrees/pw` into B/.git. P's index gets `160000 0730fcbd… .punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b`. P's HEAD is `0730fcbd…`, so that is the superproject's own commit.
  - **super-linked-wt:** run `git worktree add B -b sw` in P. Same result: the gitlink equals P's HEAD (`0730fcbd`).
  - **bare-to-other-wtdir:** bare repo R with worktrees w and w2. In w, write `gitdir: R/worktrees/w2` into B/.git. The index gets `160000 6058fddc…`, which equals HEAD (`6058fddc`).
- **Why it matters:** this is the harm the function's own comment names, "a gitlink to the superproject's own HEAD". `.gitmodules` records URL U, so a fresh clone of the superproject cannot fetch that commit from U.
- **Fix:** take B's common dir with git's own rule: if `<resolved>/commondir` exists, use `resolved` joined with its trimmed contents, otherwise `resolved`. Refuse when that common dir is the same file (`os.SameFile`) as the superproject's common dir. Add the gitfile-to-`worktrees/<other>` case to TestAddBundleRefusesTheSuperprojectsOwnGitDir.

## What passed
- **Self-reference refusals:** the symlink to P/.git, the gitfile to P/.git, and the relative symlink and relative gitfile all fail on HEAD with the new message. On main they succeed: the symlink case stages no gitlink and the gitfile case stages a gitlink to P's HEAD.
- **Bare main repo:** R/.git (`to-common`) and `R/worktrees/w` (`to-own-wtdir`) are refused on HEAD and succeed on main, so the `--git-common-dir` branch works.
- **No other regressions:** across 33 layouts, every case that succeeds on main succeeds on HEAD with the same index entries and `.gitmodules`. That includes bare-config, wt-rel-missing, wt-abs-missing, wt-abs, wt-super, gitfile, gitfile-rel, dotgit-symlink, upworktree, the absorbed submodule of another repo, and clone-other. HEAD refuses earlier, with no network, in: emptydir, file, bare, empty `.git`, dangling `.git` and gitfile-missing.
- **Tests:** they pass on HEAD. With the `refuseOwnGitDir` call mutated out, both subtests of TestAddBundleRefusesTheSuperprojectsOwnGitDir fail. The "hands it to git submodule add" subtests would fail against the old show-toplevel heuristic, which errors on bare-config and wt-rel-missing. `loggedGit` logs only `$1`, so "submodule" cannot match a temp-dir path. I found no (d) violations.
- **The "no repository around it is consulted" comment is accurate:** strace shows `git rev-parse --resolve-git-dir` touches only HOME/.gitconfig and B/.git. It never touches P/.git.

## Not blocking
- The isOwnGitRepo comment (line 692) calls `--resolve-git-dir` "git's own adoption test", and DESIGN says the same in its parenthetical. `git submodule add` actually uses `is_nonbare_repository_dir`, which also accepts a gitfile it cannot open. The only visible difference is the message: for `chmod 000 B/.git` as a gitfile, both versions refuse.
- With an unreadable separate git dir (the gitfile target set to `chmod 000`), git says "not a git repository" and HEAD adds "remove it" to a real clone. Main shows git's "not a valid git repo" instead. A fix for finding 1 does not cover this case.
- An empty `.git` file is reported as "examining the bundle path …: invalid gitfile format", a probe failure, rather than as a "not a git repository" refusal. It is still refused.
- The `--git-common-dir` branch has no unit test. Only the absolute-git-dir path is covered.
- A `.git` pointing at another submodule's git dir in the superproject (P/.git/modules/other) is adopted on HEAD and main alike, so two submodules share one git dir.
- Run from a linked worktree of P, add-bundle targets P's main checkout; HEAD and main behave the same.

- **Where:** DESIGN.md:12920–12921, "A `.git` that cannot be examined is reported with the operating-system error." The isOwnGitRepo comment at cmd/ethos/team_bundle.go:724 says the same thing.
- **Input:** an ordinary clone at `.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b`, then `chmod 000 b/.git` (the .git directory), then `ethos team add-bundle <up> --name b --apply`. This is the p01 `unreadable-dotgit` layout.
- **HEAD (exit 1):** `ethos: the bundle path …/b has a .git git does not accept: fatal: not a gitdir '…/b/.git'`. No operating-system error appears. Lstat succeeds, and git gives "not a gitdir", which is turned into a `dotRefusedError`.
- **main (exit 1):** `fatal: '.punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b' already exists and is not a valid git repo` / `ethos: running git submodule add … exit status 128`.
- **Why it matters:** a .git ethos cannot read is reported as one git rejects, so the user gets no hint that this is a permissions problem. Only a .git that cannot be lstat'd, because the bundle directory is not searchable, gets the OS error.
- **Fix, either of:**
  - (1) Narrow the prose, e.g. "A bundle path whose `.git` cannot be stat'ed (the directory is not searchable) is reported with the operating-system error; a `.git` git cannot read is reported with git's message." Make the same change at line 724.

- **Linked worktree targets the main worktree:** run from a linked worktree `pw`, add-bundle clones into and stages in the main worktree `p`, not `pw`. `p`'s index gets `160000 … .punt-labs/ethos-bundles/b` and `.gitmodules` (from-linked-wt-* layouts). Main behaves identically; it should be tracked as its own bead.
- **Another submodule's git dir is accepted:** a bundle `.git` that points at `$P/.git/modules/other` is staged as a second gitlink sharing that submodule's git dir, on HEAD and main alike. DES-079 does say "any other existing clone is passed to git submodule add".
- **Error text is inaccurate:** for a linked-worktree or other-worktree git dir, the refusal says "the bundle path's .git is this repository's own git dir (<common dir>)". The bundle's git dir is actually a different one that shares the common dir.
- **"remove it" advice:** for a `git worktree add` at the bundle path, this advice can discard uncommitted worktree changes and leave a stale worktree entry. `git worktree remove` is the safer advice.
- **Unused unwrapping:** the `errors.As(err, &refused)` pass-through in checkBundleDestination (team_bundle.go:654–657) only drops a prefix. No test tells the wrapped and unwrapped forms apart.
- **Untested branches:** the absolute-path branch of the `commondir` read and the non-ErrNotExist `commondir` read error.
- **commondir parsing:** `strings.TrimSpace` on `commondir` differs slightly from git, which strips only trailing CR/LF. This only matters for a hand-edited file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: origcheck.sh <sandbox> <data-repo>
# For every staged withheld record, check that the original whose sha256 it
# names is kept in the local quarantine zone with that hash.
set -u
S=$1
D=$2
export GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=$S
Q=$D/.punt-labs/local/ethos/quarantine
ok=0
bad=0
while IFS= read -r p; do
  case "$p" in *.corrupt*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  rec=$(git -C "$D" show ":$p" 2>/dev/null | head -c 2000)
  case "$rec" in *'"withheld"'*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  sha=$(printf '%s' "$rec" | sed -n 's/.*"sha256":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1/p')
  f=$(ls "$Q" | grep -F ".${sha:0:12}.corrupt" | head -1)
  if [ -n "$f" ] && [ "$(sha256sum "$Q/$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sha" ]; then
    ok=$((ok+1))
  else
    bad=$((bad+1))
    echo "MISSING original for $p sha=$sha"
  fi
done < <(git -C "$D" ls-files)
echo "records-with-original=$ok missing=$bad quarantine-files=$(ls "$Q" | wc -l)"

The evaluator's own contract (internal/hook/preconditions.go:76-78) says the block reason must be operator-actionable.

The two suffixes are the only explanation the operator gets for a block that a Read cannot clear:
- :91-93: the path was redacted from another user's home, so no Read on this machine can match it.
- :97-98: N earlier Reads were ignored because their audit lines predate the path format, so the file must be Read again.

Without them the operator sees the contract message, Reads the named file, and stays blocked with no reason given. The contract's message is still the first part of the string, unchanged.

package mcp

import (
	"context"
	"errors"

	"path/filepath"

// A caller named by session metadata is refused an identity when the store
// cannot be located, as every other whoami is: the metadata branch comes after
// the store-location refusal, so it never answers from an unusable store.
func TestMetadataWhoamiRefusedWhenStoreCannotBeLocated(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("live location fails", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, _ := metadataHandler(t)
		base := t.TempDir()
		dir := filepath.Join(base, "r")
		require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755))
		require.NoError(t, os.Symlink(filepath.Join(dir, "nowhere"), filepath.Join(dir, ".git")))
		t.Setenv("GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES", base)
		t.Chdir(dir)
		result, err := h.handleIdentity(context.Background(), metadataCall(t, "ses_A", map[string]any{"method": "whoami"}))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.True(t, result.IsError)
		text := resultText(t, result)
		assert.Contains(t, text, "identity is refused")
		assert.NotContains(t, text, "Repo alice")
	})

	t.Run("handler built for a failed location", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, _ := metadataHandler(t)
		WithStoreError(errors.New("store not located"))(h)
		srv, _ := fullServerFor(t, h)
		res, err := srv.GetTool("identity").Handler(context.Background(), metadataCall(t, "ses_A", map[string]any{"method": "whoami"}))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.True(t, res.IsError)
		assert.Contains(t, resultText(t, res), "refusing")
		assert.NotContains(t, resultText(t, res), "Repo alice")
	})

	t.Run("iam checks no persona against it", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, _ := metadataHandler(t)
		WithStoreError(errors.New("store not located"))(h)
		result, err := h.handleSession(context.Background(), metadataCall(t, "ses_A", map[string]any{
			"method": "iam", "persona": "carol", "session_id": "ses_A", "agent_id": "ses_A",
		}))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.True(t, result.IsError)
		assert.Contains(t, resultText(t, result), "refused")
	})
}
EOF

Merge commit: ff49e12. Its parents are 97896fd and 88a7963, and the commit message carries a Co-Authored-By line.

**`internal/mcp/tools.go`**
- The Handler struct has both sides' fields: slice 1's `storeErr` and `relocation` plus #540's `opencodeSessionMetadata`.
- `handleWhoami` now runs in this order:
  1. the `resolve.Roots()` refusal on `loc.Err()`;
  2. the `bundle.ConfigIssue` refusal;
  3. #540's metadata-session branch;
  4. `resolve.Resolve(h.store, h.sessionStore, loc.Checkout)`, with slice 1's three-argument signature.

**`cmd/ethos/serve.go`**
- Slice 1's structure is kept: `locateServeStore`, `buildServeHandler`, `RelocateStore` and the store-error message.
- `runServeImpl` creates `mcp.WithOpenCodeSessionMetadata(opencodeSessionMetadata)` once. It passes it to both the first `buildServeHandler` call and the relocation builder, so a relocated handler keeps it.
- `buildServeHandler` takes `extra ...mcp.Option` and appends them. I made it variadic so the existing test call sites did not change.

**Other #540 call sites**
- The `identity` tool is strict-guarded, so `whoami` through the guard already refused on `storeErr`. Both the live-location check and the guard are now covered by tests.
- `session iam`'s metadata branch loads identities from `h.store`, and the `session` tool is unguarded. That branch now refuses when `h.storeErr` is set: "iam: ...; the persona is refused rather than checked against the global store". The non-metadata `iam` path loads no identity, so I left it alone.
- `resolveSessionID` and `callerParticipant` use only the global session store, so they need no change.

**Tests**
- New `internal/mcp/metadata_refusal_test.go` has three subtests:
  - `whoami` with session metadata is refused when the live location fails (a dangling `.git`).
  - A handler built for a failed location refuses it through the guard.
  - `iam` with session metadata is refused when the store cannot be located.
- None of them leaks "Repo alice" into the result.
- I did not add a test that a relocated handler keeps the metadata option. It is covered only by construction.

"""Drive ethos serve over stdio with OpenCode session metadata.

usage: python3 -I drive.py <sandbox> <variant>
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

SB = sys.argv[1]
VARIANT = sys.argv[2]
BIN = os.path.join(SB, "bin-" + VARIANT, "ethos")
RUN = os.path.join(SB, "run-" + VARIANT)
HOME = os.path.join(RUN, "home")
REPOS = os.path.join(RUN, "repos")

ENV = {
    "PATH": os.environ["PATH"],
    "HOME": HOME,
    "TMPDIR": os.path.join(SB, "tmp"),
    "GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES": SB,
    "USER": "nobody",
}


def ident(root, handle, name, kind="agent"):
    d = os.path.join(root, "identities")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(d, handle + ".yaml"), "w") as f:
        f.write(f"name: {name}\nhandle: {handle}\nkind: {kind}\n")


def git(*args, cwd):
    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t",
                    "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", *args], cwd=cwd, env=ENV,
                   check=True, capture_output=True)


def make_repo(name):
    d = os.path.join(REPOS, name)
    os.makedirs(d)
    git("init", "-q", cwd=d)
    eth = os.path.join(d, ".punt-labs", "ethos")
    for h in ("alice", "bob", "carol"):
        ident(eth, h, "Repo " + h)
    git("add", "-A", cwd=d)
    git("commit", "-qm", "init", cwd=d)
    return d


def setup():
    if os.path.exists(RUN):
        shutil.rmtree(RUN)
    g = os.path.join(HOME, ".punt-labs", "ethos")
    for h in ("alice", "bob", "carol"):
        ident(g, h, "Global " + h, "human")
    sd = os.path.join(g, "sessions")
    os.makedirs(sd)
    for sid, persona in (("ses_A", "alice"), ("ses_B", "bob")):
        with open(os.path.join(sd, sid + ".yaml"), "w") as f:
            f.write(f"session: {sid}\nstarted: '2026-10-26T00:00:00Z'\nparticipants:\n"
                    f"  - agent_id: human\n    persona: bob\n"
                    f"  - agent_id: {sid}\n    persona: {persona}\n    parent: human\n")
    make_repo("healthy")
    dang = os.path.join(REPOS, "dangling")
    os.makedirs(dang)
    ident(os.path.join(dang, ".punt-labs", "ethos"), "alice", "Repo alice")
    os.symlink(os.path.join(dang, "nowhere"), os.path.join(dang, ".git"))
    bad = make_repo("badbundle")
    with open(os.path.join(bad, ".punt-labs", "ethos.yaml"), "w") as f:
        f.write("active_bundle: does-not-exist\n")
    make_repo("flip")


class Server:
    def __init__(self, cwd, flag=True):
        args = [BIN, "serve"] + (["--opencode-session-metadata"] if flag else [])
        self.p = subprocess.Popen(args, cwd=cwd, env=ENV, stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                                  stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
        self.n = 0
        self.rpc("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2025-03-26", "capabilities": {},
                                "clientInfo": {"name": "drv", "version": "0"}})
        self.p.stdin.write(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}) + "\n")
        self.p.stdin.flush()

    def rpc(self, method, params):
        self.n += 1
        self.p.stdin.write(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": self.n, "method": method, "params": params}) + "\n")
        self.p.stdin.flush()
        while True:
            line = self.p.stdout.readline()
            if not line:
                raise SystemExit("server closed: " + self.p.stderr.read())
            m = json.loads(line)
            if m.get("id") == self.n:
                return m

    def call(self, tool, args, sid="ses_A"):
        params = {"name": tool, "arguments": args}
        if sid is not None:
            params["_meta"] = {"ai.opencode/sessionID": sid}
        r = self.rpc("tools/call", params)
        res = r.get("result", r)
        texts = [c.get("text", "") for c in res.get("content", [])]
        out = " | ".join(t.replace("\n", " ")[:300] for t in texts)
        return ("ERR " if res.get("isError") else "OK  ") + out

    def close(self):
        self.p.stdin.close()
        self.p.wait(timeout=10)
        return self.p.stderr.read().strip()


def show(label, s):
    print(f"  {label}: {s}")


def reset_rosters():
    sd = os.path.join(HOME, ".punt-labs", "ethos", "sessions")
    for sid, persona in (("ses_A", "alice"), ("ses_B", "bob")):
        with open(os.path.join(sd, sid + ".yaml"), "w") as f:
            f.write(f"session: {sid}\nstarted: '2026-10-26T00:00:00Z'\nparticipants:\n"
                    f"  - agent_id: human\n    persona: bob\n"
                    f"  - agent_id: {sid}\n    persona: {persona}\n    parent: human\n")


def main():
    setup()
    for name in ("healthy", "dangling", "badbundle"):
        reset_rosters()
        print(f"== {VARIANT} / {name} (flag on)")
        s = Server(os.path.join(REPOS, name))
        show("whoami ses_A", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
        show("whoami ses_B", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}, "ses_B"))
        show("roster implicit", s.call("session", {"method": "roster"}))
        show("iam carol", s.call("session", {"method": "iam", "persona": "carol", "session_id": "ses_A", "agent_id": "ses_A"}))
        show("whoami after iam", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
        show("whoami bad meta", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}, "../x"))
        show("identity get alice (no meta)", s.call("identity", {"method": "get", "handle": "alice"}, None))
        print("  stderr:", s.close()[:300])

    reset_rosters()
    print(f"== {VARIANT} / healthy (flag off)")
    s = Server(os.path.join(REPOS, "healthy"), flag=False)
    show("whoami meta ignored", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    s.close()

    # relocation: healthy -> broken -> repaired, one server
    reset_rosters()
    flip = os.path.join(REPOS, "flip")
    print(f"== {VARIANT} / flip relocation")
    s = Server(flip)
    show("1 healthy whoami", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    os.rename(os.path.join(flip, ".git"), os.path.join(flip, "git.real"))
    os.symlink(os.path.join(flip, "nowhere"), os.path.join(flip, ".git"))
    show("2 broken whoami", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    show("2 broken iam", s.call("session", {"method": "iam", "persona": "carol", "session_id": "ses_A"}))
    os.remove(os.path.join(flip, ".git"))
    os.rename(os.path.join(flip, "git.real"), os.path.join(flip, ".git"))
    show("3 repaired whoami ses_B", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}, "ses_B"))
    show("3 repaired iam carol", s.call("session", {"method": "iam", "persona": "carol", "session_id": "ses_A"}))
    show("3 repaired whoami ses_A", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    with open(os.path.join(flip, ".punt-labs", "ethos.yaml"), "w") as f:
        f.write("active_bundle: does-not-exist\n")
    show("4 bundle-broken whoami", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    show("4 bundle-broken iam", s.call("session", {"method": "iam", "persona": "alice", "session_id": "ses_A"}))
    os.remove(os.path.join(flip, ".punt-labs", "ethos.yaml"))
    show("5 bundle-fixed whoami", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    s.close()

    # start broken, then repair: the rebuilt handler must keep the metadata option
    reset_rosters()
    dang = os.path.join(REPOS, "dangling")
    print(f"== {VARIANT} / start broken then repair")
    s = Server(dang)
    show("1 broken whoami", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}))
    os.remove(os.path.join(dang, ".git"))
    git("init", "-q", cwd=dang)
    show("2 repaired whoami ses_B", s.call("identity", {"method": "whoami"}, "ses_B"))
    show("2 repaired roster implicit ses_B", s.call("session", {"method": "roster"}, "ses_B"))
    s.close()


main()

## Merge ff49e12 review: no findings in the four reported categories

No #540 behaviour is lost. No slice-1 refusal is bypassed. I found no false comment that the merge introduces. Every new test can fail for the defect it names. I confirmed each answer by running the code: a stdio JSON-RPC driver against built binaries, plus mutation tests.

**Sandbox:** ~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/merge540-classes/
- `git archive` of ff49e12 and 88a7963, each `git init`-ed, with binaries in `bin-merge/` and `bin-main/`.
- Every run set `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>`, `TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp` and a sandbox `HOME`. `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` were never set.
- Nothing touched the real repo or its worktrees except `git show`, `git diff` and `git archive`.
- Scripts: `scripts/drive.py` (the MCP driver), `scripts/ttl.py`, `scripts/mutate.py`, `scripts/gotest.sh`.

**Static check.** `git diff -U0 97896fd ff49e12` for `cmd/ethos/serve.go`, `internal/mcp/tools.go` and `internal/session/store.go` is purely additive, apart from realigning the `Handler` struct fields. The additions are #540's code plus three things:
- the `extra ...mcp.Option` threading in serve.go;
- the `h.storeErr` check in the iam metadata branch (`tools.go:219`);
- the metadata branch placed after the `Roots()` and `ConfigIssue` refusals in `handleWhoami` (`tools.go:293`, after lines 282–292).

### (a) #540 behaviour is kept
I ran `ethos serve --opencode-session-metadata` with `_meta {"ai.opencode/sessionID": ...}`.

- **Healthy repo:** the merge binary and the 88a7963 binary gave identical output:
  - whoami for ses_A returned "Repo alice"; for ses_B, "Repo bob".
  - An implicit roster call returned ses_A's roster.
  - iam carol returned `Set persona "carol" for ses_A in session ses_A`, and whoami then returned "Repo carol".
  - A `../x` session ID returned the `_meta ... safe session ID` error.
- **Flag off:** the metadata is ignored and the call falls through to the legacy `no identity resolved: ... CLAUDE_PID ...` error.
- **After RelocateStore rebuilds the handler:**
  - I started a server in a repo whose `.git` is a dangling symlink; whoami was refused.
  - I replaced it with a real `git init`. The rebuilt handler then served whoami for ses_B by metadata (`Global bob`, which is correct: that repo holds only alice) and an implicit roster for ses_B.
  - In a second server, I set a bad `active_bundle` and then removed it. After the removal, whoami answered "Repo carol" by metadata.
- **Go tests in the sandbox:** `internal/mcp` (all tests), `internal/session` (all tests), and `TestServe*` in `cmd/ethos` all pass.

### (b) No slice-1 refusal is bypassed
- **Dangling .git:** metadata whoami (ses_A, ses_B and malformed) returned `refusing identity: it is only answered from a...`. Metadata iam returned `iam: the repository store could not be located (...); the persona is refused rather than checked against the global store`.
- **Bad bundle (`active_bundle: does-not-exist`):** metadata whoami returned `refusing: nothing is answered while it cannot be honoured`. Metadata iam returned `iam: the repository's bundle or policy configuration is unusable (...); the persona is refused ...`. This works because `locateServeStore` folds `configIssue()` into `loc.Err`, so `h.storeErr` is set.
- **Healthy, then broken in the same server:** whoami and iam are refused once the location cache entry expires (at 31 s).
- Metadata roster stays answered under every failure, as intended: the session tool is unguarded and the roster is global.

### (c) No false comment in the resolution
- The serve.go comment on `extra` options is true: a rebuilt handler keeps the metadata option, as shown in (a).
- The iam comment at `tools.go:219` is true.
- The merge commit message is accurate.

### (d) The new tests can fail
I ran each mutation against the sandbox copy, then reverted it:
- **Metadata branch moved above the `Roots()` refusal in `handleWhoami`:** the subtest `live_location_fails` fails (`metadata_refusal_test.go:29`).
- **iam `storeErr` check removed:** the subtest `iam_checks_no_persona_against_it` fails (`metadata_refusal_test.go:54`).

### Not blocking
1. **A just-broken .git is still served for up to 30 s.** A healthy location stays cached for `locateTTL = 30s` (`internal/resolve/resolve.go:923-933`). For that window after a `.git` breaks, metadata whoami and iam still answer from the repository store; so does non-metadata `identity get`.
   - Observed: right after the break, whoami returned "Repo alice" and iam carol returned OK. After 31 s, both were refused.
   - This is slice-1's documented TTL and applies to every tool, so it is not a metadata bypass.
   - Still, the comment at `metadata_refusal_test.go:15-17` ("so it never answers from an unusable store") is true only once the store is located again. Suggested wording: "...so it never answers once the store is located as unusable (a cached healthy location is reused for up to locateTTL)."
2. **One subtest does not guard the ordering.** The subtest `handler built for a failed location` (`metadata_refusal_test.go:35-45`) still passes with the metadata branch moved first. `guardStore`'s `strictTools["identity"]` refuses before `handleWhoami` runs. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: loop.sh <ethos-binary> <repo> <logfile> <home>
set -u
SB=~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/sfh29-redact
export GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=$SB
export TMPDIR=$SB/tmp
export HOME=$4
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_COMMON_DIR
BIN=$1
REPO=$2
LOG=$3
: > "$LOG"
cd "$REPO" || exit 1
prev=""
for i in $(seq 1 400); do
  out=$("$BIN" audit seal 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  printf '### seal %d rc=%d\n%s\n' "$i" "$rc" "$out" >> "$LOG"
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "seal ok after $i iterations" >> "$LOG"
    echo "done iterations=$i"
    exit 0
  fi
  chunk=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -o 'corrupt chunk [^:]*' | head -1 | sed 's/^corrupt chunk //')
  if [ -z "$chunk" ]; then
    echo "seal failed without a corrupt chunk" >> "$LOG"
    echo "stuck iterations=$i"
    exit 2
  fi
  if [ "$chunk" = "$prev" ]; then
    echo "same chunk twice: $chunk" >> "$LOG"
    echo "loop iterations=$i"
    exit 3
  fi
  prev=$chunk
  qout=$("$BIN" audit quarantine "$chunk" 2>&1)
  qrc=$?
  printf '### quarantine %s rc=%d\n%s\n' "$chunk" "$qrc" "$qout" >> "$LOG"
done
echo "cap"
exit 4

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build two data templates from a copy of the real ethos .punt-labs state:
#   tpl-r  verbatim (run with a /root-like HOME: every ~ is foreign)
#   tpl-u  jfreeman -> sfhuserx everywhere (run with HOME=~[redacted-user] own home)
set -eu
S=~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/sfh30-redact
SRC=<repo>
export GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=$S
export TMPDIR=$S/tmp
for t in tpl-r tpl-u; do
  D=$S/$t
  rm -rf "$D"
  mkdir -p "$D/.punt-labs"
  cp -a "$SRC/.punt-labs/ethos" "$D/.punt-labs/ethos"
  cp -a "$SRC/.punt-labs/local" "$D/.punt-labs/local"
  cp -a "$SRC/.punt-labs/ethos.yaml" "$D/.punt-labs/ethos.yaml"
  cp -a "$SRC/.gitignore" "$D/.gitignore"
  if [ "$t" = tpl-u ]; then
    grep -rlZ jfreeman "$D/.punt-labs" | xargs -0 -r perl -pi -e 's/jfreeman/sfhuserx/g'
    for f in $(find "$D/.punt-labs" -name '*jfreeman*'); do mv "$f" "${f//jfreeman/sfhuserx}"; done
  fi
  # Remove ethos git hooks influence: plain repo
  cd "$D"
  git init -q
  git add -A
  git -c user.name=x -c user.email=x@x -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -qm snap --no-verify
  echo "$t: $(git ls-files | wc -l) tracked, $(grep -rl jfreeman .punt-labs | wc -l) files with jfreeman"
done

# Build the cr35 sandbox: git-archive copies of hd=90b3548, ad=ad96432, dd=ddefb51, each git-inited, with the cr30-cr34 probes.
set -euo pipefail
SB=~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/cr35-redact
OLD=~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/cr34-redact
WT=<repo>/.claude/worktrees/redact
export GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="$SB"
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_COMMON_DIR
for pair in hd:90b3548 ad:ad96432 dd:ddefb51; do
  t=${pair%%:*}; c=${pair##*:}
  rm -rf "$SB/$t"; mkdir -p "$SB/$t"
  git -C "$WT" archive --format=tar -o "$SB/$t.tar" "$c"
  tar -xf "$SB/$t.tar" -C "$SB/$t"
  if [ "$t" = dd ]; then src=$OLD/base; else src=$OLD/head; fi
  cp "$src"/internal/mission/zz_*_test.go "$SB/$t/internal/mission/"

  echo "$t $c"
done

n=$1; M=$SB/mut_$n
rm -rf "$M"; cp -a "$SB/hd" "$M"
case $n in
  slug1) # drop the first alternative of leakSlugAudit
    sed -i '931s#(?:^|\[^a-z0-9\])-(?:home|users)-\[^\\\\s/\\"'"'"'`-\]+|##' "$M/internal/redact/redact.go"
    sed -n 931p "$M/internal/redact/redact.go" ;;
  plain) # mission path predicate back to plainPathField (ad96432)
    sed -i '55s#redact.RepoRelative(s)#c.plainPathField(s)#' "$M/internal/mission/guard.go"
    sed -i '745s#redact.RepoRelative(s)#r.plainPathField(s)#' "$M/internal/mission/redact.go"
    sed -n 55p "$M/internal/mission/guard.go"; sed -n 745p "$M/internal/mission/redact.go" ;;
  ownrule) # OwnHomeRule drops the dash-encoded own home
    python3 -I - "$M/internal/redact/redact.go" <<'EOF'
import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
old='func OwnHomeRule(s, home string) string { return leakRule(s, home, ruleOwn) }'
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,'func OwnHomeRule(s, home string) string { if r := leakRule(s, home, ruleOwn); r == "names this machine\'s home directory" { return r }; return "" }')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
    ;;
  auditfull) # audit plain path field judged in full
    sed -i 's#return leakRule(s, home, ruleAuditPlain)#return leakRule(s, home, ruleAuditFull)#' "$M/internal/redact/redact.go"
    grep -n "ruleAuditFull)" "$M/internal/redact/redact.go" ;;
esac
cd "$M"
bash "$SB/scripts/gt.sh" mut_$n ./internal/hook ./internal/mission -run "^(TestPathField_|TestAudit_)" -count=1 2>&1 | grep -E "^(ok|FAIL|--- FAIL)|Error:|Messages:|Test:" | head -60

done

import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()

open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
old='if err := refuseOwnDashHome(s.repoRoot, &updated, onDisk); err != nil {'

open(p,'w').write(s)

tool_input.message:
Final-round review of 90b3548..0a2e020 (ethos, DES-080). I found nothing under (a) or (d), and no leak or data loss under (b). Under (b), one changed entry gets past the prior-comparison, but it is stored exactly as ddefb51 stores it (rewritten to `-~`), so it causes no leak or loss; it is folded into (c)-3. There are three false comments under (c). Everything was run in ~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/sfh36-redact/ using git archive copies of 0a2e020 (head/) and ddefb51 (base/), with GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES and TMPDIR set to the sandbox. The real repo and worktree were only read, with git log, show, diff and archive.

## What was run
- `go test ./internal/... ./cmd/...` on HEAD: all pass.
- **Real-data loop** (scripts copied from sfh35, at sfh36-redact/scripts/run.sh, migrate.sh, records.sh), on a copy of the data, head and base, with both the `hr` and `hu` HOMEs:
  - Seal loop: 24 iterations, then 1 iteration, then 0 files changed, for all four combinations.
  - `mission scrub`: identical output on head and base (57 files to rewrite; the same 2 failures, `m-2026-08-22-011` `success_criteria[1]`).
  - `mission migrate --dry-run` and per-id migrate: identical (32 ids, all "no repo session").
- **Records probe**: head and base binaries, each run against both data copies. All 8 runs give identical output: missions=232, events=656, warnings=0, and the one refusal is `m-2026-08-22-011 SuccessCriteria[1]`.
- **Data differences, head vs base**: 3 audit `tool_input_preview` values that base replaces with `[redacted-path]` and head keeps. Each holds only a bare `"/home/"` string with no username, and the same text already sits unredacted in `tool_input.command` on both sides. The 4th difference is the key order of one mission log line. These come from ddefb51..90b3548, and none is a leak.
- **Other writers** (probe sfh36_writers_test.go, HOME=~[redacted-user] Migrate of a legacy contract, scrub of a planted contract, and a delegation skeleton's `spawn_pattern` all store `.claude/projects/-~-proj/...` with an announcement, and do so identically on base and head. Pipeline instantiate (cmd/ethos/pipeline.go:285), the MCP create tool (internal/mcp/mission_tools.go:165) and the CLI create paths (cmd/ethos/mission.go:1211, 2180) all go through `Store.Create`, so they are refused. `Correct` writes only an event. `import` is identity-only.
- **Mutants of HEAD**:
  - Remove the refusal from Update: `TestPathField_InFlightMissionWithTheOwnSlugCanFinish` fails.
  - Remove the refusal from Create: `TestPathField_RefusesTheOwnDashHome` and `TestPathField_OrdinaryFileNamesAreStoredAsWritten` fail.
  - Put the refusal back in `RedactRecordNotify`: the in-flight test fails.
  - Pass a nil prior in Update: **every test still passes** (see Not blocking).

## Findings

**(c)-1 — internal/redact/redact.go:961-963**
- The comment says: "A path-tagged field is refused when it does: the writer would rewrite the slug to -~". This was true at 90b3548 and false since c054144.
- Input (HOME=~[redacted-user] `WriteDelegationSkeleton` with `SpawnPattern: ".claude/projects/-~-[redacted-slug]/x"`.
  - HEAD: err=nil, stored `spawn_pattern: .claude/projects/-~-proj/x`.
  - Base: the same.
- `AppendResult` `files_changed` behaves the same way (`TestPathField_InFlightMissionWithTheOwnSlugCanFinish` passes on HEAD).
- Fix: "Store.Create and Store.Update refuse a new or changed repo-relative contract path entry that holds it (refuseOwnDashHome); every other writer rewrites the slug to -~."

**(c)-2 — internal/mission/slug_repo_relative_test.go:12-15 and :82-84**
- Two comments state a general refusal that no longer holds:
  - Lines 12-15: "a path-tagged field that holds this machine's dash-encoded home anywhere is refused".
  - Lines 82-84: "its home and its dash-encoded slug anywhere are refused".
- Same inputs and output as (c)-1: a result's `files_changed` and a delegation's `spawn_pattern` are rewritten to `-~`, not refused. The tests themselves only exercise Create.
- Fix: limit both comments to "when a contract is created or its path entries change".

**(c)-3, with the (b) prior-comparison check — internal/mission/redact.go:588-589 (comment) and :600-610 (code)**
- The comment says "path entries, new or changed from prior". The code instead checks whether the value appears anywhere in the prior contract's path fields (`slices.Contains(had, fs.Value)`), not per field. An entry that is new to one field passes if its value sits in any other prior field.
- Input (sfh36_prior_test.go P1, HOME=~[redacted-user] the on-disk contract has `write_set: [.claude/projects/-~-[redacted-slug]/x.md]`, as written by an older ethos or by hand. `Update` then sets `inputs.files` to the same value.
  - HEAD: err=nil; disk holds `- .claude/projects/-~-proj/x.md` twice (write_set and inputs.files).
  - Base: identical.
- So there is no leak or data loss compared with base, but this is a changed entry that gets past the comparison.
- The other probe cases behave as intended: new entries in any path field (write_set, inputs.files, extract_into, require_read, tools, ticket, references, uppercase spellings) are refused on both Create and Update. Unchanged planted entries and duplicates pass and are rewritten to `-~`, as at base.
- Fix: key `had` by field path with indexes stripped (e.g. `map[string]map[string]bool`, keyed `"WriteSet"`, `"Inputs.Files"`, …), and check `had[stripIndex(fs.Name)][fs.Value]`. Alternatively, reword the comment to "whose value is not already a path entry of prior".

## Not blocking
- The Update prior-comparison has no test. A mutant that passes `nil` as prior (store.go:928) leaves internal/mission, internal/hook and cmd/ethos green, yet it refuses an unrelated Update on an in-flight own-slug mission (probe P4: "field WriteSet[0] holds this machine's dash-encoded home"). The ddefb51 behaviour that c054144 restores is therefore unguarded; add a test for P4.
- Migrate (migrate.go copyIfExists), scrub, and delegation and result writers store a newly added own-slug repo-relative entry as `-~`, with an announcement and no refusal, the same as ddefb51.
- `refuseOwnDashHome` returns nil when the redactor fails (redact.go:598). The following `writeContractNote` → `RedactRecordNotify` → `NewPathRedactor` fails the same way, so the error is not hidden.
- A bare foreign slug in free text (`grep -e -~-[redacted-slug] x`) passes `LeakRule` on both base and head. On the copied real data this keeps `-~` in `tool_input.command` at line 13041 of the 837b52b4 session audit, identically on both.
- With HOME=/root, `ci/build-root/x` is refused on both base and head. HEAD's Create message now says "must name the file without the home slug", which is misleading for that name.
- The Update assertion at slug_repo_relative_test.go:156 does not check the error text. The Update mutant shows it does fail without the refusal.

Reproduced and fixed in fd13d00. Before the fix, both seal and quarantine recovery failed in LoadEvents with `json: unknown field "redacted"`.

`missionLineGuard` (internal/hook/audit_mission_guard.go) now runs for the mission namespace in `sealDirLocked` and in `QuarantineChunk`. A line that decodes strictly as a `mission.Event` goes through the mission writer's own passes, `RedactRecord` and then `CheckBytes("log.jsonl")`. Its fields are handled as follows:
- No field is added at the top level of the line.
- A leaking detail is scrubbed leaf by leaf, and `details.redacted` is set. If the caller already uses that key, the marker goes under `redacted#N`.
- Numbers are kept exactly (UseNumber).
- A duplicate key, or keys that differ only in case, send the line to the audit guard's marker and print a notice, as before.

Tests: `TestSealMission_SealedEventLoads` and `TestQuarantineChunk_RecoveredMissionEventLoads` load the result with zero warnings. On the real data, 656 events load with no warnings.

package hook

// TestAudit_CredentialAsAKeyIsRedacted: the credential pass runs on map keys as
// well as values, so a token used as a nested tool_input key does not reach the
// audit log or the chunks sealed from it. Two keys that redact to the same name
// do not merge.
func TestAudit_CredentialAsAKeyIsRedacted(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())
	tok1 := "ghp_" + strings.Repeat("a1B2", 9)
	tok2 := "ghp_" + strings.Repeat("c3D4", 9)
	in := map[string]any{"x": map[string]any{tok1: 1, tok2: 2, "ok": 3}}
	out, _ := redactToolInput(map[string]any{"tool_input": in}, "Bash", t.TempDir())
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.NotContains(t, string(b), "ghp_")
	x := out["x"].(map[string]any)
	assert.Len(t, x, 3, "no two keys merge")
	assert.Equal(t, 3, x["ok"])

	// Through the writer and a seal of the file it wrote.
	repo := t.TempDir()
	payload, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"session_id": "s1", "tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": in})
	require.NoError(t, HandleAuditLog(bytes.NewReader(payload), repo, ""))
	live := liveAuditPath(repo, "s1")
	data, err := os.ReadFile(live)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.NotContains(t, string(data), "ghp_")
	sealedLines, _ := guardTail([][]byte{bytes.TrimSpace(data)}, "label")
	assert.NotContains(t, string(sealedLines[0]), "ghp_")
	_ = filepath.Join
}
EOF

## Review of e5a7e42..9ea93c6 (fix/redact-tracked-writers)

I reviewed four commits: 62a6fad (credential keys), cf279b7 (quarantine reason), 74fcaf0 (scrub lock order) and 9ea93c6 (StoreRootOf / preconditionTargets). I found **2 blocking findings**, both in 9ea93c6. The other three commits are clean against the bar.

Everything ran in the sandbox `~/Coding/punt-labs/.tmp/cr37-redact/{new,old}`: `git archive` copies of 9ea93c6 and e5a7e42, each `git init`ed. The environment was GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>, TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp and HOME=<sandbox>/home. I wrote nothing into the worktree. My probe tests are kept in `.tmp/cr37-redact/probes/`.

### Finding 1 — (a) regression against e5a7e42: `require_read` is wrongly denied when ETHOS_REPO_ROOT points at a linked worktree
**Where:** `internal/hook/preconditions.go:153` (`mission.ExpandPath(resolved, resolve.StoreRootOf(repoRoot))`), together with `internal/resolve/resolve.go:768`.

**Cause:**
- The contract is written by a Store rooted at `resolve.StoreRepoRoot()`. That function honors ETHOS_REPO_ROOT as-is (`repoRootOverride(true)`), so with the override set to a linked worktree that has a `.punt-labs/ethos` store, `<repo>` in the contract means the worktree.
- `StoreRootOf` ignores the override. It stats `<wt>/.git`, finds a file, and returns the main work tree.
- So the stored entry expands to `<main>/cfg/config.yaml`, while the recorded Read is `<wt>/cfg/config.yaml`.
- The new comment on `StoreRootOf` ("A contract is serialized against this root") is false in this case.

**Input:** probe `TestProbe_OverrideLinkedWorktree` (`probes/probe_override_test.go`):
1. A main repo with a linked worktree `w` at `.claude/worktrees/w`, plus `mkdir w/.punt-labs/ethos`.
2. `ETHOS_REPO_ROOT=<wt>`, so `StoreRepoRoot()` and `envRepoRoot()` both return `<wt>`.
3. Contract = `RedactRecord(StoreRepoRoot(), require_read <wt>/cfg/config.yaml)`, which stores `<repo>/cfg/config.yaml`.
4. `auditRead(envRepoRoot(), …)`, then `EvaluatePreconditions(..., envRepoRoot())`.

**Observed:**
- e5a7e42: PASS (allowed).
- 9ea93c6: FAIL, `deny: read it first (…)`. The Read that was recorded is refused.

**Fix:** expand against the root the contract was actually loaded from. Either:
- pass `tierBStoreRoot()` (`resolve.StoreRepoRoot()`) from `evalContractPreconditions` into `EvaluatePreconditions` as a separate store-root argument, or
- make `StoreRootOf` return the validated ETHOS_REPO_ROOT override first, exactly as `StoreRepoRoot` does.

Add the override case as a test. Also compute the root once, outside the `for _, entry := range p.RequireRead` loop (line 144). It currently runs 2 `git rev-parse` subprocesses per entry per tool call.

### Finding 2 — (c) false comment: `StoreRootOf` was inserted inside `worktreeStoreRoot`'s doc comment
**Where:** `internal/resolve/resolve.go:757-779`. The `worktreeStoreRoot` doc block (757-764) now sits directly above the `StoreRootOf` comment (765-767) and func (768). `func worktreeStoreRoot` (779) is left with no doc.

**Observed:** `go doc -u ./internal/resolve StoreRootOf` prints "worktreeStoreRoot resolves the repository root that owns the store for a directory whose .git is a file … StoreRootOf returns …". `worktreeStoreRoot` prints no doc.

**Fix:** move `StoreRootOf` and its comment above line 757, so the `worktreeStoreRoot` comment again sits directly on `func worktreeStoreRoot`.

### Checked and clean against the bar

**Lock order (74fcaf0).** The locks are: per-mission store lock (`s.withLock`), then repo mission lock (`AcquireMissionLock`/`AcquireMissionLockExclusive`), then delegation lock. Every caller that takes more than one takes them in that order:
- Close: store lock released before the exclusive mission lock; the sweep takes no delegation lock.
- `dispatchTierB`: shared mission lock, then delegation lock (`pretooluse_dispatch.go:791,803`).
- Disclaim/Abandon: store lock, then exclusive mission lock, then delegation lock (`store.go:1578,1232,1616`).
- Scrub: shared mission lock, then delegation lock. It holds no store lock around it, and files are processed one at a time.
- `closeSkeletonOnHashRefusal` (`subagent_start.go:978`): delegation lock only.

No path takes the delegation lock and then the mission lock, so there is no inversion and no deadlock.

**Scrub test and the 300 ms wait.** With the lock in place the outcome is deterministic: the closer blocks until scrub releases. The 300 ms only bounds how long the mutation has to show up.
- `go test -race -count=20 -run TestScrub_DelegationRecordSerializesWithTheCloseSweep`: ok, 20/20 pass.
- Mutation (the `AcquireMissionLock` call replaced by a no-op), same command: 20/20 FAIL.

The test is not flaky and can detect the defect it names.

**StoreRootOf on error and edge cases.**
- Stat error: returns dir silently. This matches e5a7e42, which used the checkout root.
- Submodule: `gitStoreRoot` returns the worktree, so dir.
- Bare repo or no `.git`: dir.
- Outside a repo: dir.
- `.git` file that git cannot resolve: `manualStoreRoot` warns to stderr.

The only silent wrong answer is the override case in Finding 1.

**RenameKeys (62a6fad).** `planKeys` places unchanged keys first and reserves their names, so a key that is not a credential is never renamed or overwritten. Colliding credential keys get `#N` suffixes, skipping names already taken.
- Probe `TestProbe_KeyIdempotent`, input `{tok1:1, tok2:2, "[redacted-secret]":9, "[redacted-secret]#2":8, "token":"[redacted-secret]", "ok":3}`, output `"[redacted-secret]":9, "#2":8, "#3":1, "#4":2, "ok":3, "token":"[redacted-secret]"`. Nothing merged.
- A second pass changes nothing.
- `guardTail` on the live line gives no notes and identical bytes.
- `file_path`, which `sweepSecrets` holds out, is restored unchanged.

**New tests fail on old code.** All four fail when copied onto e5a7e42 and pass on 9ea93c6:
- `TestAudit_CredentialAsAKeyIsRedacted`: ghp_ in the output, the live file and the sealed line.
- `TestQuarantineChunk_ReasonThatStillLeaksIsReplaced`: alice in both branches.
- `TestScrub_…CloseSweep`: verdict is open, expected aborted.
- `TestEvaluatePreconditions_LinkedWorktree…`: deny.

**Gates.** `go vet` and `staticcheck` are clean on redact, resolve, mission and hook. Package tests pass, except `TestPostToolUseHook_WorktreeResolution`, which fails identically on e5a7e42 in this sandbox (environmental, not a regression).

### Not blocking
- `internal/mission/scrub.go:179`: `AcquireMissionLock` runs `MkdirAll`. A dry-run scrub of a tracked delegation record whose mission dir was deleted now creates `<repo>/.punt-labs/ethos/missions/<mid>/.lock`. Probe `TestProbe_SkipFootprint`: `res.Skipped=[…]`, and the `.lock` file exists afterwards. The `ScrubFiles` doc says "With dryRun it writes nothing." Close deliberately avoids creating this directory (`missingRepoTreeDir`); scrub could stat the mission dir first in the same way.
- `internal/redact/redact.go:575-577`: the `SecretsValue` doc has a stray line break ("and\n// replaces the").
- `internal/hook/audit_quarantine.go:78`: the fixed text "it named a home directory" is also used when `LeakRule` matched the `..`-climb or unknown-home absolute-path rule. Those rules are not literally about a home.
- `resolve.StoreRootOf` and the body of `StoreRepoRoot`'s walk duplicate the same `.git` file/dir branching.

The store root is computed once per call. It handles all three ways of running correctly:
- a plain checkout;
- a linked worktree without an override, where the store is the main checkout;
- `ETHOS_REPO_ROOT` set to a linked worktree that holds its own store.

Tests:
- `TestEvaluatePreconditions_LinkedWorktreeEntryExpandsAgainstTheStoreRoot`.
- `TestEvalContractPreconditions_LinkedWorktreeWithoutOverride`.
- `TestEvalContractPreconditions_OverrideToALinkedWorktree`.

Both of the evalContractPreconditions tests fail if the store root is replaced with the checkout root.
